That little 'recommended' button comes with some rather large [IF] brackets.
First and foremost, the game is -incredibly- grindy.  You spend countless hours doing the same things over and over for very little gain.  Quite honestly, in my (now) 16 hours of playtime, I've had so very few mods that I have many, many open slots on my gear that I just can't fill without buying mod packs (real world cash here).
That being said, its a ridiculously fun grind.  Each time I do a mission, I can (kinda) choose a different approach.
"Okay, so -this- time, I'm going to treat the game like Dishonored and assassinate every one of my 106 required kills without getting detected."
"Okay, so -this- time, I'm going to use nothing but my Kunai and run and slide at every foe in my path."
So yes, I recommend playing this game, because its fun.  However, if you're absolutely the type of person that can't have fun without some immediate gratification of achievement, you'll probably get frustrated unless you're very, very, very patient.

If you have functioning eyes and are a living being with a brain, you will witness:
- A truly awfully optimised game. No hardware will make this hit native 1080p60 with anything above PS2 era graphics.
- Alternatively, an awful looking game, littered with fuzzy jaggies from upscales and no shadows, a tragic draw distance and low quality textures and meshes. Not that this runs much better.
- A despicable DLC scheme; as in, there is paid DLC. Costing £15.
- CRASHES HITCHES AND GLITCHES WHOOP
- An ongoing legal battle?!
- Frequent updates of massive file sizes that do... what? Dinosaur cosmetics? I don't even know anymore.
- (Debatably) passable gameplay, riding dinosaurs is cool, insta-kill bees from hell if you spawn on the wrong side of the island is not cool. Beginners are screwed tbh.
- A modding system that requires you to have an editor the size of the game installed to use it.
Please don't buy this game. And if you got it from that one Humble Monthly a while back, don't bother installing it. Waste of storage space.

First things first; anyone under at least 700 hours, does not have an extensive amount of experience for a game this in-depth and therefore should stray away from giving a review and possibly flagging this game with a negative review. *I know there a people with 5,000+ hours with negative reviews, advising individuals not to purchase this game. * in my opinion, if a game looks fun, I'm going to play it to form my own opinion. Also, keep in my mind, I bought this game on June 2, in 2015. So, I have been around since the beginning, before Argentavis' could even land and walk.
Pros are as followed,
-Visually stunning
-Any mechanic within the game is very in-depth, (easy to get side tracked.)
-A lot of different maps, that showcase some reoccurring and some brand-new eco-systems, (some deadlier than others.)
-140+? (Give or take) creatures in ark roaming around, 85% are tamable, and each animal and dinosaurs alike serves a purpose. (i.e. beaver is the best wood collector, as the moose is the best thatch collected.)
-This game supports and feeds your creative needs, build on anything you could imagine, (of course, if there are proper foundations supporting it, structural integrity matters.)
-Wildcard is actively listening, and implanting responses, and concerns from the community.
-and many more, I would be here all day typing out positive thing.
Cons are as followed,
-This game is demanding; so, therefore, an individual with a lower end pc on the power spectrum sometimes tends to be on the lower side of advantage.
-Laggy, and bandwidth problems. (Not so much Ark itself, be cautious when choosing your mainland server.)
-The in-game community seems to be almost immature 75% of the time, people letting their anger speak for them.
-Similar to the games demand on your hardware, it is also very demanding and dependent on an individual’s time. (This is a legitimate concern, I could see being breeding grounds for negative reviews.)
-Official servers seem to be the center of negativity within this game. (Highly recommend playing unofficial.)
-Just like the Pros of this game, there are a lot of Con's that would require me to sit here all day.
Ark is a great game, with volumes of activities to partake in, also it is very time consuming and tends at some-points of playthrough feel like a full-time job. I would recommend this game to a stable, young individual who has no history of anger and a lot of free time. Neglecting careers and studies is not a very smart move, but Ark makes that decision seem a lot easier to make. This game is dangerous to a lot of people, because in reality a lot of you guys/girls reading my review have longed been in search for a game exactly like this. Plus it has dinosaurs.
To sum things up, Ark has a bad reputation. However, it does have its own fair share of bugs, that everyone deserves to know prior to purchase. Even though, that doesn’t stop individuals from publishing a negative review relevant to performance issues because they failed to consult the System Requirements tab on the store page prior to purchase. Another quick note about a trend I noticed. It seems a lot of people have experienced being wiped out by another tribe and then instantly came to the forums to post a negative review. Although, there are legitimate negative reviews, just filter out the stupid ones.

Ok so here goes...
Ark is the most irritating, frustrating, fun game that there is.
If there was a "I might recommend this game" option, that is what I would pick. Let me start from the beginning...
I bought Ark shortly after it came out, the game was almost unplayable... besides all the glitches, crashes, bugs... there were only official servers and unofficial servers in europe (I am from South Africa, so constant 200-300ping).
During this time, I played on the official servers... do not, I repeat, do not ever try do this alone... it took me about 10 hours to make a mini thatch base with nothing else to show for it... I then deleted the game and didn't touch ark for another 6 months or more.
6 months later, I re-installed the game... the game literally doubled in size (I think it was around a 15gb download, or more)...
Great times were had with mates on unofficial servers, where the rates vary from 10x - 60x, making the game much faster and enjoyable (in my eyes), with these rates you can literally put up a very decent stone base along with grinding machines within 2 hours, solo, much quicker with some mates...
Here is where this game really frustrates the living crap out of me (soz for swearing)
- you spend hours taming, building, grinding... just to find that the server shuts down and disappears (unofficial servers)
- you go offline for 1 day and some little 10 year old kid that looks like the hunchback of Notre Dame has completely wiped out your base
- sometimes Ark relseases an update twice a week... sometimes more... and we are talking about a minimum of 600mb-1.5gb update
- along with the ark updates, all the mods then need to be updated, so depending on the server... another 10 updates on stack mods, level mods, advanced buildings, etc... each mod is at least 25mb+
- when joining an unoffical server you are literally going to join and time out and download for 30mins (sometimes less if you are lucky) so the game can download and install and update all the mods
So here are all my points. This game is really fun, the graphics are out of this world... but make sure you are jamming with a friend, official servers are not worthwhile IMO, goodluck trying to join an unoffical server and actually playing on it for more than a week.

Liked: Has (or maybe had by the time you read this), a mix of game play: guns, melee, mobility, nukes and other large radius powerful abilities.  The Art Department is great.
Disliked:  The development over the past 2+ years where my fun was repeatedly nerfed and the game cannibalized to expand the Pay or Grind Wall.  The lack of freedom to play the game because every peice of loot or reward is compartmentalized into a specific  mission, faction, mode, and tileset.  Anything popular is nerfed "because everyone is doing it" and "because balance" (yet "balance" never happens), then whatever made it popular is reintroduced behind a new Pay or Grind Wall.  Anybody who exposes this is drummed out of the forums.  Digital Extreme's excuses, twistedly regurgitating what players say to cover what it does.
On 02/08/2013 DE stated that Warframe is about 4 Tenno Devastate Massive Armies (skip to 2:54)

In 2015, after months of wrecking the spawn code, DE decided that a reduction to 30 enemy on the field at once is more than enough enemy on the field at once.  In other words, DE was sooo over that Massive Army stuff.
DE's not too crazy about the 4 Tenno Devastate part either, but, it knows that "OP" sells.  So DE nerfs, releases "OP", nerfs, releases "OP", nerfs ........ never stops jerking the player base around.  There's a history of power creep too, all the while "balance blah blah blah...", nerf, power creep, nerf, power creep, nerf ....
The Warframe Meta:
It's possible to have every piece of player content in this game without spending money thanks to trade, by following this simple Meta:
1)  Join a good clan that will carry you around.
2)  Camp camp camp.
3)  Grind grind grind.
4)  Trade trade trade.  Trade your syndicate mods and weapons, trade Void Trader exclusives. trade rewards and loot.  Trade it all to new players who don't know better, or completionists.  Do it before it gets nerfed, or wait until it's taken out of the loot/reward tables then sell it to completionists for a lot more.
Recommendation:  I do not recommend this game to people who like to own something when they spend money for something.  There is too much turmoil in it's development for that.  However, if you don't mind the flux and find the camp, grind, trade "free to play"(or not) meta appealing, then you might be happy with Warframe.  It's your choice.  Have fun, if you will, or can.
My experience has been fraught with opposition and disappointment, even though I spent ~$185 on Warframe, so I'll have to avoid such games in the future.

+ Wide range of gears available
+ Mod customization has really cool concept
+ Fluid Movement
+ Good graphic
+ Good community
+ GRINDFEST!!!!
Cons:

- RNG can be very.... stingy

I have put in about a doller per every hour I've played in this game, according to the ingame time counter, and steam's own money spent counter.
My love of this game will never go away, but my tolerance of the actions of Digital Extremes (the developers of Warframe) has slowly been declining over the last 2-3 years. Compared to the developers of most other F2P games, they're still pretty good. However, they used to be entirely honest, community oriented, and in-touch with their game. Over the past year and a half, they've delayed a major update by half a year and allowed other content to be held back as a result, they've conducted a major nerf wave on several of the classes in the game (the warframes) with the promise of rebalancing later (hasn't happened), they've taken legal action against a player of the game after sensitive information was leaked and content was manipulated by another party entirely, they've broken drop tables and allowed subpar rewards to be available in high tier missions where they don't belong, and a handful of other things.
I'm leaving a negative review at the moment because of the legal action they took against the community member here in the last week. In addition, they've been very stubborn and defensive. Unless this is resolved in such a way that it makes up for the damage done, my review is remaining negative.

pretty neat guyver-esque art style, cool canadian devs for the most part, really dedicated team that cares deeply about constantly iterating on the game's design
new to update 17 is a complete rework of the movement/parkour system ingame, and while some old things were lost, by and large it is a huge improvement and big step in the right direction IMHO
fun 3rd person guns and melee with lots of options for different primary/sidearm loadouts as well as unique melee animations and 'combo's for each different melee weapon type
all in all over the last 2+ yrs i have had a lot of fun playing each different frame and all the different weapons over all the different ingame tilesets (the level design team are srsly awesome) and killing all the different various enemies/factions along the way
the game is CONSTANTLY getting nonstop updates/patches/luv/etv
its been rough sometimes, and of course for a veteran, there are plenty of nitpicks and critiques, but i would recommend the game at this point [there were times b4 that i did not feel as rosy]
still in an 'open-beta / soft-release' as they've been taking $$$ since CB, but there are still at least a half dozen to a dozen enemies/bosses that are currently 'placeholders' until a unique rework is done, but i would guess at the current rate the game should officially no longer be in any kind of beta either sometime later in 2016 or early 2017
check out the warframe wiki and/or the /r warframe sub-reddit for more info

This game is fantastic, you get all the updates for free, two DLCs for free, and one for a decent price (they've been working on this long enough that they're probably not getting many money gifts or anything like that - if they ever were - so it makes sense). I, personally, have to wait until I have a little more money, I don't even have $10 to spend, but what's $20 to most people now-a-days? Sorry to be rude (kinda), but I think half the people ♥♥♥♥♥ing about paying for Scorched Earth have mommy and daddy pay for everything and mommy and daddy don't feel like it right now. When they start charging more than a measly $20, say, maybe more like $60 for a DLC, then I might worry about them becoming "money hungry."
Anyway, it's a fantastic game, there are bugs and glitches, but I personally don't run into many of them. I'm on an HP laptop running 4gb of ram, too, with a puny graphic's card, okay. I don't have a top of the line computer (I would love to though, omg, High and Epic level graphics are mind blowing.) I have to run my graphics in Low or Medium, which is expected with my computer. I do think they should adjust the minimum requirements to what it currently needs to run, not wait they're aiming for (which is what I think it currently reflects) because that is certainly misleading (likely unintentionally so). I honestly kind of laugh at the idea of a dual-core running the game, since my quad has a hard time when things get intense.
I also would like it if they would fix the issue where you lag in caves. Caves are completely unplayable for me, and that's where some of the best loot is. I thought it was just my computer for a while, but evidently a lot of people have that issue. So please do put that on the list, devs, if you see this post and if it isn't already. Also, always optimizations, I think they're wittling away at it, so I look forward to future improvments there.
And to those fussing about it still being an early access game... could you not? It is a MASSIVE game, and a huge project, and these guys are not Nintendo or Microsoft, okay? They over-estimated when the game would be finished. They ran into roadblocks, things came up that needed fixed, ect. The ammount of work that goes into creating something like this is monumental. Early access also means we're going to keep getting patches and fixes for the glitches. It's not ready to be a full release game - and that's okay. It's still available to be played, so you can enjoy it anyway. It's not as if you can't play it at all until it's full release.

Seen alot of negative reviews complaining about a a buggy and unfinished game. Personally I have not found the game to be overly buggy (I only play on singleplayer) aside from the rather anoying tendency for your dinos to get stuck in rocks or trees if your not carefull. Definetely not game breaking though. As for the game being unfinished, the early access part kind of gives that away. It may not be finished but it certainly does not lack for content. Two fully finished maps for free filled with all types of dinos and more still coming. Tons to build, tame, create and explore. If this what the game is like now, can't wait to see the finished product. The only downside i've come across is performance. I have a GTX 970, 3 gigs of VRAM, 24 gigs of regular RAM, and a intel I7 2.5 ghz proccesser. This game eats about anywhere from 5-8 gigs of RAM on high settings. However the graphics don't effect the fps much, it's the dinos. On the main map there are about 40,000 on the map at any given time. I changed the .ini to set the dino spawn to 50%(look it up on google, I don't remember the exact steps.) That fixed my fps probems and now run smoothly. Also might have a memory leak in the game. If playing all day RAM usage goes from around 5 gigs to 8 and game starts to chug. A simple restart of my computer fixed this. All in all a very fun game even in single player and probably even more fun to play online with friends.

Warframe.
In this game, you play as a space ninja known as a Warframe, which contain special powers and differ from one another, yet united for a cause.
Anyways, let's get on to what you want to know.
Type of game:
Warframe is a third-person shooter that takes place in the future. It is free-to-play. It includes Gun battles, melee fights, parkour, and special abilities. Most items in this game have two options on how to get them.
Option one: Spend real-life money and buy the selected item.
Option two: Buy a blue-print (through in game "credits"), then find the parts to build it.
This game can be entirely free-to-play, but money is optional for stuff like cosmetic items.
Universe:
In this game, you are the Tenno, masters of the Warframes, suits with power of the Orokin, an old race who have gone extinct. Each Warframe is different, yet they all fight for the same cause. You have been awoken from your cryopod by the Lotus, your friend and guide. As you fight against enemies, you learn more of the old ways of the Tenno, and more to the cause of them.
Warframes:
These are the "characters" you play as. Each carry their own abilities, but are balanced compared to one another. Their are many Warframes, each suited for different play styles and purposes.
(Examples of some Warframes, not all)
Excalibur: The first Tenno, Excalibur is a combination of both mobility and offense, making him a good choice for any playstyle.
Loki: Using the power of manipulation and stealth, he is a reasonable choice for advanced players.
Rhino: With strength and durability, Rhino is the tank of the bunch.
Volt: Harnessing the power of electricity, Volt is a shocking agent of death.
There are some Warframes, but there are many more to be discovered.
Weapons:
This game has varities of weapons, suiting many purposes and uses. There are three main categories for weapons:
Primary: The Big Guns. Assualt Rifles, Sub Machine Guns, Light Machine Guns, Bows, Snipers, Laser weapons, and more.
Secondary: Your personal side arm. pistols, mini-crossbows, small shotguns, and such.
Melee: The Up close and personal. Swords, Bow Staffs, Knives, Axes, Machetes, Katanas, Brass-knuckles, and much more.
This game is worth the time that in it (And how big this review is). I highly reccomend you play it if you enjoy all of the above. It's beautiful, it's fun, it's co-op, it's interesting, it's fill with stuff to do, it's worth it.
And Remember, Ninjas Play Free.

As you see, I have put about 3,000 hours into the game and have been playing for almost 2 years. I am a hunter level founder and have spent almost as much money as I have time into the game (more than I care to admit to). It really hurts that I have to re post my review and change it to negative, but I am honest and not a fanboy. I will try to be a short as possible and just list my various problems with this game.
- RNG. Enough said about that
- Weapons have no impact. One of the fun aspects of any shooter is feeling the pain you're dishing out to your enemies. This game does not do that.
- Lackluster quests and lore. I have never been more bored in my life with lore than I have been with this game. It's vague and uninteresting.
- The cesspool that is the community. Seriously, just avoid the forums and region chat. It'll give you cancer.
- DE. While I do not hate the game, I do dislike the developers. There's a reason why they stay up past midnight working on every major update while no other companies do that. They have no structure and that's not a good thing. As big as they are, there's no excuse for the lies, stealth nerfs, and procrastination.
- Painfully slow movement. With "Parkour 2.0" they removed coptering. I am fine with that as long as you can add in something replace it to keep the fast pace. DE did no such thing and instead made us slower, probably to make the grind more tedious and try to force us to buy their stupid prime access and new weapons of the moment that they're pedalling.
- No character at all and/or cringeworthy jokes. Seriously, Ordis needs to go die in a hole. He is NOT funny and is very annoying. The only character that was funny, became unfunny because of DE's lack of sense of fun. I refer to Darvo of course, DE ruined their only good character. Also, the newest quest was just terrible and made me realize even more how unoriginal anything in this game is. Sentients is a stupid♥♥♥♥♥name for a race and are obvious cheap knockoffs of the reapers from Mass Effect. There was a point where scorpions (another unoriginal rip off from MK) had the description "make the pain feel good." Instead of adding nice descriptions like that to add character, DE opts in instead to remove that and not add anymore like that.
Overall, just play something else. I am not even getting into how much of a rip off the plat prices and market prices for all the garbage that's being pedalled is. This game has no fun factor at all. It has nothing.
Just came back after a year of not playing. Can confirm it is not burn out, the game is just gradually getting worse.
-Nitain Extracts are hands down the worst resource ever implemented into this game. These just need to go. There is no saving them, ♥♥♥♥ whoever thought these were a good idea.
-Defection and Infested Salvage mission types are cancer. I don't know who at DE thought escort missions were fun, but you're wrong. Also, why are SO MANY mission types in warframe a defend the objective type mission? Just please stop.
-Riven mods are fine, but why are weapons like Soma and Dread able to get them too? This was an easy way to fix some of the power creep and yet DE somehow screwed it up by allowing Soma and Dread and Boltor Prime to get these mods.
-The Sands of Inaros, Glast Gambit, and Chains of Harrow quests are bad. They are extremely repetitive and uninteresting. Octavia's Anthem and the War Within are good though.
-So many of the new weapons that came out in the last year are just garbage. I holster leveled so many new weapons and many of them were really resource intensive and expensive. Of the 2 that I enjoyed, one of them was not worth keeping (Stradavar) and the other (Tenora) I kept, but why is there such a shortage of good secondary weapons?

Like many others I have enjoyed playing this over the past year or so. 235 hours of play time as I write this. Dropped out for around six months playing other games, etc, but decided to pick it back up again the other day. I was underwhelmed.
I'd have expected over the past six months (well, year, really) for progress to have been made on at least some serious bug fixing, AI improvements (the pathfinding is just terrible) and perhaps making structures a little easier to work with terrain. Unfortunately this was not the case. Instead I find that the developers have released a standalone game of the Survival Of The Fittest mod and added two new maps to play on.
Firstly: in an Early Access game it woulds seem that bug fixing and improving the core gaming experience should be priority number one. The dinos are great and all but after a year of seeing them walk straight into cliffs or trees and getting stuck it begins to get old. The new maps are always good, but again, get the core game working properly first before bringing out major content. If you need to get your car fixed you'd start with the engine before you bother to install a fully sick dual-subwoofer surround system and neon lights, amiright?
Secondly: Survival Of The Fittest did not need to be its own standalone game, plain and simple. It just needed to be a mode of the game, which it already was.
Thirdly: the Scorched Earth expansion pack. DLC while the game is still in Early Access? Are you serious? I understand that the studio may need some cashflow (if that's the purpose of the DLC) but perhaps - just perhaps - if they fixed up the overdue issues in the core game players wouldn't get frustrated and write "Not Recommended" reviews, hmmm?
Overall it's still a fun game to play, but I would not recommend buying it until further improvement has been made - at the least on the most glaring of the bugs and issues.

This game has undergone many and varied changes over the years it has been available for public play, and the latest one, Update 17 is one of the best ever. It marks a turnign point in Warframe and the way it is played, and perhaps more importantly, the way it is developed. Basic changes include: Complete overhaul of movement mechanics. The slogan of the game has long been about being a 'space ninja', and now with this movement scheme, you really feel like a badass space ninja. ALL surfaces of the game environment are playable, and you can reach anywhere with only a little effort, and perhaps a good deal od ingenuity and creativity. Many new weapons as well, and a new frame with the characteristics of Day and Night, Yin and Yang, Male and Female; well you get the picture. Also included is a new quest concernign the Sentients. Without including too much top spoil it, this quest explored the origins of the Tenno, the Lotus, and why the universe is the way it is now (in the game at least)
All of that is but a part of the last update, there is more to be had including a new tileset on Uranus, which uses the Archwing as an underwater machine as well, opening up new and cool ways to play.
At the core however, Warframe is still a 4 player (sometimes 8, in the trial missions) cooperative shooter game with a myriad of badass little perks to it that set it head and shoulders above the crowd in this genre. It isn't a perfect game by any means, but the positive aspects of it far outweigh any negatives.
What are the negatives? Here's a few:
1: The game is still fairly repetitive, even with the addition of quite a few new mission types and environments. This repetitive nature of the game is further emphasized by the grind of getting items and resources for crafting, if the player wants to play for "free".
2:  The game is a beta. While the game is quite polished and so forth, the PC version f the game is basically a stress test for builds that will later on become the builds used for the PS4 and XB1 versions of the game. This means that each time significant changes to the game are made, there are always quite a number of bugs that must be dealt with that can have a negative impact on the  player's experience.
In my opinion, those are the major negative aspects of the game. There are more I am sure, and varied as well, each player probably has their own list of pet peeves, but these 2 seem to cover the majority of them. But, the game offers the player the chance to have a massive amount of fun with their friends, in a fully realized world (the lore and story are coming along) where one can be as badass as they want to be.
I highly recommend this game for anyone wanting an inexpensive way to have a blast with their buddies, or maybe a few more people in a clan. There are so many ways to have fun there isn't much point trying to list them, my advice is to play the game and see for yourself. I'd firther say that if your buddy can come along and the both of you explore the game together, you'll more than double your fun.

Like many others I have enjoyed playing this over the past year or so. 235 hours of play time as I write this. Dropped out for around six months playing other games, etc, but decided to pick it back up again the other day. I was underwhelmed.
I'd have expected over the past six months (well, year, really) for progress to have been made on at least some serious bug fixing, AI improvements (the pathfinding is just terrible) and perhaps making structures a little easier to work with terrain. Unfortunately this was not the case. Instead I find that the developers have released a standalone game of the Survival Of The Fittest mod and added two new maps to play on.
Firstly: in an Early Access game it woulds seem that bug fixing and improving the core gaming experience should be priority number one. The dinos are great and all but after a year of seeing them walk straight into cliffs or trees and getting stuck it begins to get old. The new maps are always good, but again, get the core game working properly first before bringing out major content. If you need to get your car fixed you'd start with the engine before you bother to install a fully sick dual-subwoofer surround system and neon lights, amiright?
Secondly: Survival Of The Fittest did not need to be its own standalone game, plain and simple. It just needed to be a mode of the game, which it already was.
Thirdly: the Scorched Earth expansion pack. DLC while the game is still in Early Access? Are you serious? I understand that the studio may need some cashflow (if that's the purpose of the DLC) but perhaps - just perhaps - if they fixed up the overdue issues in the core game players wouldn't get frustrated and write "Not Recommended" reviews, hmmm?
Overall it's still a fun game to play, but I would not recommend buying it until further improvement has been made - at the least on the most glaring of the bugs and issues.

EDIT: This edit is being made 8/30/17, a bit after the full release went live. For anyone who takes a quick stroll through the reviews available, it's pretty obvious to see how poorly people are responding to the full release. So I'll just make/reiterate a few points here. First of all, the game runs fine if you're anywhere above the minimum specifications for it. I BARELY meet the minimum specs and run the game on low memory, and it runs flawlessly 95% of the time. (A few high-intensity areas cause problems, but it's typically short-lived.) I don't have pristine, top shelf, perfect max-setting graphics, sure. But big whoop. People throwing a tantrum over the lack of optmization and persistent bugs either haven't played recently or are embelishing things significantly. There's been a lot of progress in all aspects, from minor bugs that are little more than inconvenience to easy and stable server hosting without the several minutes of loading time the game used to have. Additionally, people are still giving flak for Scorched Earth. If you don't like the paid DLC, DO NOT BUY IT. No one is forcing anyone's hand, there are two free MASSIVE DLC maps, one of which contains content from Scorched Earth, and plenty of player mods to choose from if that's somehow not enough--nevermind procedurally generated ARKs. With regard to people losing their minds over server wipes, WildCard has been very transparent about how things are being transferred and brought over from servers being taken down. Chalk this up to people not paying attention to the news regularly put out for this game which they care so much about. Or don't, since they all seem to be quitting. As a final point, there is the price. Yes. The game has gone up to $60. You can agree or disagree with the reasoning, but frankly that's not going to change anything. The game has been out for a long time in EA and has gone on sale at almost every conceivable opportunity. WildCard was transparent on the point that there'd be a price increase. No one is getting screwed over here, no matter how people want to spin it. I say the game is worth $60. I think a fair rule is a game is worth buying if you can get an hour out of every dollar spent. Look at the reviews. Even the negative ones. There are tons that are in the thousands, and even more in the hundreds. The game didn't go through any fundamental, earthshaking changes on release. It's the same game. It's worth buying. And if you read the news posts, you'll know. WildCard isn't done yet. They plan to keep working on the game. If $60 is out of your price range? Wishlist it. Wait for a sale. The DLCs go on sale too. People are overreacting out of what seems to be a false sense of entitlement, in a lot of cases. Look up the gameplay. Do a bit of research. About the GAME. Not the drama around it. Draw your own opinion. And once you've done that? Hopefully we'll be seeing you waking up on the beach, ready to fight for your survival.
tl;dr: Love the game. It's worth buying. You don't HAVE to buy the DLC (stop calling it P2W...). Most people posting negative reviews are overreacting to say the least. Pay attention to their playtime. You don't sink 200, 500, 700, 1100+ hours into a game if it's NOT good. The DLC did nothing to the base game, so just disregard those idiots and their knee-jerk petulant responses.
In spite of my "limited" playtime, I've thoroughly enjoyed the game. Seems like a lot of people get hung up over the whole "Early Access" thing and the recently released DLC. Honestly, I doubt as much of that would be going around if the "Early Access" denotion was removed. The game could definitely use improvements in some areas and there are absolutely some bugs here and there, but that's any game--it's come a long way since I first bought it, and saying that it "doesn't feel like a finished game" would be an outright lie. With respect to the DLC, while I haven't played it, it seems like a lot of the "reviews" (calling them that is generous) are overstated. Not to mention, for some reason, people are inexplicably behaving as if they were contractually obligated to purchase the DLC. In any case, don't let all the people feeling "betrayed" discourage you from buying at least the base game. Even if you only play it a couple hours at a time in your free time, or just play solo to mess around, or whatever, I think it's absolutely worth the buy. The visuals are spectacular, there's a lot of freedom in how you play, and thanks to the fact that there are mods and access to commands via the console, you can basically tailor the game itself to be however you want to be. There's also the fact that the game is also updated with an impressive level of frequency. Oh, right, and all the people losing their minds over Scorched Earth seem to always fail to mention that there's another, FREE DLC, The Center, with a map almost twice as large as the base map, as I recall. The only "negative" things I can say about the game would be that the system requirements are higher than average, so getting it to run on a lower end rig can definitely be a chore. Nevermind if you're one of those people who demands constant >60 FPS with no drops at 1080p or whatever. Otherwise, though, contrary to a lot of reviews, it really is fine. My only significant issue is entering and leaving water (specifically the camera shift from surface to under water) will cause a momentary freeze/frame drop/whatever. That is legitimately the worst thing I can say about the game, though. My only other issue has been that, in solo, taming creatures legitimately is exceptionally time-consuming. But, then, the game is really meant to be played with many people, and it is significantly more fun with a group. So I think that point is moot. Main takeaway here is that this game is a delight, and I'd happily have bought it at a higher price. I look forward to my next several hundred hours in this game.

NOTE: This game is EARLY ACCESS, incase those of you who are to lazy to read 2 words and rather read my positive review and argue on it instead. Expect the main game plus ARK expansion(s) to have bugs, glitches, and exploits as it further develops to fix those bugs, glitches and exploits and to add new content such as dinosaurs, items and more.
PROS:
*It's challenging.* A challenging game is a good game, mostly when you first start and try to tame your first less dangerous dinosaur then go on to more dangerous dinosaurs such as gigi, t-rex, etc...If it were to easy, then it would get boring quickly, now as you get better, it could get a bit boring.
*Amazing graphics.* As game development gets more, and more advanced with better quality and additional stuff to make the game more beautiful, I say ARK takes one of those awards for amazing graphics. (Long as you have a good graphics card.)
*Survival, crafting, building, exploring, taming, breeding, and care.* The kind of survival ARK gives is not only worrying about carnivor dinosaurs, but you got to worry about the weather, hunger, thirst, and players. (If you play on pvp servers.) You also got to craft in order to harvest stuff more quickly, you got to build a base to stay warm or out of the cold or from carnivor dinosaurs or players, you got to explore in order to get different resources like pearls, iron, crystals, and other dinosaurs to tame. Then you got breeding, how many games have that? That you can make a stronger dinosaur by breeding 2 high level dinosaurs to make the ultimate one! Plus baby dinosaurs! This game also makes you have to care for them, got to put food in their inventory so they don't starve out.
*Updates, patches, and fixes.* The team that is developing this game makes good timing on releasing updates, and patches to fix those bugs, glitches, and exploits. Yes, they don't release them everyday, but that's because it's hard to make a game and fix those issues without creating new ones.
~~~~~~
CONS:
*Requires/Optional Good Graphics Card.* Takes a good computer and graphics card to run the game with decent to good settings.*
*Hackers & trolls.* Lets face it, no matter what game you play, you're gonna run into these in the offical and sometimes community servers. But less on community servers if admins are active and do their job to get rid of them "ban them."

The official servers are pretty slow and grindy, but once you get into 5x unofficial servers it becomes a lot of fun while still having a good amount of challenge and things to aspire to. I love building houses and taming a few dinos and getting powerful. PvP is fun, although destroying things takes a lot less time than building them haha.

As you see, I have put about 3,000 hours into the game and have been playing for almost 2 years. I am a hunter level founder and have spent almost as much money as I have time into the game (more than I care to admit to). It really hurts that I have to re post my review and change it to negative, but I am honest and not a fanboy. I will try to be a short as possible and just list my various problems with this game.
- RNG. Enough said about that
- Weapons have no impact. One of the fun aspects of any shooter is feeling the pain you're dishing out to your enemies. This game does not do that.
- Lackluster quests and lore. I have never been more bored in my life with lore than I have been with this game. It's vague and uninteresting.
- The cesspool that is the community. Seriously, just avoid the forums and region chat. It'll give you cancer.
- DE. While I do not hate the game, I do dislike the developers. There's a reason why they stay up past midnight working on every major update while no other companies do that. They have no structure and that's not a good thing. As big as they are, there's no excuse for the lies, stealth nerfs, and procrastination.
- Painfully slow movement. With "Parkour 2.0" they removed coptering. I am fine with that as long as you can add in something replace it to keep the fast pace. DE did no such thing and instead made us slower, probably to make the grind more tedious and try to force us to buy their stupid prime access and new weapons of the moment that they're pedalling.
- No character at all and/or cringeworthy jokes. Seriously, Ordis needs to go die in a hole. He is NOT funny and is very annoying. The only character that was funny, became unfunny because of DE's lack of sense of fun. I refer to Darvo of course, DE ruined their only good character. Also, the newest quest was just terrible and made me realize even more how unoriginal anything in this game is. Sentients is a stupid♥♥♥♥♥name for a race and are obvious cheap knockoffs of the reapers from Mass Effect. There was a point where scorpions (another unoriginal rip off from MK) had the description "make the pain feel good." Instead of adding nice descriptions like that to add character, DE opts in instead to remove that and not add anymore like that.
Overall, just play something else. I am not even getting into how much of a rip off the plat prices and market prices for all the garbage that's being pedalled is. This game has no fun factor at all. It has nothing.
Just came back after a year of not playing. Can confirm it is not burn out, the game is just gradually getting worse.
-Nitain Extracts are hands down the worst resource ever implemented into this game. These just need to go. There is no saving them, ♥♥♥♥ whoever thought these were a good idea.
-Defection and Infested Salvage mission types are cancer. I don't know who at DE thought escort missions were fun, but you're wrong. Also, why are SO MANY mission types in warframe a defend the objective type mission? Just please stop.
-Riven mods are fine, but why are weapons like Soma and Dread able to get them too? This was an easy way to fix some of the power creep and yet DE somehow screwed it up by allowing Soma and Dread and Boltor Prime to get these mods.
-The Sands of Inaros, Glast Gambit, and Chains of Harrow quests are bad. They are extremely repetitive and uninteresting. Octavia's Anthem and the War Within are good though.
-So many of the new weapons that came out in the last year are just garbage. I holster leveled so many new weapons and many of them were really resource intensive and expensive. Of the 2 that I enjoyed, one of them was not worth keeping (Stradavar) and the other (Tenora) I kept, but why is there such a shortage of good secondary weapons?
-Sortie reward pools are garbage. 4000 endo, Forma, Ayatan sculpture, standard focus lens, and the exilius adapater are insulting. These should be removed from the pool altogether.
-Even more annoying enemy design. I'm talking about those annoying little things that Coprus Snipers deploy, Mutalist Swarm and Tar infested, and Nox. None of these things add anything to the game.
-On the topic of enemies, stunlock is not good design. Neither the player nor enemies should be able to stunlock. Also, why do the corpus now have TWO nullifier enemies? Creativity must be running wild in DE's offices.

As far as I can tell, this game exists to give console gamers the illusion of not sucking at video games while not-so-subtly milking them for every dollar they have.
You are a ninja robot. Here is your melee weapon. Would you like a bow or gun? Would you like a pistol or throwing knives? Now, don't pay any actual attention to anything as you valiantly press "forward" through linear levels, one-shotting every enemy you encouter by choosing to either executing a devastating chain of attacks by pressing the left mouse button, or pressing the 1-4 keys to activating abilities that don't actually change the outcome of the battle, but are just flashier ways of one-shotting enemies. Smash open the containers you find every 30ft to find lots of ammunition  and health packs you don't need. Every level is a speedrun straight to the end, because there's nothing to see or do anyways. Run along walls, slide along the floor, do flips off things, and lots of other cool moves that make you feel like a real badass!
WASN'T THAT FUN!? Now head back to your ship. Go to the marketplace to find a new weapon. $$$$$CASH TIME$$$$$ RealMoney.RealMoney.RealMoney.RealMoney.RealMoney. [I seriously couldn't even find the items that took in-game credits]. Now it's time to upgrade your look! Add a decoration to the hilt of your weapon! RealMoney.RealMoney.RealMoney. Change the color of your outfit! Here are the 12 colors you can pick--the other 36 cost RealMoney. Here's 20 other color palletes, each one costing RealMoney. Look at these RealMoney Helmets! RealMoney accessories! RealMoney addons! Now that you've paid us lots of money, you look EVEN COOLER as you LMB ninja flip one-button destruction speedrun without saying a single word to other players.

ARK is a really fun game with a lot of options for how you want to play it. Official servers make for a slower rate of progression with lots of people to both help and hinder your progress. Unofficial (player-hosted) servers can increase the speed of gameplay if you find officals too slow, as well as having a plethora of server options and fan-made mods to diversify gameplay. If you want to avoid interactions with other players, the single player mode has all of the above, and you can later open your single-player world to your friends if you wish.
The adventure is only limited by your creativity and imagination. You can build large sprawling bases and outposts across the map, take to the seas in ships of your own design, or live as a nomad wandering through dense jungles, plains, mountains, and arctic tundra. Engage in wars against enemy tribes of players or form trade alliances and empires. Be a ghost in the trees, striking at opportune moments and disappearing as quickly. Live as a hermit on a deserted island, your only friends the small creatures you feed. Always be aware of your surroundings, for danger doesn't wait for you to find it in this game.
As far as the recent controversy over the Scorched Earth DLC, I can understand the bad precedent it sets for releasing DLC while still in Early Access. However, the base game was not abandoned to pursue DLC cash-grabs, with heavy development still going into the game to bring it into full release. Studio Wildcard seems to be standing behind their game and seeing it through to completion.
If you want a fun game that feels like Minecraft or Rust with dinosaurs and modern graphics, this game is probably for you.

Now that the game is officialy out of Early Access I can finally write a full review. In short, this game is incredible and definitely worth your purchase.
However, that does not mean this game is without it's flaws, and boy does it have flaws.
Now, I play on a mixture of Singleplayer, SP worlds with a few friends, and an unofficial server hosted by a friend and populated with other friends I know, so I have very little knowledge of the public sphere of the game outside of people complaining on the subreddit. With that in mind let me tell you some of the few gripes I still have with the game
-Bosses are still nearly impossible to kill without glitching their AI, which makes getting to the end-game content near impossible without cheating. This is easily my biggest gripe with the game.
-Some tames are frankly stupid to tame. I don't have a problem with passive taming, it's the method used on certain dinos that makes passive tames the worst. Ex. spiders, centipedes, mantis, mantas (especially the mantas), and cave bats. Luckily none of those tames are ever super useful except for the fantastic mantis, and the use of bug repellant makes the process infinitely easier, it can still be a pain, but overall, not a big deal.
-The sea can be a little clunky. I LOOOVE the dinos and content you can find under the sea, some of the most interesting creatures imagineable can be found. Giant Whales that can nom your raft in a single bite, massive squids that grab hold of you and your mount, a salamander that speeds along under the water and provides you oxygen as you need it, A ♥♥♥♥ING MAGICAL LOCHNESS MONSTER FOR CRYING OUT LOUD. With all the amazing content the sea has to offer, I wish there was a little more usability when it comes to sea stuff. Rafts are slow, motorboats are better but takes AGES to craft and is late-game content, the scuba gear fixes all my issues I have with the ocean, but again, it's unlocked at level 75 so late-game content, which is a shame, because I always end up wanting to do ocean stuff, but I know I can't unless I invest 500 points into oxygen, or wait dozens of hours until I get the scuba set.
-Hitboxes are still a bit wonky when dealing with melee, but luckily after a certain point you won't even touch a pike again because of the abundance of guns, so this is only a very small gripe.
-WHERE ARE THE DYNAMIC BRIDGES. I'M SO CLOSE TO BUILDING AN EWOK WORLD OF WONDER AND THIS LITTLE UPDATE HAS BEEN PROMISED FOR YEARS NOW! WC PLEEEEEASE!
All things considered, I really wish WildCard had fixed all the issues the game has before the full release, but in the end the flaws detract from small portions of the game, but not enough to even come close to harming my overall enjoyment of the game as a whole. This game has SO MUCH DAMN CONTENT it baffles me how they manage to add new and interesting dinos almost every week, and it looks like they have no plans of stopping.
Closing thoughts and message to readers: If you like survival games, and collecting a MASSIVE amount of interesting and rideable dinos, building big bases, and using dino friends to help you become king of the island than this is the game for you. Honest score 9/10, with the possibility of a 10/10 once all the main issues have been fixed (which is going to take quite a while).

What can I say about Warframe?
Well, for one it is a very visceral and enjoyable game at its core. The gunplay can be pretty amazing and the devs are constantly coming up with new weapons.
The problem comes in the sense of progression. If you have missed any of the major events (which if you are reading this you almost certainly have) then you will be seemingly forever behind the curve. This is because Digital Extremes tends to put exclusive Weapon Mods in these events. That may not sound too bad, but you should be aware that these mods tend to be keystones in a lot of builds.
If you can put up with the fact that you will generally be behind on a lot of content and power, you'll find the general Space Ninja-ness of the game shines pretty well.

530 hours of time well spent, that's my biggest take-away from Ark.  I don't do the public servers or the open non-official ones, I set up a private server for myself and my girlfriend to play in our own little world which lets us side-step all the sillyness and griefing.
The first hundred hours were by far the best, that sense of adventure and limitless wilderness to explore and all the dangers that exist beyond the camp fire's light at night.  Evolving your home and equipment to the point where those lurking monsters like the Titan Boas are approachable was a significant sense of accomplishment.  Slaying our first Spinosaur (with the help of spike walls) was meaningfully powerful.  Taming your first dinosaur, taming your first Pteranodon, wow.  Finding a good source of Iron, building iron stuff!  Taming your first Quetzal!
You can modify your server quite a bit to suite your tastes - Want to make resource gathering less grindy?  Easy.  Want to turn on a flag that prevents you from accidentally spearing your favourite dinosaur to death?  Easy.  Mods?  Wow there are a lot of cool mods.  (Don't install Small Dragons until you're getting near the end of your experience, they are so awesome but make everything too easy at the same time).  This is a game aimed at larger groups of players working together so it was very appreciated that I was able to modify things to suite just the pair of us playing, its worked out great.
As for end-game content we didn't get into TheIsland's caves too much, a lot of instant-death in there without much reward.  The other maps' caves systems like TheCenter and Vahalla were pretty awesome though.  Because we didn't do the caves we never got enough of those things to summon the bosses but that's okay too, I imagine much like Gigas they have to be approached with greater numbers and its just another bag of hit points any ways.
We haven't bought Scorched Earth yet either, probably do that the next time we decide to play in Ark some more.  Maybe the procedural worlds code will be working by then too.

I have been playing this game for several years now and feel over this time that I have grown as a gamer.  In light of that revelation I felt that I should return to some of my previous reviews and update  them.  Even though I put Warframe down from time to time, it always draws me back in.  I stand by my origional statement that this games development team is more dedicated to keeping this game fun and fresh.  They have just recently dropped a new expansion called The Plains of Eidolon.  This new area is an open world environment for old and new players to explore.  The base area itself is fairly low level so new players aren't jumping into a nightmare zone.  You can adjust the level of the area by taking out high level bounties from quest givers in the city of Cetus.  Cetus acts as a hub, much like the Relays, for players to get missions and turn in rep for rewards from the new factions.  It is not nessecary to take missions or bounties to enjoy The Plains.  You can simply bypass Cetus and jump straight into the base Plains.  Random missions spawn up around you all of the time, which often lead to Lotus bugging you but what else is new.  You can do many thungs on The Plains like fishing, harvesting gems, exploring caves, or just killing the Grineer.  The graphics for this new 'tile set' are far more amazing than anything the Dev's have produced before.  The water and lighting effects are as crisp and natural as you would expect from a AAA publisher.  The overal detail in the terran is complemented by the natural wildlife and the insanity of the occupying Grineer forces.  The transition from day to night and night to day is amazingly well done.  At first I was skeptical about this expansion because it felt very grindy and was rather difficult.  However, after rallying the members of my dojo together, I found that it didn't have to be about grinding rep with the new factions (plus there is a limit to the amount of rep you can get from turning in stuff).  There is plenty to do either solo or in a group on The Plains of Eidolon.  I rate this expansion a 9/10 until the bugs have been worked out (it has been out less than a week at the time of this review).  The overall game itself has always been one that I will be playing for years to come.

Dinosaurs + Survival + Crafting = F*** YES!!!!
Whoever decided that your basic surviving on an island needed hundreds of dinosaurs of all different kinds to cohabit with, that person needs some sort of medal!
I started off building a straw hut, with the skills i had (can learn to use stone/metal through levelling) I built my hut on the edge of the forest by the beach, i thought I'd be safer closer to the water, plus there is food and lots of trees for firewood. It was a lovely hut, looking out across the ocean, such a peaceful view, almost tranquil...almost.
The darkness came rather quickly, I wasn't too scared at first, because i had a crude fire lighting my hut. I was warmish and sheltered. Then i felt the ground tremble beneath my feet, I thought to myself that could easily be one of those Brontosaurus I saw earlier a little way down the beach, it wasn't....I peeked outside my hut, there wasn't anything there. Then I felt the tremble again, only this time it was much bigger and louder, I slowly edged back into my hut and picked up a wooden spear I had made, suddenly the trees behind my hut started to crash down, it was at that point the trembling stopped...
I couldn't hear anything at all, I slowly stepped outside, I looked around into the tree line< it was still so dark to see.
Something bashed up against my hut behind me, I turned quickly, but again there was nothing..it was at that point I felt a cold shiver running up my spine. Whatever was out there, toying with me, was also standing directly behind me right now!!
It let out a blood curdling growl and I could see its breath come past my shoulder, grasping my spear tightly in my hands I turned to see myself face to face with a large carnivore, I was ten paces from my hut, I didn't make it one step before being torn in two.
Dead.
I respawned where i started a little way down the beach, I had lost everything, I decided to go back for my items hoping the beast had moved on. I hid behind a large rock about 40 yards down the beach, it looked clear, so I made a run for it, I could see my items where I had died, just as soon as I had reached my pack, the same beast came running out of the trees at full speed! It had laid a trap and was waiting for me to return! Clever lizard, it charged me down and sent me flying into the shallows, I wasn't dead, but I was badly injured, leg was broken and I was bleeding out. Death was imminent unless I could find a way back onto land to get some healing. Luckily the beast didn't venture far into the water, I thought it couldn't swim, but that wasn't the reason. The water was just as dangerous as the land, if not more so...!!
Dead again.
Respawned, cut my losses and went the other way.
Managed to capture a Pteranodon, made a saddle and flew it away. At last I was safe, there were dangers in the sky too, but I could easily outrun them on this fast bird. I flew over my old hut, I could see clearly now, I had set up base in the nest of a rather angry carnivore and the one that attacked me was only a baby, glad I wasn't around for the mother, who was four times the size!
I now live in a sky base I built, high above an island filled with Herbivores. Getting to and from the island for certain supplies is still a challenge, for the water has some extremely dangerous beasties in it!
10/10 Love this game
It's a test to even the most extreme of survival expert, I thought I was a pro at survival games until I played this!

3. Other than creating mods, the community is often toxic. In official PVE servers, please expect to see others' pillars everywhere which prevent you from building; In official PVP servers, please expect to meet hackers and huge dominating tribes consist of full-level players transfered from other servers.

and you'll see.

Of all the mods(which are your usual weapon upgrades supposed to help you customize your weapons) the only useful ones are the one which allow you to do MORE DAMAGE. So the whole travel across the world of Warframe becomes a story about you stacking damage to grind things to stack some more damage to grind some more etc.etc.

Almost every gameplay mechanic present in warframe could be easily deleted since the only thing necessary for progression is to stack some more damage so these bullet sponges they call enemies in warframe won't care if you mastered the parkour moves or know every enemy type and its weaknesses.
Now lets talk about pros of this game, there are 3 of them: first is art and graphics, second is interesting world and lore with big potential, third is nice sound quality.
So here you have it, massive amounts of grind, nonexistent gameplay, and pretty picture. Game just doesn't work at its core, so don't play it unless you hear about developers suddenly scraping the whole player progression system away and coming up with something new.

---Please note that I am writing this review while Ark is still in EA, and things might be different by the time you read me---
Where do I get started on Ark. The game itself is very much grindy, a pretty slow grind in fact. Because that's what you have to get ready for : everything in Ark takes ages. You play a certain tier of dinos/equipment corresponding to your level, then work your way up, lower tiers becoming easier to handle and higher tier staying at the same relative difficulty, making the "uphill struggle" not too difficult to bear but the game rarely feels any less grindy. And this is true mostly on official servers, where a higher lv, high tier predator tame will take HOURS, not counting all the work you put before said tame into gathering the required ressources. Unofficial servers have other problems which I will not delve into, because this is about the way Wildcard support their own servers and vanilla game.
The game is very challenging at first, but if you power through the first tedious hours, you'll get to see just how deep and enjoyable it is. Though you will also encounter one of your worst ennemies that isn't raiders or wild dinos trying to eat you : bugs and glitches. Losing a tame you spent hours on, and a couple more hours lvling up, sucks, especially when it happens in an instant because you glitched through spikes, walls, clipped a wild dino or even fell through the map (!!?). Ark is Bethesda-levels of bugged and barring the occasionnal transfer bug, Wildcard doesn't give a damn what happened to you or your dino. This is especially impactful the earlier you are in the game and can pretty much turn you off of it for good if you lost a couple of your first tames in the early stages. The fact that there is no backup to restore dinos lost to glitches is a HUGE PROBLEM, that EVERYONE will experience at least once playing this game.
The game itself is really deep as far as strategies and builds go, and there are lots of things to challenge the most hardcore players. Sadly, simply playing doesn't teach you much about the best strategies, the best approaches and builds you can go for. You will have to look through hours of videos and reading to understand some of the deeper aspects of the game, which is where you will feel the huge burden of knowledge that this game comes with. You want a tame? I hope you have a dododex page open in the background. Want to build a cool raft? Better cycle through some videos to understand how snap points work. So on and so forth.
Surviving feels hard, frustrating at first, but in my opinion this is exactly what a survival game should be like. Be warned though that this is a very time consuming game, even more than any other survival, because of the super long taming system and just how far back you can be set up by the smallest mistake. If you don't have much free time on your hands, odds are the game will feel too slow on official servers for you, but do know that most unofficial servers offer increased resource gathering/taming speed to compensate for those of us who want to compete while still having time for work/family. Though this begs a question : Does Wildcard only give a damn about super hardcore players with lots of time on their hands? Because if so, how does the game develop beyond a core foundation of avid players?
Would I recommend Ark? Yes. Overall, because it does what lots of survival games fail at : it immerses you and makes you want to keep going further in your race for power. Dinos feel incredibly satisfying to tame, though some a bit clunky to maneuver, and there is an actual balance between tribes that soon installs itself, creating interesting, player-made scenarios and truly epic battles.
No other online game ever managed to take me in so well, and no other game managed to frustrate me as much.

Experienced players will know this game's real name is "bugframe".

As for the grind/RNG that everyone is complaining about, yes, they exist. But it wasn't that bad because you can have experienced friends help you. There are also some "optimal" ways to play the game to speed up your progress if you do your research well. Farm the right things from the right places, and use certain warframe combinations and builds to farm certain mission types more effectively. Be warned though, there are developers and forum trolls that seem to want to widen the gap between the end-game players and newer players so some of these synergies between warframes are likely to get nerfed. Let's just make the game harder and the grind tougher because who cares about newbies catching up with the endgame players right? If you are not prepared for the grind then don't start playing this game.

If this Jurassic Park Simulator ever escapes from Early Access; is made functional, polished, and balanced; then it may be worth a buy.  As it stands now, its a frustrating, tedious, stressful, unbalanced, unfinished, broken mess, which, at best, serves as a poorly paced timesink.
+ Build Bases
+ Pet Dinosaurs
+ Pretty Graphics
+ Rename Chests
+ Lots of items/upgrades
+- Double Weekends.  Not only are these rates still too slow (most private servers do x10, at all times), but it makes everything you do during the week feel like a waste of time/mats, especially taming.
+- Hunger and Thirst.  While these are only drained by player actions, instead of a permenant poison type effect, they're still only an annoyance, instead of a contributive or integrated part of gameplay.
- Early Access
- Early Access pay2win DLC
- Toxic Community, even on PvE
- Tamed Dino HP was nerfed, by a lot
- No holiday events on the center map
- Airdrops should fall in random locations
- Dino AI is worse than the average zombie
- System Resource Destroyer (memory leaks?)
- The worst graphic and network performance, of all time
- Character customization can break the preview window
- If not installed on an SSD it will take 10+ minutes to load
- Friendly fire, no matter server type, or settings, or alliances
- Dinos and items can glitch through ceilings, floors, and walls
- Building mechanics bug-out if there are multiple snap points nearby
- Server setbacks can cost you hours of work and/or steal rare items
- Demolish only gives half the resources back, should give you the item back
- Inventory weight limits, expiration timers, and durability (especially on armor)
- So many bugs, flaws, inconsistencies, missing features, clunkiness, and worse
- Game being developed for 3+ modes at once, meaning none of them work correctly
- Youtubers, who make this game look interesting, play on privately owned, boosted servers
- Demolishing things can destroy huge chains of other things, without giving any resources
- Every bug, exploit, and issue that I quit playing this game for, over a year ago, is still in the game today.  There are even some ridiculously basic bugs that the devs are too incompetent to fix, like your HP bar always showing as empty, or it saying you gained the wrong level when you levelup, which would literally take 2 letters added in the code to fix, but they don't do it.
- PvP is broken, and equates to PvE raiding of offline bases and/or cheaters who import items
- PvE isn't much better, as you get repeatedly spawn killed before you can even get started, and is still full of griefers, exploiters, cheaters, thieves, and worse.  And to top it all off, PvE still has offline "raiding".
- Whistles are poorly implemented.  While a good idea, having them on random buttons is horrible.  They should simply bind the whistle wheel to something more accessible than ', like Q
- Whistle "Mount" is needed.  Primarily for birds, who like to hover 20 feet above your head, out of reach, and/or spaz around in circles.  The nearest dino would swoop in and you would auto-ride when within range.
-The radial menu changes based on distance, dis-mounting, and/or inventory context, among other things.  It can even change once you've already opened it, causing you to pick the wrong thing, making it one of the worst interaction systems ever developed.
- Taming times are insultingly long, uninformative, and not balanced properly to be interactive/fun or AFKable.  The addition of kibble further broke the already poorly designed taming system.  Now instead of gathering mats, and trying to tame a dino on some sort of timer that should have been balanced, you instead wait around for weeks, to slowly collect kibble-able eggs, and even with kibble, the timers are still ridiculously long.
- Doors are incredibly annoying, even if they worked right, which half the time they don't due to bugs and lag.  They need a way to auto-open/close doors and/or a high level barrier you can simply walk through.
- The devs regularly push back updates, and fail to deliver on promises, but apparently have no problem putting out a paid DLC, when the base game isn't even finished yet
- Because of nerfs to dinos, and the addition of new tools and features, dinos have gone from being fully integrated and necessary companions, to nearly useless vanity pets.  You no longer need one to farm berries, because gardens can grow more than you'll ever need.  The same goes for fiber, as a tool was added to easily harvest that.  Aside from a Quetz, none of them are good for transport anymore, because you basically
a boat with a taming base built on it now.  You no longer need a shark or dolphin, because with scuba gear you can easily make underwater trips, plus there are alternate land-based methods to acquire pearls and oil now.  Chitin, which used to require dedicated and dangerous cave adventures on a sabertooth, are now practically passively acquired for all but the largest projects.  Dinos no longer serve as tanks, combat allies, or even as general travel companions, because their HP was nerfed so hard that any random wild dino can easily kill them.  Pet Dinos were one of, if not the best system that this game had to offer, and now they're irrelevant.  Now they've announced the Tek Tier, which is going to take dinos out of the game even more, as everyone flys around in ironman suits.

I want to state initially that I abosolutely love the premise of this game. Beyond that the execution, for the most part, is nearly flawless. But, there are a few things about it that absolutely break it for me. They are the exact reason why I will not be logging on until these things are fixed. If they are not, then I will still feel as if I got my money's worth, but will be somewhat disappointed.
First, the good things.
+ Emergent gameplay is top notch here. I have rarely felt so immersed in a game and the devs ought to be highly commended for creating something so original and deep.
+ Graphics are great, and the style is solid.
+ Regular content updates are cool to watch and experience, as it makes the game feel alive.
+ Devs tend to listen to the community and impletment community suggestions.
+ Dinos are all unique and provide actual gameply mechanics which are badass!
+ The tech tree is expansive and allows for a feeling of specialization between clanmates. Farmers, Blacksmiths, Architects, Harvesters, etc...
+ PvP is intense with real time being invested by both sides. (See Caveat Below)
+ Strategic base building leads to interesting designs.
So, all of these things lead to an overall terrific game experience and leads me to really want to give it a thumbs up because I really do feel invested in this title. The thing is though that the balance on this game is truely busted. New players can and will get absolutely get shafted by alphas. No matter how much preparation is made, you will be entirely vulnerable while offline. This makes the game less about honest and fair pvp and more about pure griefing. 2x weekend while nice, also entirely breaks this games balance and here is why. Get a flyer, get c4 which can be farmed much faster on 2x weekends, fly over any based and drop c4 on it. Win!!!! There is no possible base defence that can defeat that exploit as turrets have a limited range and flyers do not. I have been in tribes with 16 members and tribes with 2 members, and the fact of the matter is, if your base can be seen from the air it will get raided using this exploit. This isnt the only negative about this game, but it just flat out breaks it and is why I will not return until it is fixed.
Here is the list of negative aspects of the game:
- Constant server de-syncs on servers with a high number of players.
- Significant memory leaks which degrade performance over long play sessions.
- Some wonky hit boxes which get rafts stuck on the center map.
- Flyer exploit mentioned above makes months of work and any base defense entirely pointless.
- Alpha tribes can destroy any new player without any effort whatsoever deterring players entirely from wanting to play.
- Offline raiding has no risk, this isnt pvp its griefing pure and simple.
- A naked player with a club can nearly 1 hit ko a player with full armor. Torper as a stat needs re-working.
- Inventory system is a bit clunky, search features were a great addition, now how about category tabs? All, Structures, Equipment, Materials, Refined Materials, etc...
Now, the performance issues, while important, are difficult to fix and I understand this game will be undergoing optimization up till release. The offline raiding in this game needs a fix asap. Easy fix could be that a base gains immunity 30 minutes after the last tribemate has logged off. This would stop griefers from easily exploiting the fact that some people have to work to make a living, but also be fair in that a tribemate couldn't log off the second the base got attacked to avoid having any damage done. 30 minutes is plenty of time to raid a base. Most importantly this change needs to take place on the official servers for the vanilla game. Un-official servers have already started implementing this rule, and scorched earth has 4 official servrs with this ruleset too. I love this game, but i'll be damned if it isn't broken in the wrong places.
P.S. For any players Complaining about scorched earch being a paid DLC who have over 100 hours on their account. Think about the last AAA 60$ title you have had 100hrs in. How many years ago was it? Was it as good as this game already is?

Warframe, a game that was released in the spring of 2013. At the time of it's release was one of the most dissapointing games available. The very low amount of content available and the simple fact the game had more bugs than lines of code was turning people away from it. However, the staff at Digital Extremes didn't give up, and over the next 4 years they have added an imense amount of content. this can be seen in Warframe's 22 major updates. I will structure my review in two parts, each with it's own gameplay and sound design.
-Part 1: Warframe before update 22
The gameplay in Warframe has evolved a lot since 2013. A brand new movement mechanic, more enemies, more guns, more warframes, more tilesets and even lore. Warframe feels much more fluid compared to how it felt as little as 1 year ago. The introduction of a new movement system revitalised the comunity back in update 17. Update 18 introduced the first cinematic quest to warframe as well as expanding the background lore available. Update 19 introduced the second cinematic quest as well as the operator mode, even if that still is less enjoyable than the warframe combat. The game was in a good place... But during Tennocon 2017 (warframe's own festival) something was revealed... An update that could change how Warframe was played.
-Part 2: Plains Of Eidelon
Update 22 is hands down, the biggest update available for warframe. It introduced the concept of "open world" to a randomly generated tileset game. Update 22 has brought an imense map for tenno to wonder into, unique gameplay mechanics that have nothing to do with shooting and that are surprisingly enjoyable and the concept of "world bosses" even if they are not so much a world boss. Great game. I have 2 accounts. One on steam and one not. It still hasn't gotten old yet. I have spent many days playing the game. It gives you something to think about while working through your day. There are not very many games out there that will make you think (or say) "Oh yay! my frost helmet will be ready when I get home!" You go around the solar system killing enemies to get credits. Then with those credits you buy blueprints for weapons and warframes. Then if you don't already have the resources, you go back into the solar system to get the resources from enemies. You then begin the construction of the item and wait anywhere from 12 hours to 3 days for it to finish. If you want a challenge you can travel into the void to fight harder enemies. This offers a greater reward. Or you can do a nightmare mission which would also be a good choice for advanced players. The hardest thing that I have done in the game is a nightmare alert. In these missions, you have no shield and the anemies are much harder. These missions are for the extremly advanced players. Don't be fooled though, there are things for the novice players too.  You can do a defence mission where you fight off waves of enemies that get progressively harder. You could leave early while everything is easy, or you can stay and push your limits. This game offers something for every style of player. You can upgrade the shields and health of your warframe to make a tank, or you can hone your stealth skills by sneaking through air vents to assasenate your targets. Will you use laser, a flamethrower, a bow, or will you try using only a sword?
