I have mixed feelings about this game. I have owned it for a long time but have not played that much of it. It has certainly improved greatly, and continues to do so at a steady pace.
TL;DR - Best played with friends on a 'Non-Dedicated Host' server with some of the setting set to make the game progress faster. Many problems exist but still fun and functional. Progress seems slow but is steady.
Pros
There is a huge amount of things you can do. You have so much customisation available to you. It takes a long time to progress, but the sense of achievement when you can feel yourself actually getting somewhere is great. Team play is mechanically encoraged. It is one of the best games to play witha friend. Hosting your own server allows access to a huge amount of customisable options, which can take the edge off the grind.
Death is brutal and you lose a lot if it happens.
Cons
Many systems are unclear. You either need someone who already knows what's up, or will have to put in a lot of hours on the wiki.
Many of the mechanics are clunky to use. Building, for example, works, but the snapping and where it meets the ground is still quite messy.
It's hard to run. The game is poorly optimised. This is no where near how bad it used to be. Turn everything down and you will be able to run it. That said, when you can run it at full, it looks amazing.
Bugs are a never ending problem. Mostly to do with dinosaur pathing. They are just so stupid T.T
I have said it is a great game to play with friends, which it is. However, the solo play I find agony. On your own, there are so many recipies you cannot learn due to the way the game is set up.
I would not advise online play. Not to begin with at least. The amount of time required to advance is daunting, made more so when confronted by people who already have done so whilst you're still breaking your hands to get wood from a tree rather than just thatch. Grab some friends and have some community progression, rather than joining a developed tribe and being thrown into all out wars.
The base settings of the game is extremely grinding. Painfully so. I would advise turning up resource gathering, dinosaur taming, exp gain as a base. This creates a far better pace, without making it easy (unless you keep turing the up).
Death is brutal and you lose a lot if it happens.

It's really well done and polished, but have fun paying for all the cool stuff.
I would like it a lot more if you could unlock stuff like Platinum, by like, I don't know, playing the game.
If you got a buck to spare, give it a shot.

So Warframe is a TPS with redundant rpg elements and a whole lot of grind to do if you want to acess all of its content without paying 1000$ or so. Problem is though, there is nothing to do in warframe. This game doesn't have any kind of meaningful progression for the player and the only thing you can strive for is to unlock all of its content, but the content itself is really bland and does not bring much diversity to your gameplay.
Just imagine: of the whole bunch of 200 or so various weapons you will only use at max 5 or 6 just because the only useful weapon in Warframe is the weapon which does more damage. Of all the different warframes(which would be called classes in other games) the most useful are the ones which allow you to do more damage. Of all the mods(which are your usual weapon upgrades supposed to help you customize your weapons) the only useful ones are the one which allow you to do MORE DAMAGE. So the whole travel across the world of Warframe becomes a story about you stacking damage to grind things to stack some more damage to grind some more etc.etc.

Almost every gameplay mechanic present in warframe could be easily deleted since the only thing necessary for progression is to stack some more damage so these bullet sponges they call enemies in warframe won't care if you mastered the parkour moves or know every enemy type and its weaknesses.
Now lets talk about pros of this game, there are 3 of them: first is art and graphics, second is interesting world and lore with big potential, third is nice sound quality.
So here you have it, massive amounts of grind, nonexistent gameplay, and pretty picture. Game just doesn't work at its core, so don't play it unless you hear about developers suddenly scraping the whole player progression system away and coming up with something new.

Warframe, a game that was released in the spring of 2013. At the time of it's release was one of the most dissapointing games available. The very low amount of content available and the simple fact the game had more bugs than lines of code was turning people away from it. However, the staff at Digital Extremes didn't give up, and over the next 4 years they have added an imense amount of content. this can be seen in Warframe's 22 major updates. I will structure my review in two parts, each with it's own gameplay and sound design.
-Part 1: Warframe before update 22
The gameplay in Warframe has evolved a lot since 2013. A brand new movement mechanic, more enemies, more guns, more warframes, more tilesets and even lore. Warframe feels much more fluid compared to how it felt as little as 1 year ago. The introduction of a new movement system revitalised the comunity back in update 17. Update 18 introduced the first cinematic quest to warframe as well as expanding the background lore available. Update 19 introduced the second cinematic quest as well as the operator mode, even if that still is less enjoyable than the warframe combat. The game was in a good place... But during Tennocon 2017 (warframe's own festival) something was revealed... An update that could change how Warframe was played.
-Part 2: Plains Of Eidelon
Update 22 is hands down, the biggest update available for warframe. It introduced the concept of "open world" to a randomly generated tileset game. Update 22 has brought an imense map for tenno to wonder into, unique gameplay mechanics that have nothing to do with shooting and that are surprisingly enjoyable and the concept of "world bosses" even if they are not so much a world boss. I'm going to skip over all the issues with the developer and just review the game that I played, which was both the base game and Scorched Earth.
Pros:
- Satisfying crafting and building.
- Dinosaur taming that goes beyond simply having a cool looking mount. Dinosaurs have different abilities that assist with every aspect of your survival.
- The world feels mysterious and I felt immersed from the very beginning and the ominous obelisks floating in the distance fill me with a sense of forboding that I never quite shake, no matter how established my island becomes.
- There are a wide variety of settings for both private games and server hosting. The tools are only getting better too.
- The game itself looks good with surprisingly few graphical errors. I've heard that there are complaints, but I am able to run on max settings with  a GTX 980 Ti, i7-5930K, and 16 GB of RAM. I haven't looked up hardware in awhile, but I know I'm behind a couple generations.
- For all the complaints about paid DLC, Scorched Earth actually brings a lot t the table with an enormous new map full of new enemies, new recipes, and new lore. I am currently awaiting the journal that will add story to the game in the form of notes created at certain areas like ruins.
Cons:
- Corpses will slide underneath objects occasionally. For example, I once killed a dodo only to watch it slide beneath a rock. Luckily, I was able to break the rock and get the bird underneath for that precious meat.
- Occasionally, there are issues with placing objects, but it's still much better than the building in Fallout 4, which I also enjoyed.
- You can run out of stuff to do in a hurry unless you like repeating. Leveling goes pretty quickly, and you'll eventually find yourself banking engram points to just spend as needed.
A lot of things are dependant on what server you're on. Alternate server settings and a plethora of mods ensure that no two servers will offer quite the same experience. This is both good and bad as a difficult server will make others seem boring, while an easier server will leave you ill-prepared for the real deal. This goes double if you move from an easy server to Scorched Earth.
Overall, it's a great game to play. Once again, I don't care what your issues are with the developers. It's still fun and it was worth what I paid for it. In the end, that's all I care about.

Dear future Tenno,
This is a game about working hard towards your goal of becoming a badass, armed-to-the-teeth, bonified space ninja. Well technically there is a space pirate...ninja...and a gunslinger ninja...and...a dragon.....also i'm pretty sure there's a kitty cat berserker....then theres also primed versions and I mean the game is like..really lean on the whole ninja title..You do ninja stuff though! I promise! Basically you can either be a badass ninja, or a crazy hunter killer who is extremely efficient and murdering everything that moves...wait is that a ninja? I may have just described a ninja twice.....buuuuuut I am getting ahead of myself here.
Basically you start off as a scrub like any other game. You work hard and unlock nodes to planets and assassinate bosses and such. It may sound pretty flat when I say it like this. But ooooh boy. There's just something special when you sprint towards an enemy...spin around and cleave their entire body in half...then pull out a bow and shoot a single arrow that pins 3 other enemies to a wall. Or using one of your warframe's powers to decimate an entire squad of enemies.
Just know this game is pretty grind-y. You're going to be running certain missions repeatedely for a RNG item to drop that allows you to build something awesome. Like another warframe...or a weapon...or a pet...or..whatever. There is end tier content like raids and high leveled void missions and such. The only main problem this game has is the grind factor. But hey, if you enjoy being a friggen space ninja, and you enjoy murdering things. Then go ahead and give this game a try!
Also there is a pay-to-win kinda thing in-game. But it should be more or less called the pay to not wait as long to craft everything in the game...thing. Don't let that bother you though, everything in the game is unlockable for free. Again, this game is grindy and requires patience...y'know..like...like a ninja...Just give it a try!
-Sincerely, Other Tenno Person!

Now this...this is a great game as a F2P (free-to-play). The upsides is that it is cooperative with friends, who you can have a clan of sorts with and have you own Dojo (essentially a base) where you can research new weapons and equipment. You get different warframes which means a plethora of new abilities, skills and attack styles with a VAST array of weapons to choose from. Fighting against many different alien-esque species, you can find yourself passing so many hours keeping up with alerts, void missions, or trying to fight off the pesky STALKER (yes, a random guy with a bad-a##ed scyth with hunt you and hack you up....if you arent careful)...which leads me to my main issues.
The issues I have are that all the different missions are basically same map - and after several hours of playing, all the missions are the same mission over and over. Dont get me wrong, its still great, but it just gets really repetative. I SHOULD POINT OUT HOWEVER that DE are working on fixing this.
The second is the whole micro-transaction thing. You buy platinum which will let you buy weapons and warframes straight up - no need for the grinding. It gets EXTREMELY tiring grinding for everything. I should know, I buy too much platinum -
Overall, warframe is a great game and I would recommend it to anyone looking for a great, free to play action shooter game on PC.

To start off, yes i am a founder and yes i have played over 2 months worth of hours in game, but even i still don't know everything, so there is a wiki for it all.... and well they even have youtube channels if you get really into the game that much. So yea, then there are the developers, who are wonderful and literally Will respond if you are having problems in-game, or have a suggestion, but due to there fan/player base don't expect for them to answer every little detailed question.
As far as content, there are consistent game updates that have either a newer warframe or weapon/s that are added to the clan dojo/market if that's a thing for you. Lore is now a thing as well. and with that comes gameplay. I personally am a keyboard & mouse kinda guy and i have the Steam controller as well (takes a bit of getting used too) but it is supported as well.
The biggest issue atm is when you start you're limited and to some it feels like there is no true sense of direction, BUT that's the beauty of it all, you can start anywhere your Mastery Rank allows (i will talk about in a second). being in an active clan helps Sooooooo much due to the dojo access and weapons (arguable some of the best non-primed/non-syndicate weapons are located) so realistically you have freedom to expand by completing each planet, leveling up weapons, warframes and earning affinity to rank up your MR (Mastery Rank) and get better.
Mastery is a thing that scales your true knowledge in game (and well, what you actually have access too). it is ranked up by earning affinity (this games xp) and when you just think your about to rank up you have... you said it... a rank up test, to some its easy, and to some depending on how far they have progressed in the game, it can get really challenging, each test has it difficulty, from eliminating enemies a certain way to using some tactics (just meaning some are just require your commons sense some require you to use advanced thinking). upon completion, your are granted the next rank up, if failed you wait 24hrs to retake it, but any affinity gained will be counted for your next rank. It is possible to get enough affinity to level the next day you log in after passing a test.
There you have it, a small beginners guide to the game, if you have any questions my ingame name is NJDevil2k12 and i can assist with your questions if need be, but for now..... farewell my Tenno the Void is Calling for my presence.

You start off on the beach, in nothing but your underpants and your fists with a strange glowing stone embedded in your wrist, on an island full of things that know you're a meal on two, delicious little legs.  The beach seems safe, fluffy, colorful dodos waddle past you, chirping happily as they go about their pointless existence, Trikes will amble past, completely ignoring you as long as you don't antagonize them and if you do gather up the courage to try and bring one down for it's hide and meat, pray it doesn't have friends near by.
Your first dive into the ocean to look at the coral reefs send you fleeing the water in terror as a massive, grinning face comes swimming at you from the depths as a shark the size of a baby whale pursues you into the shallows before lazily swimming off once it's meal escapes.
You punch trees for wood, gather stones off the sand and harvest berries for food and plant fiber to craft yourself some form of clothes that offer little protection but keep you a little warmer at night when the cold sets in.  You'll be living on the beach for a while to get your feet under you while you figure out where you are and how to make things work.
You finally fashion some crude, brittle weapons and eventually have the thrilling satisfaction of killing your first trike.  Using it's hide, you craft your first set of leather armor, and armed with your bone spear, a water skin and the first good haul of food in your inventory, you feel powerful.  The beach is no match for you anymore, and you make your way to the dense trees of the forest bordering the beach.
Before you can reach the underbrush, however, you hear the pattering of feet running after you, and a high pitched purr comes from behind.  Turning around, you see a tiny, adorable creature on two legs.  It looks like a miniature, baby raptor but with the cutest face you've seen yet since the Dodos.  It looks up at you, it's head following you as you move around.  You back up, it follows, you move away, it runs after you and once again, stops at your feet, gazing up into your face.  Suddenly, you hear more footsteps and more purrs running from the underbrush, two, three... five more join the first and gather around your feet and all the sudden your wonder turns to unease and you realize something is very, very wrong as you start backing away.
Your character suddenly shouts in pain as the first lunges at you, emboldened by its friends and the whole pack attacks.  You attack them, thinking you can easily kill them all they're so small, but you stab and you stab until your spear breaks and are lucky if you only kill one.  By now you're at half health and you run, fleeing for your life as the Compy pack chases until your stamina runs out and you can't go any further, left at the mercy of the pack as you try to beat them off with your fists.
You wake up again, naked on a new stretch of beach you haven't seen before, your inventory empty and all of your accomplishments from the past 3 hours gone.  You feel small, weak and fully at the mercy of the island now as you eye the forest warily, and set off once again punching trees for wood, knowing that what happened was only going to happen again, and again, and again, and again until you're finally strong enough to brave the inland with the help of an old, befriended trike who will defend you at the cost of its life against the bloodlust of this unforgiving island.
Welcome to Ark.
><><>
Ah, Ark.  We go back a long time in a viscous love/hate relationship on a road full of ups and downs.
First off, I want to say that if it were not for unofficial servers, I wouldn't be playing this game period.  If you're looking to buy this game, know that first and foremost, this game is a huge time sink.  Taming takes hours upon hours of babysitting unconscious dinos, unable to leave for some types, breeding takes hours upon hours of hatching/raising/hand feeding.
Want to tame a high level bronto?  Have fun, you're not going to sleep tonight if you want it.  The tame times on the larger dinos are pure insanity.
It's a task nearly impossible for one person, but unofficial servers allow the admins to set the rates they want and you can easily find one that fits your time schedule and makes the game fun rather than tedious, taming quick and exciting and gathering no longer a dread.
The game is unstable, which is really my only main complaint.  There are lots of crashes and disconnects, which then cause your character to fall unconscious while the game continues to play around you and results in the loss of dinos and gear/items (and woe if your character happens to fall through the world).  I'm hoping down the line this will be fixed and optimized.  Currently, it takes quite a beefy machine to run this game at an acceptable rate/graphics.  There's what I like to call silly putty mode, which I played in for half a year before I got a decent machine.  The world now is absolutely stunning with a nice graphics card.

Amazing game, I love it to pieces, but the issues that plague it will ruin your enjoyment a lot and sometimes cause rage quits, but if the concept of this game compels you, you probably won't regret it once you get past the unforgiving first few hours of the game.

WF went from a game where they had cool ideas about what they wanted to do, to a bunch of half baked, never quite finished or polished ideas that eventually just seem abandoned. I.E. the revamp of damage/armour and weapons, Archwing, or Void Tower missions. Void missions were meant to be hard, and for the elite, and have amazing loot according to DESteve before they were implemented, but in reality they are very easy, and just another place to run a million missions hoping for the 1% drop chance for the item you want.
As I see it now:
Pros:
+Art team (sound, animation, graphics i.e.) is AMAZING (no sarcasm).
+Not P2W. Is it pay for convience, or pay to skip? Yes, to a fault imo, considering the prices are stupid. But everything can be earned in game, even if it takes a stupidly long time, and that time doesn't corrospond to how good whatever the item you wanted is.
+Stamina/movement has been reworked. No longer do you run like a ninja. Who has asthma. And both their left lung just collapsed. And their right lung. And just had both their legs broken in a tragic zorencoptering incident.
Cons:
-massive, MASSIVE grind and time walls (sometimes at the same time). Some grind is good, some waiting is ok. Done properly it enhances a game wonderfully, making that epic item so much sweeter and cool. WF however uses it in place of real content.
-P2P connection, no one likes lag, and WF rakes in cash. Servers should be a priority for WF.
-weapons are kinda meh. All the weapons of a given type feel the same (i.e. all bows feel the same, all snipers feel the same down to the RoF). By that, I mean they all just have slightly altered stats, none feel like they have recoil, or a worry about accuracy, or take more than point and click in the general direction. What I'm trying to say is that a lot of weapons (imo) just don't FEEL like they should compared to a lot of other shooters.
-Plat is incredibly ♥♥♥♥ing expensive. I.e. weapon is around $10 roughly, and a new frame is roughly $20 iirc (assuming you don't want to do the farming for them). To make it worse, there's no rhyme or reason to their pricing. A garbage weapon might be more expensive than a better weapon for no reason, along with NO WAY to try before you buy ANYTHING. And contrary to what some people will say no, just because you like something does not automatically make it good, viable, or top tier.
-Enemies are stupid. The only difficulty there is for enemies is how many they throw at you, and how high their armor/HP/Shields and damage are. There's no attempt here, not even say, to make the trash mobs stand by the heavy enemies who either give buffs, have bigger guns, and use special abilities (i.e. projecting a shield).
-Farming is either survival, interception, or defense missions. Everything else is either a ghost node (level/area) generally.
-Balance... doesn't really exist outside of a general nebulous concept. This doesn't sound like a problem, but balance is the lifeblood of any game. I'm not talking about one or two slightly OP weapons, I'm talking EVERYTHING is whacked. Clan tech weapons (very expensive to craft weapons) are mostly worse than what you can find in the markets for way cheaper (roughly 1/3 fewer mats in some cases). Worse, there are mods that have been around for a year roughly, and are just as useless as the day they were created, for example, "Warm Coat" is a mod that reduces shield reduction on missions that have the completely random ice effect, halving your shields. Besides the obvious flaw of not knowing when you'll enter an ice mission, you'll get better results from simply using a +shields mod of the same cost as Warm Coat.
-No endgame stuff. Sure there's raids, but that's just another place for them to add grind walls in place of real content. You'll do some massive farming, but at the end of the day, it was all for naught unless you wanna run hour long survivals, or high wave interception/defenses. Once you get a weapon decently modded, any skill requirement goess out the window.
-Content is sparse, and often trapped behind massive grind or time walls to stretch it out. Problem with that is that it's stretched nearly to the breaking point. Content comes down to grinding weapons/frames to level 30, forma'ing them (aka prestige) to make them slightly better, and repeat. Fusing mods to make them better and stronger, assuming you can FIND the ♥♥♥♥ing ones you want in the first place.
-New players have it extremely rough. They start off with garbage versions of mods, unknowingly, and the planets they unlock generally have the same mats, or atleast not enough different mats, which makes crafting anything very hard early on. Unless a new player has an older player helping them, they're SOL. And the one thing that was supposed to help new players, the codex, doesn't. You need to spend time unlocking it to learn enemy weaknesses, and what drops from them, making it even tougher for new players to learn about their enemies. Oh, and to scan the enemies? That costs credits for a consumable.
(INB4 "But there's a wiki!" the info should be in game, easily accesible.)
-Lore, what they have is great, and really sets up a unique universe, the problem is that they don't have almost ANY anywhere. Prime 'frames in their codex entry have a tidbit, normally just an short few paragraphs, as do some of the other codex entries, and TSD which adds a good bit about the tenno. This isn't so much of a con as they need more lore, which would be fantastic.
-Rushing
Inherently nothing is wrong with rushing, but as a new player getting put with the more experienced players who just rush missions mean you're getting left behind, and missing vauable loot (for a new player) as the mission ends early because people got to the extraction zone and started a 60 second timer to end the mission.
-Communication
This is their biggest fault, their streams are a mess. DEsteve or DEScott usually being the cause. I feel sorry for DERebecca trying to control their lazy attitude towards the stream, treating it as a place to drink beer instead of answering question the community asks, and avoids/dodges questions with half answers or jackassery to (rarely) straight up insulting people (mild insults at best however) and flatout telling them they're wrong despite everything saying they're not (i.e. armor in D1.0 scalled up to a 95% reduction pretty quickly, and every weapon that did not ignore armor was pretty useless, DESteve was against reworking this, even though all but 4-5 weapons were considered useless).
Also, going along with this, they're NOTORIOUSLY poor at including all changes in the patch notes.
-Bugs! I expect some, hell, EVERYONE does. But DE either seems to do ZERO testing, or so little that people are unable to log onto the servers at all more than once. As in a 100% fail rate for everyone, not just a server overload or something. So, either they're not doing enough in house testing, or they're letting things get changed at the last moment before a patch rolls out.
Conclusion:
I had high hopes for this game, and DE pretty much crushed them. If you like grinding korean MMO style, go for it. Otherwise stick with something better, like Evolve Stage 2 or, Overwatch. Or almost anything else.Overall, as the game is now, I cannot recommend it, as no matter how much things change, the more they stay the same.

You start off on the beach, in nothing but your underpants and your fists with a strange glowing stone embedded in your wrist, on an island full of things that know you're a meal on two, delicious little legs.  The beach seems safe, fluffy, colorful dodos waddle past you, chirping happily as they go about their pointless existence, Trikes will amble past, completely ignoring you as long as you don't antagonize them and if you do gather up the courage to try and bring one down for it's hide and meat, pray it doesn't have friends near by.
Your first dive into the ocean to look at the coral reefs send you fleeing the water in terror as a massive, grinning face comes swimming at you from the depths as a shark the size of a baby whale pursues you into the shallows before lazily swimming off once it's meal escapes.
You punch trees for wood, gather stones off the sand and harvest berries for food and plant fiber to craft yourself some form of clothes that offer little protection but keep you a little warmer at night when the cold sets in.  You'll be living on the beach for a while to get your feet under you while you figure out where you are and how to make things work.
You finally fashion some crude, brittle weapons and eventually have the thrilling satisfaction of killing your first trike.  Using it's hide, you craft your first set of leather armor, and armed with your bone spear, a water skin and the first good haul of food in your inventory, you feel powerful.  The beach is no match for you anymore, and you make your way to the dense trees of the forest bordering the beach.
Before you can reach the underbrush, however, you hear the pattering of feet running after you, and a high pitched purr comes from behind.  Turning around, you see a tiny, adorable creature on two legs.  It looks like a miniature, baby raptor but with the cutest face you've seen yet since the Dodos.  It looks up at you, it's head following you as you move around.  You back up, it follows, you move away, it runs after you and once again, stops at your feet, gazing up into your face.  Suddenly, you hear more footsteps and more purrs running from the underbrush, two, three... five more join the first and gather around your feet and all the sudden your wonder turns to unease and you realize something is very, very wrong as you start backing away.
Your character suddenly shouts in pain as the first lunges at you, emboldened by its friends and the whole pack attacks.  You attack them, thinking you can easily kill them all they're so small, but you stab and you stab until your spear breaks and are lucky if you only kill one.  By now you're at half health and you run, fleeing for your life as the Compy pack chases until your stamina runs out and you can't go any further, left at the mercy of the pack as you try to beat them off with your fists.
You wake up again, naked on a new stretch of beach you haven't seen before, your inventory empty and all of your accomplishments from the past 3 hours gone.  You feel small, weak and fully at the mercy of the island now as you eye the forest warily, and set off once again punching trees for wood, knowing that what happened was only going to happen again, and again, and again, and again until you're finally strong enough to brave the inland with the help of an old, befriended trike who will defend you at the cost of its life against the bloodlust of this unforgiving island.
Welcome to Ark.
><><>
Ah, Ark.  We go back a long time in a viscous love/hate relationship on a road full of ups and downs.
First off, I want to say that if it were not for unofficial servers, I wouldn't be playing this game period.  If you're looking to buy this game, know that first and foremost, this game is a huge time sink.  Taming takes hours upon hours of babysitting unconscious dinos, unable to leave for some types, breeding takes hours upon hours of hatching/raising/hand feeding.
Want to tame a high level bronto?  Have fun, you're not going to sleep tonight if you want it.  The tame times on the larger dinos are pure insanity.
It's a task nearly impossible for one person, but unofficial servers allow the admins to set the rates they want and you can easily find one that fits your time schedule and makes the game fun rather than tedious, taming quick and exciting and gathering no longer a dread.
The game is unstable, which is really my only main complaint.  There are lots of crashes and disconnects, which then cause your character to fall unconscious while the game continues to play around you and results in the loss of dinos and gear/items (and woe if your character happens to fall through the world).  I'm hoping down the line this will be fixed and optimized.  Currently, it takes quite a beefy machine to run this game at an acceptable rate/graphics.  There's what I like to call silly putty mode, which I played in for half a year before I got a decent machine.  The world now is absolutely stunning with a nice graphics card.

Amazing game, I love it to pieces, but the issues that plague it will ruin your enjoyment a lot and sometimes cause rage quits, but if the concept of this game compels you, you probably won't regret it once you get past the unforgiving first few hours of the game.

An extremely well polished, sleek, sexy third person shooter/hack-n-slash where you take control of a space ninja.
Warframe will see you rise from your slumber, at the behest of some broad wearing an impractical visor, who will promptly start telling you what to do, where to go, and how to do it. She will provide such riveting input as "It's the Grineer!" and "Doors sealed." and who could forget the classic: "Why do you spend so much time playing that game?". From there, you galavant around the solar system slaughtering thousands and doing physically impossible things like:
- Operating around Mercury, a planet so close to the sun the average temperature is about 400 degrees.
- Traversing a plane of existence populated only by mind-controlled techno-zombies.
- Getting the last piece of Rhino Prime.
Warframe likes to build itself up as a complex and lore-rich game filled with boatloads of content and a tight combat system.
Unfortunately, what it actually is is a more technologically sophisticated version of Farming Simulator. You want that fabulous looking gun from the market? Well get your wallet out because this game will suck you dry like a vampiric ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. If you don't like spending extortionate amounts of disposable income on a FREE TO PLAY GAME, then tighten your belt, grab your pillow and get ready to play the captivating, soul-crushing experience that is Warframe.
The game's general gameplay is a fun blend of shooting and slashing. Your character carries both ranged and melee weapons, as well as using a set of abilities that come with whichever "Warframe"(Class) you choose. These weapons can range from pistols, to rocket launchers, to flamethrowers, to a gun that literally shoots rubix cubes. The variety of these weapons is a major selling point of the game. As it stands right now, there are dozens of weapons to choose from, as well as a great deal of "classes", most of which are well thought out and interesting. Some of which make you question the whole "space ninja" ideal (really? A water frame?).
When you first get into Warframe, you'll see all this content, the lovely graphics, the polished sound design and fluid combat and think "All of this is free to play?! Hot damn that's amazing!".
Sadly, this is what most people think before they begin to understand DE's business model.
Warframe is a game about grinding. You perform the same missions ad nauseum for the sole purpose of levelling up your weapons/classes, and gathering materials that have a mercilessly low drop rate. If you've played World of Warcraft, you know the feeling of running the same boss again and again and having it not drop what you want. That concept is applied to this entire game. You will grind. Forever. I've played for over 850 hours and I only just got every warframe and about 80% of the weapons.
It's a structure of loot-tables and abysmal drop rates designed to stretch the game's overall playing time to the longest possible length. It teases the player with what they could accomplish, and then forces them to spend entire days playing for a single item, only to hit them with hurdle after hurdle.
You want to get a new Warframe (class)?
Here's what you need to do:
- Play the game until you unlock the planet's final boss.
- Grind the boss, many of which feature invincibility phases and can take up to 5 minutes to kill each time even with a full team of players.
- Pray to whatever gods you believe in that 1 of 3 "parts" drop.
- Run the boss again and again for the other 2.
- Build each 'part' of the frame, each of which costs even more resources, credits, and literally 12 hours of real-world time.
- Buy the 'blueprint' from the marketplace, which is often extremely costly for newer players.
- Use your parts to fashion the final Warframe, which will take, and I'm not kidding, THREE DAYS TO BUILD.
Remember raid lock-outs from WoW? That concept where if you kill a boss you have to wait a whole week until you can kill it again? The same thing exists in this game, but in a different form. You will spend most of your time in Warframe waiting for things to happen. You will wait for weapons/warframes to build. You will wait for the (entirely randomised) alerts to pop up with something good. You will wait for something interesting to happen. It's like if someone made Stormwind into a full game.
Every now and then, the developers will throw out an event, these are usually half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ completely rigged against the player, extremely poorly thought-out, rampant with bugs, and a massive waste of time. But they'll make you feel forced to play the terrible content by granting players that force themelves to endure it a big shiny one-of-a-kind weapon. And it often isn't worth the trouble.
The story isn't much to write home about. You wake up from stasis and find yourself in the middle of a warzone between clones, zombies and jews. From there you stab and slash your way to victory. Victory isn't actually in the game yet though, so you might want to set your sights a bit lower first. Maybe try getting Volt Prime, I dunno.
Warframe is a good game. I would even say a great game. It's just dragged down by developers that don't understand how to balance or handle the game they've created. It's a restrictive, neutured experience which constantly keeps players on the edge. A nefarious business model based entirely around the carrot-on-a-stick method.
If you don't mind grinding, if you have friends that already play this, if you don't mind developers consistently wrecking the game every patch and if you have a great deal of podcasts you need to catch up on, then I would recommend Warframe.
If you want a game that will grant progression based on how much time and effort you put into it, then I would not. The game will slam you with real-life time restraints and force you to wait days for content you already spent weeks grinding for. It's a time-sink in every sense of the term, and it's not enjoyable in that respect.
A good game hindered by greedy developers and the micro-transaction business model designed to keep players playing for as long as possible.

Oh Warframe, what could I do with you...
I have no clue on what my stance on this game is. On one hand, it's a really fun thirdperson shooter with cool game mechanics, decent story and really fun quests.
On the other hand, you have a boring grindfest just to get that one last blueprint that you were so desperatly searching for and you end up really wasting your time unless you know what you're doing so precisely to the pinical point of punctuation.
I've put a decent amount of hours into the game because my friends got me addicted for about a week or two. After that time period, however, the game just got stale to me. I didn't care much for the story, getting good weapons is a bit difficult, and if you tell me that you liked the ending to the Second Dream Quest, you're lying.
I don't like calling games "Pay to Win", even when they are, but damn it this is really pay to win. Not something as bad like World of Guns where you literally couldn't play the game without paying even though the game says it's free. But it does get on my nerves that if I want to get new colors for my Warframe, I have to pay 5 whole dollars. Now sure, that doesn't sound like much to spend, but if you take into consideration of how small something as customizing your character is, and realize that there are a lot more things that you could be purchasing in the game, it makes you wonder if it really is something "small". For example, once I reach a high "Mastery Rank" in the game, I can go to the in-game Market, get a blueprint for a weapon, and grind my way to get the crafting materials I need to make it, and then play the "waiting game" as I have to wait over a DAY for decent weapons. But there is another option. I could go to the Market, find the weapon I want, purchase it with real money, and use it right off the bat. Do you see the problem with this system? Keep in mind that 75 Platinum (the game's currency) is 5 USD and decent weapons are over 100, so you would end up paying around $10 because you wanted a new Rifle.
Alright, I'll be honest, I like this game. So much infact that it pains me to give it a "Not Recommend" on this review. But I've had enough of these "CoD like" business practices where these devs tell us that the game is finished and ready for everyone to play, but include these stupid in-game currency where you can only purchase with real money.
If there was a "Mixed" button to recommend this game, I'd do that instead. But for now, the negatives really outweigh the positives.

I can't believe how many people are giving this game a negative review because there is a paid DLC before the game has fully released. I know it doesn't make any sense but how does that make it a bad game? Yes there are bugs and issues to be fixed and lots of other stuff like that but this game is still undeniably one of the best games you can get in terms of survival games. You do realise this game gets updates virtually every god damn day to improve it and the DLC itself is actually great on its own. Now i have heard that there is some things with the DLC that SUPPOSEDLY make it P2W but that doesn't make this game a bad game.
The Point of a review is to establish an opinion on a game and help people to understand whether or not it is worth getting.
ARK Survival Evolved is a survival game with perhaps the most potential out of anything in its genre. It has great value for money and is undeniably one of the best games on steam. Before the wave of people complaining about the new DLC it was one of the most popular games on steam and probably still is.
Graphically this game is one of the best out there with outstanding graphics for a game of its magnitude which in incredible on its own though it does mean that for the best experience you might need a good graphics card.
In terms of gameplay this game is very similar to rust in terms of resources and item mechanics but is also very different altogether. The Dinosaurs are the obvious difference, each one having their own stats, shapes and sizes meant to be a realistic (well, mostly realistic) fantasy of a world where humans could control dinosaurs and build things that you wouldn't see till very recently. Each dinosaur is fun in a different way whether it be riding the big dinosaurs to prove your might or to just have a little Bird that can't do crap but is just fun to have. The building mechanics and stuff are alright and is definitely an area to be improved but you can still make a fortress that you think is perfect for you and your dinos.
Multiplayer wise this game is also very fun and lots of laughs can be had with friends which is a game which other survival games don't offer as well. In a game like Rust you'd be likely to have a laugh about blowing up someone's base whereas in this game it is as simple as throwing yourself off a yeti.
This isn't the most detailed review ever and I can't sayu that it will help all of you but the purpose of this review was to tell the people that this game is actually worth buying and that all this crap about the Paid DLC are just salty people who don't like that the devs are releasing paid DLC (which actually are fun) instead of fixing the game itself first. Needless to say the people forget the amount of updates this game gets proving that the dev team is actually hard at work to make this game better.
Rating: 9.2/10
P.S. Get over the DLC and move on

Review, part 2.
Ok, i've almost reached 100 hours.
Many things happened from my first review.
I'm updating my review to speak about a couple of aspects in particular of the game.
The first one is the Mastery Rank.
I thinks this is a very nice thing of Warframe.
Basically, even if any Warframe, weapons, etc, have a level cap of 30, the Mastery Rank is something you need to proceed, and to increase it, you need to level everyting there is to level.
Mathematically speaking, you gain points for the Mastery Rank when you level for the first time an item, be it a Warframe, weapon, etc. If you sell it, buy it again, and re-level, you do not earn points. Same thing with the missions.
In short, it's a system that forces you to experiment new content. If you do like in many of the MMORPG around, stuck forever on your favourite character and strongest equipment, you'll never go up in the game, and i really like this.
On the other side, it's a system that forces you to purchase platinum.
Having a (very) limited amount of inventory slot, that you can expand only purchasing them with platinum, it's a bit unfair. Of course you can maximise an item, and sell it to free a slot, but you'll soon realise you want to keep the stuff you level, to switch playstyle anytime you want, so you really have no other choice than purchasing slots with platinum.
Another aspect i want to discuss, is the item named "Forma"
This is a big minus of the game.
Each warframe and weapons has several slots for mods to power it up. Each slot can have a polarity, that if matched with the mod, it will half the cost of the mod.
The "Forma" item allows to add or switch polarity of a slot, to increase the strenght.
Unfortunately, when you apply it, the item will reset to level 0, and you have to re-level it every time you use it.
Of course you will NOT earn mastery point
I honestly found this as a cheap trick to force you to buy EXP Boosters for platinum

Review Part 1
I've spent around 30 hours, and i've barely scratched the surface of this game.
I want to write something about, having just grasped the basics. I will probably update it in time, but for now, hear me out.
Warframe is a Free to Play done right. It’s incredibly fun, full of content, graphically excellent and addictive.
Let's instantly answer to the most important question:
Is it a Pay to Win game?  NO
Everything can be obtained by playing without spending a single coin, through heavy (and i underline HEAVY) grinding.
To avoid grinding you can spend real money to purchased the ingame currency named "Platinum", and accelerate several processes, so, basically, it's a "Pay to Speed Up"
You begin the game choosing one of the three basic Warframes: the "Power Suit" that you wear and gives the title to the game. There are almost 30 in total, and more are coming, each one with specific abilities that you can test and change to choose the one that suits you to your playstyle. From the caster to the tank, to support, to healer, to gunslinger, to a mix of these. In time you can obtain them all and switch them for the role you need and want, without "reroll" a single character from scratch like the most famous MMORPG like World of Warcraft. Here one single account, one single character, can achieve everything, and that's a positive thing. You will never feel the need to start over for a wrong role picked up, because in time, you can have them all, without losing anything (except social life).
Each one of the Warframes equips a primary weapon (Assault Rifle, Shotgun, Sniper, Bow, Grenade Launcher etc), a secondary one (Pistol, Kunai, etc), a melee (Sword, Axe, etc, single or double), and each one of those can be upgraded with experience, mods, sentinels, augmentations, etc to power it up.
Your character lives in a personal spaceship.
In here you manage everything, from missions, to mods, to equipment, and building stuff in your personal forgery.
Warframes, weapons, etc must be built. You need to find (or buy) blueprints, gather materials, and then start building. The building process can take from few min, to 3 - 4 days. Just as EVE online, the building process goes on even if you're offline, and you can build multiple things at the same time, without putting them in a queue.
Each warframe and weapon can be levelled up by using it, so, you guess it, when you find a new weapon destined to become powerful, you need to grind it ffirst.
Reputation is present, and the factions (here called "syndacates") requires to do missions for them with their symbol placed on you. There are 6 syndacates, and they cross each other in relationships of ally/neutral/hate, so gaining on one, will make you lose rep on another one, and so on. Gaining rep makes you access to very good rewards at high levels.
To join a syndacate requires virtual money and materials, also when you need to upgrade your rank inside the syndacates. The more syndacates you join, the more resources you have to throw in.
The structure of the game is NOT an open world.
Your spaceship is the hub, and when you choose a mission, you'll instantly travel to destination in a dedicated instance.
Sorry, no free exploration of the universe.
The universe is subdivided in planets, each one with several missions (from 15 to 28), and a boss that once defeated, will drop, other than rewards, a Nav Segment to unlock a new planet to explore (there are 14), plus the Void, where you can face special missions by finding special keys during the game.
The missions can vary from killing all enemies, to survive multiple waves, to defend a particular item, to gather a certain amount of resources, to kill a target / boss, and so on.
All these missions can be faced in solo or in a team, but of course, harder missions with better rewards needs a team, and for the end game, a very well oiled one.
There are many more details that i could explain, with a lots of things to do (not last, the PVP in specific arenas), but i wanted to show the general concept to new players that meet this game for the first time.
As i said before, this is not a Pay to Win game, but a "Pay to Speed Up" game.
A lots of efforts in grinding can be skipped purchasing the in-game currency “Platinum” through real money.
With this coin, you can instantly purchase, through the market, all the stuff you normally require to gather through random drops, craft materials, and then build.
You can instantly buy the weapon/armor, without the need of blueprints and materials, and instantly rush-build an item under construction for a lesser amount of Platinum, flashing in seconds, what it usually may require days.
The balance between the grinding and the need to purchase Platinum is well studied.
There is no Paywall, but.......
The things to do (and grind) are so many, that one day, if you keep on playing, you'll feel the need of speed up things with Platinum, despite the fact that is not required.
This excessive grinding it's the true problem with Warframe. It's really a lot.
Also the fact that you need to level up every single warframe and every single weapon it's a terrible system voted to giving you the temptation to speed up things (you can buy exp boosters with Platinum of course).
Plus, the little trick to obtain a daily reward just logging into the game, and among these rewards there is a 75% discount of the platinum for 48 hours, making the speed up option, even more tempting.
So, to conclude.
Do i recommend this game? Yes. It’s truly tons of fun, graphically very well done, and it will keep you occupied for a very long time, for free. Just be ready to spend a lot of time grinding, or a lot of money to speed things up.
If you have small children playing this, do NOT associate a credit card with your steam account.
Takes some time getting used to, but it becomes fun after a while.

Do you like games where collision detection works properly, there aren't constant lag spikes and the server admins aren't smoking crack?
Then look elsewhere! But if you're looking for a game you can waste hours on only to lose everything you've been working toward, then read onward!
The ARK developers are so kind as to release paid DLC for an Early Access game. Yep, it's an early access game that's been in early access for a year and a half. They also provide constant new content updates without fixing game-breaking bugs in collision detection and construction mechanics. They also have awesome enemies called "Alpha Raptors." These enemies move so fast that the game engine can't properly keep up with it and they blink around, making it impossible to hit them or get away from one. They're an awesome way to enjoy some of the previously-mentioned losing everything you've spent hours on.
Perhaps you're the kind of person that wants doors to randomly open toward or away from you depending on the whim of the gods. Or maybe you'd like to constantly get stuck (and have no recourse other than to kill yourself, by design!)
Maybe you'd like to be unable to walk past something because its collision box goes 30% over into 'empty space.'
If these "Features" sound appealing, ARK is the game for you! Especially if you'd like these "features" to be part of a game that's supposedly "early access" so the developers can get away with not fixing issues.
If, on the other hand, you'd like to play a game that provides more joy than frustration, you might not enjoy this title.

From needing to unlock the 20 more warframes, to the dozens of weapons, sentinels, modding, trading, syndicates and missions - you wont run out of things to do too soon.
Its f2p, and as such there is a market where you can use actual money to buy weapons and frames etc. The in game credits earned via playing missions can also be used, but only for a limited number of items by comparison. For example, you could pay 200 platinum ($20 buys 370 plat atm)) for a weapon or frame, or instead use 20-100k purchasing the blueprints for them. This cannot be done with all weapons and frames at rank 1, as some of them are xp-locked - requiring more levelling up and "mastery" test to be passed. Some materials can also be purchased this way.
Keep in mind that any blueprints also require credits to complete, plus all the grinding to get all the materials that you need (some of which simply are not available early on via drops), so it is much quicker to pay real money, but far less satisfying (for me).
The community seems friendly enough as far as online games go, with plently of people looking to group up and do quests together (where the game really shines) or trade items and talk tactics.
Visually, its very good. Plently of eye candy and a nice smooth frame rate even on maxed settings (check my profile for sys specs). The audio is crisp and environmentally accurate.
I use kb + mouse for controls, and  I found them to be very fluid, although a little tricky to master without some practice. This was only a matter of probably half an hour, so nothing excessive there. The combat is fast paced and really agile. You can wall-run, slide, spin, block, deflect shots, and generally do awesome ninja stuff all whilst waving around swords, guns or anything in between.
Lets not forget the character abilities, which are unique for each frame. There use is limited by your power reserves, which can be replenished mid battle from drops, making for some strategicly mixed combat. Powers can be damage dealing, defensive, buff, or healing, with each frame having a certain style or focus on the types of powers. For example, Volt frame uses the energy in a mostly electrical sense - dealing shock bolts of lightining or creating a defensive energy barrier, super speed or electrical overload AoE.
The atmosphere works very well, fairly dark sci-fi style (dead space-esque) with plenty of unknowns and suspicious dialogue and characters going on. There's not an exessive amount of gore, but carving enimies in halves or setting them ablaze, electrocuting, freezing, shooting or bashing the hell out of enemies is certainly violent - but is on a level that works without going overboard.
There is of course, quite a lot of customisation to boot also. You can paint your space ship, choose the colour schemes inside the ship, as well as buy decorations and attachments for your frames and weapons.
I could go on but honestly I wouldnt know where to stop. All in all this is a great game, especially for a f2p.
10/10

You are a Tenno, a long-lost relic of a bygone era, frozen in stasis after defeating your enemies. There were many like you, guided and instructed by a being known as The Lotus.  You wake up, Lotus shouting in your head to get moving. You are in danger. You are alone. She will not lose another one.
Your systems surge with energy, your being and your warframe remembering how to work in concert, channeling your abilities through a tightly focused prism. You run. You jump. You fly through the air and get your target in your sights.
You're back.
-----------------
You are a space ninja, in a meaning of the word that does not resemble "ninjas" in any specific way. You operate in small cells (from 1 to 8 people), infiltrate your target area, cause undue havoc, and run swiftly for the exit.  You exemplify lightning warfare, sometimes very literally.  Ninjas are not a power fantasy. This is.
The warframe is a suit. Or is it? It's a set of abilities and durabilities specific to a a thing that has an appearance. But you, your self, seem to remain the same. Or do you?  It all blends together at the end.
The game is fast-paced and engaging. There is shooting, slashing, and setting things on fire. There are hundreds of different weapons, sidearms, and stabby-slashy things.  Enemies can evaporate in a puff of energy, bloat with microwaves, fly apart into gory chunks, or writhe on the ground, dying slowly and painfully before your eyes.
The levels are procedurally generated. There are chunks of similar terrain that are put together in novel combinations each time. That's the intent, in any case. In truth, play enough and you'll start to learn the paths, the secret stashes, and the places were enemies can be directed to die. It becomes less a marvel of design and more of a chess-board - you know where you need to go and you can take the most efficient route there.  Speed-running through levels is an art all its own.
The game is making recent strides to be friendlier to new players. It's hard. There's a tutorial, but it may not cover everything. There's a helpful community, but the vast majority are ahead of you in progress and may not want to do the early game. There's a specific set of players who self-identify as new-player guides, but you'll need some patience to find one. Finally, the game itself is full of unspoken mechanics.
There is an official forum, an unofficial sub-reddit, and a fan-maintained wiki. All are excellent resoruces, frequently visited by the development team. There are frequent videos from the very same team, giving previews, teaser, and *gasp* actually playing their own game.  There are even a few developers with a twitter presence, if you're into that sort of thing.
The biggie: Is it a Pay-to-win game? Not in my mind. There is a premium currency. It lets you buy things, including most baseline weapons and warframes. It is not required for that. This game is quite possibly one of the finest F2P monetization models that exist.  Here's a sampling:
-Login rewards to encourage you to come back every day include 25%, 50%, and 75% discounts on all premium currency purchases.
-All weapons and warframes that can be acquired in-game can be acquired by buying a blueprint and constructing it yourself with in-game resources.
-Some of the most powerful items in-game can only be acquired by playing the game (read: farming for a while).
-There is a lively trading market between players that enables someone with a valued in-game object to trade it for platinum. YOU MAY GET PLATINUM WITHOUT PAYING REAL MONEY FOR IT.
-The vast majority of the player's power is not in the weapons, but in "mods"; little in-game cards that improve your gear. These are far more available from playing the game (or trading for them) than buying them outright.
There are only two things that require premium currency: inventory slots and cosmetic items. Slots are used to store your vast and awesome arsenal. Cosmetic items allow customization of many, many parts of your "space ninja."  Spend your platinum on nothing but slots and cosmetics and you'll find a little goes a very long way.

I find it staggering and depressing that Ark, one of the best games of its genre ever made, now actually has a 'mixed' rating on steam - almost exclusively without any reference to the game itself but simply because the company has released a piece of DLC before the game is 'finished'. To all intents and purposes ARK IS FINISHED. It offers a phenomenal game experience unlike any other you can find. When I first saw the trailers I didn't believe it could ever live up to expectations - and yet it far exceeded them. Ark allows you to explore a vast and beautiful world of prehistoric creatures, and with solid multiplayer support so that you can work with friends to utilize the construction mechanics that keeps the game compulsive even after the 'wow factor' of its breathtaking visuals has worn off. But Ark achieves even more than that, as it has been so meticulously balanced and thought through that it plays almost like an MMO on some of the bigger servers.
I have had so many hours of fun on this game, and it has already topped the most I've played of any game on steam, including many triple A 'finished' releases. Ark is far more developed than many games that are put on the shop shelves, yet rather than calling it a day and 'releasing' the game so that they could charge the premium price it deserves, the developer continues to offer a constant stream of fantastic new content for FREE. There are substantial updates pretty much every day, and these are not to fix broken features (because the game is very stable) - these are content updates, each time with some exciting new dinosaur, engram, biome or even whole new maps. Compare that to a game like DayZ, which has a significant new update about once every 2 years, despite having made millions from early access.
I'm reading a lot of hate about the new DLC (Scorched Earth) simply due to the fact it has been released 'before Ark is out of early access'. Would these reviewers have been happy if Wildcard had declared the game finished six months ago and started charging $5 for every new dinosaur or engram they've currently been giving out for free? Because a lot of other companies would have done that, and to be honest they would not have been unjustified, given how Ark has been a fully playable experience for a long time now.
It is disappointing and sad to see so many spoiled and entitled gamers who have no concept of how much work and money goes into developing a product like this - people who will vote a fantastic game down and damage its success just because they feel they deserve a limitless stream of free content. People like that are as bad as developers who employ day-one DLC and abuse early access to shaft gamers. The player review system is there to protect us from shoddy, money-grabbing opportunistic developers who think they can sell a vision and then drag their feet for years and never bother achieving it, but Wildcard are nothing like that. What's needed is a balance, and Wildcard have got it bang on in my opinion. Ark is a shining example of how to do Early Access right.

First of all, let me make this clear: I am still considered new by most people who play this game. Even though at the time of writing this I have 40+ hours, I am only at Mastery rank 3 (max is 30). I have yet to experience the entirety of this game, but I have enough experience to give a review.
So is this game fun? Yes. Do I recommend it? ...sort of. For new people, it may be hard to get into.
The introduction to this game is a weird one in my opinion. You get to choose a Warframe (sort of like a class) and the first time you are introduced to combat, you have no weapons. You can only use your Warframe ability. As time goes on, you are given the option to choose your starting melee, secondary. and primary weapons (in that order, if I remember correctly) and fight with them. These weapons will get you through a couple of levels, then they start to become more and more obsolete, making you get a weapon from the Market. The game doesn't explain a whole lot after that, so it's up to you to figure out the rest.
The gameplay is very fast-paced, with the option for stealth if you're in that mood. It's very much a run-and-gun, hack-and-slash sort of game. But you can wall-run, slide, do flips, rolls, and back-hand springs. Once you pull off a wall-run jump mid-air kill with a machine gun, you'll be sold. And the best part: playing solo is always an option. If you're not the type of person to play co-op unless absolutely necessary, you can just play solo. There's a whole bunch of different mission types, such as Defense, Exterminate (kill everyone), Interception (capture the point, impossible to do solo), Sabotage (get to a thing and blow it up), and more.
The only thing I don't like about this game is the grind. I took a long break from this game because I had to grind to get to the grind. Of course there's the option to pay your way past the grind, but you don't have to. Once you get past the initial boredom of doing the same thing over and over, things really start to open up. And you can get almost everything for free; you just need to grind for it.
For new players who have never seen gameplay of this, you WILL be overwhelmed, no exceptions. There's so much stuff that you can do, with no good explanation to things. So I'll give you guys some advice: check the Training things on the Codex. These will help you understand some concepts that will definitely be useful to you, so read them. Secondly, if your starting weapon just isn't powerful enough, get the Braton machine gun from the Market. It's one of the few weapons directly purchaseable from the market with easy-to-get ingame currency, and it'll carry you through until you can make your own new weapon. Third, co-op is not your enemy. If you have trouble on a mission, join a public game. Even if one person kills everyone, you still get some experience and you can pick up the loot. Last but not least, don't be afarid to ask for help on the region chat. Most people in the Region chat will always be willing to answer your questions, no matter how nooby it may be (in the case of US East, anyway. Apparently the chat on console versions isn't great at all).
Overall, this game is very very fun once you get past the initial grind. You can put tons of hours into this game if you want to.

I would give this game a fair 7.8/10. It comes with it's flaws, but it's free.
So, what is Warframe?
It's a squad-based third person shooter with rpg elements. Or at least, that's what I would call it.
You pick a Warframe, primary, secondary and melee weapon and hop into the fray alone or with a squad of up to 4 people.
Each Warframe has a set of four different abilities, different armor, health and shield values and fulfills a certain role.
Here we come to the little balance issue I had with Warframe... certain frames are just plain better than others, prime example being a Nyx's Chaos just not being able to hold up with a Loki's Irradiated Disarm, despite them being very similar abilities.
Apart from the balance issue... the game is a massive grindfest at times, from making you run certain missions 3-5 times for a reward to having you sit in a survival mission for 20 minutes for a randomised item drop or waiting 12-72 hours for an item to be completely built. It's certainly a great game, and it is free... but it suffers a bit due to repetitive gameplay.
Is it pay to win though? No, definetely not. Paying will simply reduce the time you spend farming for items or give you certain cosmetic upgrades.

An extremely well polished, sleek, sexy third person shooter/hack-n-slash where you take control of a space ninja.
Warframe will see you rise from your slumber, at the behest of some broad wearing an impractical visor, who will promptly start telling you what to do, where to go, and how to do it. She will provide such riveting input as "It's the Grineer!" and "Doors sealed." and who could forget the classic: "Why do you spend so much time playing that game?". From there, you galavant around the solar system slaughtering thousands and doing physically impossible things like:
- Operating around Mercury, a planet so close to the sun the average temperature is about 400 degrees.
- Traversing a plane of existence populated only by mind-controlled techno-zombies.
- Getting the last piece of Rhino Prime.
Warframe likes to build itself up as a complex and lore-rich game filled with boatloads of content and a tight combat system.
Unfortunately, what it actually is is a more technologically sophisticated version of Farming Simulator. You want that fabulous looking gun from the market? Well get your wallet out because this game will suck you dry like a vampiric ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. If you don't like spending extortionate amounts of disposable income on a FREE TO PLAY GAME, then tighten your belt, grab your pillow and get ready to play the captivating, soul-crushing experience that is Warframe.
The game's general gameplay is a fun blend of shooting and slashing. Your character carries both ranged and melee weapons, as well as using a set of abilities that come with whichever "Warframe"(Class) you choose. These weapons can range from pistols, to rocket launchers, to flamethrowers, to a gun that literally shoots rubix cubes. The variety of these weapons is a major selling point of the game. As it stands right now, there are dozens of weapons to choose from, as well as a great deal of "classes", most of which are well thought out and interesting. Some of which make you question the whole "space ninja" ideal (really? A water frame?).
When you first get into Warframe, you'll see all this content, the lovely graphics, the polished sound design and fluid combat and think "All of this is free to play?! Hot damn that's amazing!".
Sadly, this is what most people think before they begin to understand DE's business model.
Warframe is a game about grinding. You perform the same missions ad nauseum for the sole purpose of levelling up your weapons/classes, and gathering materials that have a mercilessly low drop rate. If you've played World of Warcraft, you know the feeling of running the same boss again and again and having it not drop what you want. That concept is applied to this entire game. You will grind. Forever. I've played for over 850 hours and I only just got every warframe and about 80% of the weapons.
It's a structure of loot-tables and abysmal drop rates designed to stretch the game's overall playing time to the longest possible length. It teases the player with what they could accomplish, and then forces them to spend entire days playing for a single item, only to hit them with hurdle after hurdle.
You want to get a new Warframe (class)?
Here's what you need to do:
- Play the game until you unlock the planet's final boss.
- Grind the boss, many of which feature invincibility phases and can take up to 5 minutes to kill each time even with a full team of players.
- Pray to whatever gods you believe in that 1 of 3 "parts" drop.
- Run the boss again and again for the other 2.
- Build each 'part' of the frame, each of which costs even more resources, credits, and literally 12 hours of real-world time.
- Buy the 'blueprint' from the marketplace, which is often extremely costly for newer players.
- Use your parts to fashion the final Warframe, which will take, and I'm not kidding, THREE DAYS TO BUILD.
Remember raid lock-outs from WoW? That concept where if you kill a boss you have to wait a whole week until you can kill it again? The same thing exists in this game, but in a different form. You will spend most of your time in Warframe waiting for things to happen. You will wait for weapons/warframes to build. You will wait for the (entirely randomised) alerts to pop up with something good. You will wait for something interesting to happen. It's like if someone made Stormwind into a full game.
Every now and then, the developers will throw out an event, these are usually half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ completely rigged against the player, extremely poorly thought-out, rampant with bugs, and a massive waste of time. But they'll make you feel forced to play the terrible content by granting players that force themelves to endure it a big shiny one-of-a-kind weapon. And it often isn't worth the trouble.
The story isn't much to write home about. You wake up from stasis and find yourself in the middle of a warzone between clones, zombies and jews. From there you stab and slash your way to victory. Victory isn't actually in the game yet though, so you might want to set your sights a bit lower first. Maybe try getting Volt Prime, I dunno.
Warframe is a good game. I would even say a great game. It's just dragged down by developers that don't understand how to balance or handle the game they've created. It's a restrictive, neutured experience which constantly keeps players on the edge. A nefarious business model based entirely around the carrot-on-a-stick method.
If you don't mind grinding, if you have friends that already play this, if you don't mind developers consistently wrecking the game every patch and if you have a great deal of podcasts you need to catch up on, then I would recommend Warframe.
If you want a game that will grant progression based on how much time and effort you put into it, then I would not. The game will slam you with real-life time restraints and force you to wait days for content you already spent weeks grinding for. It's a time-sink in every sense of the term, and it's not enjoyable in that respect.
A good game hindered by greedy developers and the micro-transaction business model designed to keep players playing for as long as possible.

ARK is without a doubt the most feature complete dinosaur game out there, even considering it's early access status.
A large selection of dinosaurs and prehistoric mammals to tame is the key feature of the game, and what sets it apart from many other sandbox survival games. But it doesn't skimp in the usual departments, the building system is very expansive at this time, and while the building on an advanced level can be a little fiddly, It allows a large degree of freedom in how you design your bases and outposts.
If your looking into this game for PVE purposes, then there is hundreds of hours of content involved in getting the perfect base setup, hatching and raising quality dinosaurs, and conquering the harder challenges of the game, including large boss fights, caves with difficult terrain and enemies, and the ever present threats of the weather and alpha dinosaurs.
If your looking into it for PvP, That is where ark truly shines in my opinion. The mix of dinosaurs combined with technology leads to a very unique style of pvp, similiar to rust but with far more options at ones disposal.
There are some balance issues, you need a pretty good computer to run it at any sort of decent quality, and there is still a lot of content still in the works for the game, and there is 1 dlc out already even though it has not yet released. Plenty of reviews touch on that subject.
But beyond it's teething issues as ARK reaches that point in early access where it starts preparing for a release, it is a very large and impressive game, boasting huge landcapes and a lot of options for gameplay, you'd be hard pressed to find someone that couldn't find an enjoyable activity to take part in with all the myriad things there is to do in ARK.
And if you ever find the game is becoming too much of a grind, hosting your own server or searching for one of the thousands already being hosted will allow you to find a server to play on that has just the right amount of tweaked values and mods for you.
