The Bottom line is The Company Wildcard does not care about it's customers at all.
My Experience with Ark:
I played 2000 hours of Ark -
The glitches and bugs in this game are astronomical.  Easy fixes for most developers are completely ignored in this game.
If you play on PVE people that stop playing the game will just reset by logging in once a week for less than a minute, forever taking up space on the map.
If you play PVP people will quickly become Alpha tribe on the server and they check the map daily to make sure no smaller tribes will grow to big, if so they just destroy their bases, kill their dino's.
I played on a PVE and PVP server,  mainly on PVE.  Was very helpful on a daily basis to people on the server, had most of the highest level dino's and over 400 of them.    For the most part Ark was ok, until an update went through and all hell would break loose,  You would loose random Dinosaurs, they would just dissapear,  birds, ptera's would just fly off on every patch if they were outside when a patch was being updated, another glitch.   Resources would not respawn, etc etc
My personal issues with the game besides the glitches:
WIldcard has a ticket process in which if you have any issues in game can go to their website and put one in to wait for a response from devs/GM's of a server.   This process takes weeks to get any response and all the responses are all the same, "Sorry we are not allowed to help with this situation at this time"  ,  You have to be creative to get them to do anything like ask to talk with their boss.  They will 99.9% of the time brush you off.
On a patch, one of my tribe members lost their Quetzal, a very long baby raising.  We looked everywhere couldn't find it,  There was a glitch where dinos fell through the ground,  One week later my personal quetzal was completely missing as well as others on the server,  wildcard does nothing even though these quetzals take days to raise,  5-10 hours to tame. real time.
When Scorched Earth came out I bought the game on day 1.  Ark's reviews went to Negative within a few hours because they released an expansion for a game that was not even officially released yet.  I defended the company though.  With scorched earth came a new transfer character system which took your character to a new server to play on.   Overnight (day 2) they changed how transfers worked resulting in many people loosing their character files, which made the game prompt you to make a new character,  if you were in a tribe by yourself you lost all your dinos as response times took over 2 weeks; also your bases.  Now the GM I got GM Aeolus on server 373, decided to give me that old "sorry we cant help with your character" BS, which we are all accustomed to, not even trying at all to help me.  He would speak with me by email but there were gaps of 1-2 hours in between his responses.  When he left work he wouldnt even tell you and would just email you the next day while you sat waiting at the computer for 2 -3 hours,  so if you deal with a ticket and a GM you basically have to wait all day long, so I hope you people dont have jobs because wildcard apparently only helps those who have no life.   Anyhow it took over 2 weeks to get my character back by talking to what he called his superior. I was only helped because many MANY people lost their characters and the reviews were terrible.
One thing I Should point out is that when the reviews went to negative the Owner sent out a release about his game basically saying "whatever" to his customers and that basically they should suck it up.  Not a way to do business at all.
So a few weeks later, I have to take a business trip - come back and my base is completely deleted, along with all my other tribe members bases, an entire year of items collected gone, all the metal structures gone, the dino's were left but heres the thing our so kind of a tribe leader kicked everyone out of the tribe and kept all the dino's for himself. placing blame on random people.    So I played a game for 2000 hours, did my best to always help people and what im told is a GM came onto ARK, self invited into our tribe and deleted all of our bases that took over 8 months to build while tribe members were in game.   Sounds to me Aeolus decided to get payback for me talking to his boss to get my character fixed, unless someone else in tribe had a  GM issue.
The point is studio Wildcard developers of Ark do not care about you one bit.  They have no control over their own ticket responders nor GM's that watch over the servers.  Even though its against steam policy to release an expansion before your game is completed and of coarse people backlash, the Creator basically just complains on how his customers are wrong.   Glitches never fixed,  Incomplete game - puts out expansion, Gm's can do whatever they want and there is nothing you can do even though your in the right.
There is no reason to play this game, other developers see potential in this type of game and there will be competition very shortly.    If you are going to make a company this is the wrong way of going about things.
If you do play this game, play on a Private server, not official.

The Good:  addictive game in the same vein as minecraft but with dinosaurs.  Real feeling of accomplishment as you build a base, tame dinosaurs, and learn to create more powerful/useful items.  The fact that it can all be lost if you make a mistake - like building in an area where dinosaurs can spawn that would destory your base - gives a real sense of meaning to your choices.
The Bad:
- The lag.  Oh my gosh the lag.  Even worse, it can result in your death, the loss of your dinosaurs, and everything you've spent hours building.
- Memory leaks that can lead to the game crashing, potentially with you in mid-air on a bird which also results in you falling to your death, losing everything on you, your bird, and everything it was carrying.
- The crushing feeling you get when hours (8-24) of effort is lost because you made a single mistake.
Bottom line:  This game has been in production too long to call it early access anymore.  The bugs are inexusible.  Save your money for a better game.

First of all, let me make this clear: I am still considered new by most people who play this game. Even though at the time of writing this I have 40+ hours, I am only at Mastery rank 3 (max is 30). I have yet to experience the entirety of this game, but I have enough experience to give a review.
So is this game fun? Yes. Do I recommend it? ...sort of. For new people, it may be hard to get into.
The introduction to this game is a weird one in my opinion. You get to choose a Warframe (sort of like a class) and the first time you are introduced to combat, you have no weapons. You can only use your Warframe ability. As time goes on, you are given the option to choose your starting melee, secondary. and primary weapons (in that order, if I remember correctly) and fight with them. These weapons will get you through a couple of levels, then they start to become more and more obsolete, making you get a weapon from the Market. The game doesn't explain a whole lot after that, so it's up to you to figure out the rest.
The gameplay is very fast-paced, with the option for stealth if you're in that mood. It's very much a run-and-gun, hack-and-slash sort of game. But you can wall-run, slide, do flips, rolls, and back-hand springs. Once you pull off a wall-run jump mid-air kill with a machine gun, you'll be sold. And the best part: playing solo is always an option. If you're not the type of person to play co-op unless absolutely necessary, you can just play solo. There's a whole bunch of different mission types, such as Defense, Exterminate (kill everyone), Interception (capture the point, impossible to do solo), Sabotage (get to a thing and blow it up), and more.
The only thing I don't like about this game is the grind. I took a long break from this game because I had to grind to get to the grind. Of course there's the option to pay your way past the grind, but you don't have to. Once you get past the initial boredom of doing the same thing over and over, things really start to open up. And you can get almost everything for free; you just need to grind for it.
For new players who have never seen gameplay of this, you WILL be overwhelmed, no exceptions. There's so much stuff that you can do, with no good explanation to things. So I'll give you guys some advice: check the Training things on the Codex. These will help you understand some concepts that will definitely be useful to you, so read them. Secondly, if your starting weapon just isn't powerful enough, get the Braton machine gun from the Market. It's one of the few weapons directly purchaseable from the market with easy-to-get ingame currency, and it'll carry you through until you can make your own new weapon. Third, co-op is not your enemy. If you have trouble on a mission, join a public game. Even if one person kills everyone, you still get some experience and you can pick up the loot. Last but not least, don't be afarid to ask for help on the region chat. Most people in the Region chat will always be willing to answer your questions, no matter how nooby it may be (in the case of US East, anyway. Apparently the chat on console versions isn't great at all).
Overall, this game is very very fun once you get past the initial grind. You can put tons of hours into this game if you want to.

As the game reaches its 22nd update, the Plains of Eidolon, I think to myself; "has all of my time and money spent towards this game been worth it?"
Sure yeah I think so.
This game has provided me with hundreds of hours of content with different weapons, mod combinations, stupid laughs, fun community events and great, if buggy, content updates. The developers of this game over at Digital Extremes have done a fantastic job of providing content over several years of development, and clearly know what they're doing. Warframe being my currently second most played game on Steam currently holds a special place in my heart as it's one of the two games I've ever put this much time and effort into.
Taking the fact that I enjoy this game so much, there are a lot of problems with the game, even though I would still recommend it. Crafting times for items can range from almost instant to several days long, the RNG grinding and farming aspect of the game goes overboard sometimes and you could say that there are more plenty of bugs in the game. I'm going to spend the rest of this review speaking about how these problems can be approached mentally, however, to make the game seem less intimidating to a new player.
The long crafting times in the game may seem like a large turnoff to people, but even though that fact stands, it just gives you a new thing to look forward to every day. The theory of video games having arbitrary wait times only stands to make the player more interested in the future when they actually obtain the content that they worked so hard to get, and it pays to view it in that way. Having a positive outlook on the crafting times and looking forward to when something finishes crafting heavily diminishes the negative impact that the problem once would have had.
The RNG and grinding can be heavily dulled down through game mechanics and having friends to play with can help as well. It's noteworthy too that reaching out to players online can help, since the game has a community that's filled to the brim of players who have been playing for years, myself included, who would like nothing more to help new players find their way in the game. The inclusion of certain ingame mechanics like the Warframe Nekros' desecrate, which increases item drops, helps immensely with things like this, or you could always trade for the items you need.
On the topic of bugs and glitches, no game is necessarily perfect in this department. Many games that are considered the best in their fields are filled with glitches and exploits that some would consider the best features of the game. Some game developers have even been cited as keeping glitches in their games as a way to keep the game more interesting and fun. Bugs and exploits adds a community aspect where dozens of people attempt to find things that nobody else has found before, which inadvertantly adds another layer of depth to the gameplay.
These are the problems I found most troubling throughout my entire experience, but I've learned to cope with them and enjoy the game as I'd like to see it. If you're on the fence of wether or not you want to play this game, give it a shot. Who knows, you may just enjoy it.

I've seen an awful lot of complaints here about ARK being in Early Access and having DLC.
Allow me to tell you why this isn't an issue and that it's fine for there to be DLC.
Firstly, the core game has been in development for some time. This isn't just getting the game to work, this is patching in fixes & releasing new content continuously over an extended period of time. These people worked hard.
Secondly, if it wasn't labelled as early access, nobody would know or care. You could play Ark from day one of it's release on steam and although it'd have had a couple of glitches and need a bit of polish, no one would complain. It was a fully functioning and fun game and continues to be so.
Thirdly, support for the core game hasn't been completely dropped. Servers are still up, patches are still coming in and there is new content being released as well.
Honestly, I don't see where the problem is. It doesn't feel like the core game has suffered for having DLC. I can understand there being some disappointment that not everything new is going to be free but I really like the idea of adding a new biome and I think it's fresh and different enough to be justifiably chargeable under these circumstances. It's also not that expensive. Just enjoy ARK for what it is! A really good survival game with RPG elements and FREAKING DINOSAURS! What isn't there to love?

The best free-to-play game on steam. It's really grindy, be warned. Like, the entire game is a grind. That's what the game is meant to be, it appeals to people who love to grind, to work hard for their rewards, like me.
You can purchase the premium currency, Platinum, to get things quicker, but all weapons and Warframes can be acquired without it, and relatively easily, too. The only items that REQUIRE you to spend money on platinum are cosmetic items, with no actual benefit other than looking good. There is an Arcane system that allows you to add buffs to cosmetic items, but it's not even close to bringing this game down to the "pay to win" category.
Warframe, despite being FREE TO PLAY, has a very immersive and interesting storyline, great, memorable characters, and excellent world design that really allows you to feel in control.
The best thing about the game, however, is DEFINITELY the gameplay. It's really unique, you won't find it anywhere else. I suppose the SIMPLEST way to explain it to someone who's never tried the game would be "Metal Gear Rising meets Mirror's Edge". Warframe's tagline used to be "Ninjas Play Free", which sounds cringy. Cringy or not, this game really DOES make you feel like a ninja. The game can be extremely fast-paced, but it's not overwhelming at all. My reflexes are extremely poor, yet I do somewhat well in this game, I'd say. It lets you feel like a total badass, and you can flee from any fight at will if you're good enough with the controls, and are using a fast enough Warframe. That being said, it's a very challenging game once you get past the earlier levels.
I don't have friends, but I used to, and when I did, this game is a heeeell of a lot better with them. Trust me. Co-op in this game is icing on the amazing cake. Playing solo is fine, too, though! Just make sure you don't choose a Warframe oriented for team use.
I'd give this game an 8.5/10.

This game is easily one of my favourites ever to play through Steam.
It is a lobby-based online third-person shooter with a dabbling into stealth where the story is you're of a race called the Tenno and you are out of stasis/cryosleep/whatever, saved by your mysterious leader the Lotus.  You wear warframes, body armour that grants you special powers.  You were the cold, silent, shining warriors of the Orokin, "gods" of an old time passed which ended with a great war.
It is who knows how long later, you have an . . . interesting cephalon (artificial intelligence) in a stealth ship and you go around the Sol/Origin system doing all sorts of ninja-like missions with other space ninja.  Eventually you get access to more suits and weapons, and even take to space itself in the Archwing.
What this game does incredibly well is the following:
- It is hard to play as a space ninja in space and not "feel like a boss".
- No ninjaing!  All drops are given to everyone (with the exception of the occasional random modifications from special containers in a few hidden places).  All bosses drop the same gear for everyone any one time they're killed.  Despite being a game about space ninja, you cannot have someone ninja your gear.  It's wonderful.
- Grey morality.  Are you even the good guys?  Who are?  Why?  How?
- Story and mystery.  I love the fact how you still don't know so much, including but not limited to, what the Orokin are like at all, why the Stalker hunts you down stating you killed the Orokin, why your cephalon worries it deleted all the memories and sabotaged the ship, why Warframes have genders (as if originally they were tailor made to Tenno), how Valkyr, one particular warframe, was affected by experiments and grew into a creature of rage as if it is a symbiotic lifeform, how the infinitely cloned, deteriorating, armour-focused Grineer, the biological hivemind monstrosities and toxin-based Infested, or the technology/energy/shield/financially-based Corpus all came about, or really anything concrete.
- You can choose to do everything solo, include friends only, just invites, or include anyone.  People can join and leave games as they like (though leaving costs you everything but the experience and I think the credits you grab).
- Anyone can resurrect anyone else at any time, you just have to do it within twenty seconds of the "death" of the other player.  And it takes time in which you can be shot.
- Options.  Oh, the options.  You have options for the colours of each warframe (23 varieties exist, some with upgraded Prime varieties, all of which have specialities, from the limbo plane to electricity, from death to gunfighting, from assassinry to sound, from illusion to tactics, from swordplay to antimatter), each weapon (at least seventy primaries, sixty secondaries, a whole slew of melees, including whips, staves, swords (single, double, w/ dagger, w/ shield, katana, two-handers), fist weapons, polearms, tonfas, even gunblades and claws), each sentinel (a robot of which there are seven or so), your ship.  There are badges and sigils to put on your warframe.  Even helmets for the frames.  And that's just the COSMETIC.  There are many weapons to choose from and often the best choice comes down to how it's modded, playstyle, and aesthetics.  I love how you're not pigeonholed into a specific playstyle at all.  You install mechanics mods onto each warframe, each weapon, each sentinel.
- Each element/damage type has its own point and is effective in its own right.  This kind of fits into options, but I want to extol this a moment.  Also, each creature has weaknesses and strengths to different ones based on its composition.  There are thirteen types of damage.  Physical (which is divided up into Piercing, Impact, and Slashing), the Primary or Simple Elements (Heat, Cold, Electricity, Toxin) and the Secondary or Compounded Elements (Blast, Radiation, Gas, Magnetic, Viral, and Corrosive).  If you ever have two impaired elements on a weapon, it autocompounds.  Each also has an effect that it sometimes causes.  Corrosive lowers armour permanently.  Blast knocks down.  Toxin and Slashing do damage directly (toxin doing more but slashing bypassing armour) to health if non-machine, and so on.
- All Clans are tiered by the number of members in it.  All research and clan-based items have a multiplier based on that tier.  Thus, smaller clans need less and bigger need more.  This makes having a small clan not crazy and having a large clan of mostly inactive people ridiculous; both good things.
- The game runs rather well, even in borderless.
- The having so many factions, and even factions within factions.
- Details.  So much detail and little addons that mean nothing to most but is appreciated by those who are detail-oriented.  The voice work alone!  You can shoot out windows of a spaceship and lockdown a room until you hack the security windows down.  During this time, your shields and then health will be slowly drained as you don't have life support.  Rooms later on and failed survival missions just don't have life support.  The sound gets all muffled and subdued, and it sounds like you're underwater.
Here are some things I don't particularly like about it:
- Grinding.  Like any online game, there is a lot of grinding to get that one piece you need/want.  Some pieces I have never gotten.  Also, the game gives you Mastery which is based on the highest level you've achieved with every weapon.  This is fun and forces you to
- Achievements.  The higher level Steam achievements are supposed to be literally impossible (although apparently 1.4% of the game's players have them), as the maximum Mastery you have right now MIGHT get you to twenty (Silver Tiger).
- Affinity/XP is object-specific, not player-specific.  If you get rid of a weapon, sentinel, or warframe, and then you reacquire it, you must relevel it to max.  Last I heard, it did cost you only half the experience after the first time, but ow, still.  But it makes the weapon/warframe slots so much more of a hindrance.  Also, because some weapons are building components for higher weapons, ugh.
- Microtransactions.  The game does try to get you to spend money.  Now, I know the game is free-to-play and I have legitimately dropped money on this game, but the amount for some things is silly.  Such as rushing anything, or the price for colour palettes.  They give out colour palettes freely during holidays and some events.  I have one for Easter, Halloween, and Valentines, I believe.  As well as the Gamma.  All free.  It just feels pushed a little more than it needs to.  It's not in your face about it, at least.
- Trading.  It needs a better trading system that isn't just a channel and then hobbling to a clan dojo and then paying in-game funds for the privilege.
- Grineer armour scaling.  The Grineer armour levels to ridiculous points.  It makes Corrosive damage almost necessary.
- Figuring out bosses.  Some of the bosses will require some research to figure out, but they've gotten a lot better at "telegraphing".
- Mission spontaneity lack.  There are times missions will be modified in the midst of it, but this is rather rare and more often than not scripted and more of it would mix things up a lot.
- Mission type difficulty.  Mobile defense, defense, and interception are very difficult if not impossible alone especially at harder areas.  Maybe that's the point.

There are very few games that have held my attention for 1,000+ hours over the years, this is one of them. I created an account back when the game was still in Alpha (late 2012), back then it was was just a simple module with some enemies to kill with a handful of warframes to choose from. Even then though it showed promise. Over time they have added tons of content, new warframes, weapons galore, new planets, mission types, Archwing (fly in space!), events, clan dojos and foundry, player to player trading system, syndicates to join, player HUBs (relay stations), PVP, 8 player Raid etc etc. If you enjoy third person shooters, 4 player coop, pvp, raiding, RPG's and/or ninjas in space (lol) this game is a dream come true then for you. Being that it is free to play there is literally nothing to lose checking it out.
The game is a constant work in progress and the developer Digital Extremes (DE) is constantly tweaking and adding new content all the time. Warframe has a very decent crafting system and you will most likely find yourself trying many different warframes/weapons combinations to see which one(s) fit your style the best. Believe me the game encourages you to do so, it is surprising the amount of variety in the game. When you find something you like it is a rewarding feeling and you will too it is just a matter of time. Also decent customization for your warframes, weapons, Sentinels (companion), Kubrows (dog companion), Liset (your ship), with a multitude of color choices, skins and attachments.
Every Warframe has its own set of individual abilities, they all have a total of 4. Some are better at being tanky, dps, sneaking (cloaking), solo play, healers, AOE damage, defense etc. There is a Warframe for every situation it seems. You can also make your own builds for each frame based on what mods you have (you attain them while playing missions they are dropped by enemies) For example "Continuity" mod allows for longer power duration time, when you ability is activated. More ammo, damage mods etc etc sooooo many. Making building your perfect Warframe/weapons very flexible and enjoyable. You have the opportunity to have a Primary, secondary and melee weapon. With the opportunity to make your own builds for everything here adds to the games replayability imo. Same goes for sentinels and kubrow companions they all have their own set of mods, especially made for them.
That being said the game can be very grindy, especially for newer players. That is to be expected though being that it is an MMOish experience. Especially to gather enough resources and credits to craft your items. Well worth it though if you have the time to invest. Sometimes they seem to nerf warframes and weapons for no reason at all and then they rework it again and "fix" it. Nerf/Un-nerf is the nature of free to play MMO' ish kind of games. (Constant "balance" tweaking) This is not an instant gratification game either, the game gets better the more you play it. You can also purchase items with real money from the in game market, it is
necessary though. Most things can be attained just playing the game gathering resources and crafting them accordingly. Except, of course vanity items, skins, unique color palettes and limited time only items that have been available over the course of the game.
DE sometimes gifts players new color palettes and send them to your inbox (valentine's day, halloween, St. Patrick's day etc.) Free weapons too, they seem to do somethings special on the games anniversary every year. The developer also listens to community feedback and designs and have added many things based on that. Which is always a plus. The game can also get repetitive at times, but with the amount of content in game now that is harder to happen. You just have to mix it up from time to time and try new things within the game.
All in all the future looks bright for this game. A Developer that actually listens to community feedback. Constant updates/hotfixes. Plus there is so much new content coming soon! Game is not perfect of course, but what game truly is right. There is a lot to enjoy here and unique setting and premise to the game, definitely sets itself apart from the competition.

You're reading my review on this game to possibly make a decision to get it aren't you? You probably read many others too. Well. Get this game. Play with people. This game has one of the most addicting Grinding and Trading features of any game i have ever played. Buy some plat to support the Devs as they (IMO) are some of the best currently out there that Genuinely listen and pay attention to their community and what the players want, and also learn to trade. It's trading system is easily one of the best i have seen. It can definitely Rival TF2's Trading mechanics. At first it's very fun, graphics are quite spectactular for a free to play. And if you get bored in the beginning, search up or ask friends or in the Chat (Regions Chat) how to get whatever warframe you want. Some are hard to get. Most of them is just killing a boss a few times and then wait for it to build. Grinding cannot be more fun for some reason. The Devs are nowhere even close to abandoning this game. Currently that is. They are some of the coolest Devs out there. They're currently making  New Warframes, Weapons, Items, Misc, and Pets for you to do mission with and take care of.
Tips:
If you are gonna get a pet like a Kubrow (Dogs in this game) Make sure you're going to log on everyday to take care of them. They will die if you don't see them after 10 or so days.
Do not use your starting Plat on anything until you learn the basics of the game. You can buy prime Warframe sets (Anything prime is alot better than its original counter part) like Rhino P or Mag P (prime)
WTB = Want to Buy
WTS = Want to Sell
WTT = Want to Trade (for/this for that/this)
PC = Price Check (for seeing how much Plat an Item is)
P - Plat - Platinum - Prime. In game currency that you can only Buy or trade to get.
BP - Blue Prints -What you need to put together all the parts you got for a Weapon/Warframe
Regions Chat: Pretty much Global chat. Nothing much about it. The people there are usually very nice and helpful. Sometimes people won't respond to some things you ask for some reason. But i haven't met anyone obnoxious or toxic. Trolls exist but they're not really bad. Usually funny rather than annoying.
Recruiting Chat: For  joining up with other people to play missions or join a clan. Do NOT put WTB/WTS/WTT in it. You
will be banned from that chat for a few minutes. If you continuously do it you will possibly get banned for longer and longer and eventually get perma banned from that chat or more. But trust me. I doubt that the system would do that. You're Fine.
Trading Chat/Tab is for what it says to be. Trading. Don't do anything other than trade in there like asking for help or questions. You will usually get banned for a few minutes in that chat. Trading Only.

The draw backs of this game are few but they include: some really long grinds, repetitive game-play, and a premium pay to grind-less scheme. That being said the game is truly fun and is a free-to-play so premium grind-less is something that should be obvious.
The one note I will mention, which has been the main driving factor for me and my friends slowing off this game is the constant repetitive game-play that has diminishing returns. That coupled by the fact that items in-game that contribute to your overall level and progression (mastery), are often having the ability to attain them removed from the game. Which in my mind is contributing to permanent player inequality. The mere fact that I cannot receive an item that would contribute to my overall level in the community because: I either wasn't playing when it was introduced, or missed the opportunity to receive it; greatly hinders my will to proceed further based on the merit of completion. Some may not have a problem with this but others certainly do. Certain practices I don't quite agree with also include the prime access packs. Mainly in the area of pricing.
So to put it bluntly this is an overly adequate game for your time, if you so wish to play it. There are things that after playing for a while you may realize you don't like, but to each his own. Live long and kill the masses.

I don't think I'm the kind of person this game is made for.  I had some fun playing with my friends, but after nearly 30 hours of play, the rewards do not justify the time I put into this game.  First off, do not play this game without friends.  Playing in a tribe is the only way you will actually get anything cool done, especially if you are playing in an official server.  All that's because this game isn't meant to be a walk in the park.  Sure, it's easy to get started--building a hut, taming raptors, establishing a sustainable food supply--but if you want to get into the actual meat of the game (and anywhere past the starting beach), you're going to need all the help you can get and a lot of patience.  Nothing gets completed quickly in this game.  Everything you build and every dino you tame requires a lot of resources, and harvesting them is very tedious. Perhaps that's meant to be realistic, but come on.  This is a game where you can ride dinosaurs and build massive stone citadels on a 10 ft x 10 ft raft.  It's far from realistic.  My main complaint from all that is it takes way too long to get to anything fun.  The game is also glitchy as hell and poorly optimized.  Don't download the Primitive+ DLC unless you want to increase your load times by 5000% (that's not an exageration, I think this game loads the whole map+mods into ram, which takes over 10 mins to do at times, making it a major resource hog).   Also, I recommend playing this game on a private server if you can.  There's a lot of grief from randos on the public servers, and you're vulnerable to attacks from them, even after you log off.  All the work I put into building a small base in the few hours I played in the public servers were in vain, because it's all been knocked down.  Private servers prevent that from happenning, but setting one up is just as hard as playing the game.  Expect to be troubleshooting for hours, if not days, if you want to go that route.
This game is really enticing with its promises of taming dinos and surviving in a video game version of "Jurrasic Park."  It delivers on some fronts, and I've seen a lot of videos of people doing amazing things in this game, but either they have a lot more patience than I do, or they've been exploiting something I never found.  If I continue at the rate I'm going, I've got a long way to go before I'm actually able to safely explore any of the other biomes outside of the beachy one in the south, and I don't think I have the patience for that.

As the game reaches its 22nd update, the Plains of Eidolon, I think to myself; "has all of my time and money spent towards this game been worth it?"
Sure yeah I think so.
This game has provided me with hundreds of hours of content with different weapons, mod combinations, stupid laughs, fun community events and great, if buggy, content updates. The developers of this game over at Digital Extremes have done a fantastic job of providing content over several years of development, and clearly know what they're doing. Warframe being my currently second most played game on Steam currently holds a special place in my heart as it's one of the two games I've ever put this much time and effort into.
Taking the fact that I enjoy this game so much, there are a lot of problems with the game, even though I would still recommend it. Crafting times for items can range from almost instant to several days long, the RNG grinding and farming aspect of the game goes overboard sometimes and you could say that there are more plenty of bugs in the game. I'm going to spend the rest of this review speaking about how these problems can be approached mentally, however, to make the game seem less intimidating to a new player.
The long crafting times in the game may seem like a large turnoff to people, but even though that fact stands, it just gives you a new thing to look forward to every day. The theory of video games having arbitrary wait times only stands to make the player more interested in the future when they actually obtain the content that they worked so hard to get, and it pays to view it in that way. Having a positive outlook on the crafting times and looking forward to when something finishes crafting heavily diminishes the negative impact that the problem once would have had.
The RNG and grinding can be heavily dulled down through game mechanics and having friends to play with can help as well. It's noteworthy too that reaching out to players online can help, since the game has a community that's filled to the brim of players who have been playing for years, myself included, who would like nothing more to help new players find their way in the game. The inclusion of certain ingame mechanics like the Warframe Nekros' desecrate, which increases item drops, helps immensely with things like this, or you could always trade for the items you need.
On the topic of bugs and glitches, no game is necessarily perfect in this department. Many games that are considered the best in their fields are filled with glitches and exploits that some would consider the best features of the game. Some game developers have even been cited as keeping glitches in their games as a way to keep the game more interesting and fun. Bugs and exploits adds a community aspect where dozens of people attempt to find things that nobody else has found before, which inadvertantly adds another layer of depth to the gameplay.
These are the problems I found most troubling throughout my entire experience, but I've learned to cope with them and enjoy the game as I'd like to see it. If you're on the fence of wether or not you want to play this game, give it a shot. Who knows, you may just enjoy it.

The best free-to-play game on steam. It's really grindy, be warned. Like, the entire game is a grind. That's what the game is meant to be, it appeals to people who love to grind, to work hard for their rewards, like me.
You can purchase the premium currency, Platinum, to get things quicker, but all weapons and Warframes can be acquired without it, and relatively easily, too. The only items that REQUIRE you to spend money on platinum are cosmetic items, with no actual benefit other than looking good. There is an Arcane system that allows you to add buffs to cosmetic items, but it's not even close to bringing this game down to the "pay to win" category.
Warframe, despite being FREE TO PLAY, has a very immersive and interesting storyline, great, memorable characters, and excellent world design that really allows you to feel in control.
The best thing about the game, however, is DEFINITELY the gameplay. It's really unique, you won't find it anywhere else. I suppose the SIMPLEST way to explain it to someone who's never tried the game would be "Metal Gear Rising meets Mirror's Edge". Warframe's tagline used to be "Ninjas Play Free", which sounds cringy. Cringy or not, this game really DOES make you feel like a ninja. The game can be extremely fast-paced, but it's not overwhelming at all. My reflexes are extremely poor, yet I do somewhat well in this game, I'd say. It lets you feel like a total badass, and you can flee from any fight at will if you're good enough with the controls, and are using a fast enough Warframe. That being said, it's a very challenging game once you get past the earlier levels.
I don't have friends, but I used to, and when I did, this game is a heeeell of a lot better with them. Trust me. Co-op in this game is icing on the amazing cake. Playing solo is fine, too, though! Just make sure you don't choose a Warframe oriented for team use.
I'd give this game an 8.5/10.

Written:  2015/07/10
Updated:  2016/11/29
This game is easily one of my favourites ever to play through Steam.
It is a lobby-based online third-person shooter with a dabbling into stealth where the story is you're of a race called the Tenno and you are out of stasis/cryosleep/whatever, saved by your mysterious leader the Lotus.  You wear warframes, body armour that grants you special powers.  You were the cold, silent, shining warriors of the Orokin, "gods" of an old time passed which ended with a great war.
It is who knows how long later, you have an . . . interesting cephalon (artificial intelligence) in a stealth ship and you go around the Sol/Origin system doing all sorts of ninja-like missions with other space ninja.  Eventually you get access to more suits and weapons, and even take to space itself in the Archwing.
What this game does incredibly well is the following:
- It is hard to play as a space ninja in space and not "feel like a boss".
- No ninjaing!  All drops are given to everyone (with the exception of the occasional random modifications from special containers in a few hidden places).  All bosses drop the same gear for everyone any one time they're killed.  Despite being a game about space ninja, you cannot have someone ninja your gear.  It's wonderful.
- Grey morality.  Are you even the good guys?  Who are?  Why?  How?
- Story and mystery.  I love the fact how you still don't know so much, including but not limited to, what the Orokin are like at all, why the Stalker hunts you down stating you killed the Orokin, why your cephalon worries it deleted all the memories and sabotaged the ship, why Warframes have genders (as if originally they were tailor made to Tenno), how Valkyr, one particular warframe, was affected by experiments and grew into a creature of rage as if it is a symbiotic lifeform, how the infinitely cloned, deteriorating, armour-focused Grineer, the biological hivemind monstrosities and toxin-based Infested, or the technology/energy/shield/financially-based Corpus all came about, or really anything concrete.
- You can choose to do everything solo, include friends only, just invites, or include anyone.  People can join and leave games as they like (though leaving costs you everything but the experience and I think the credits you grab).
- Anyone can resurrect anyone else at any time, you just have to do it within twenty seconds of the "death" of the other player.  And it takes time in which you can be shot.
- Options.  Oh, the options.  You have options for the colours of each warframe (23 varieties exist, some with upgraded Prime varieties, all of which have specialities, from the limbo plane to electricity, from death to gunfighting, from assassinry to sound, from illusion to tactics, from swordplay to antimatter), each weapon (at least seventy primaries, sixty secondaries, a whole slew of melees, including whips, staves, swords (single, double, w/ dagger, w/ shield, katana, two-handers), fist weapons, polearms, tonfas, even gunblades and claws), each sentinel (a robot of which there are seven or so), your ship.  There are badges and sigils to put on your warframe.  Even helmets for the frames.  And that's just the COSMETIC.  There are many weapons to choose from and often the best choice comes down to how it's modded, playstyle, and aesthetics.  I love how you're not pigeonholed into a specific playstyle at all.  You install mechanics mods onto each warframe, each weapon, each sentinel.
- Each element/damage type has its own point and is effective in its own right.  This kind of fits into options, but I want to extol this a moment.  Also, each creature has weaknesses and strengths to different ones based on its composition.  There are thirteen types of damage.  Physical (which is divided up into Piercing, Impact, and Slashing), the Primary or Simple Elements (Heat, Cold, Electricity, Toxin) and the Secondary or Compounded Elements (Blast, Radiation, Gas, Magnetic, Viral, and Corrosive).  If you ever have two impaired elements on a weapon, it autocompounds.  Each also has an effect that it sometimes causes.  Corrosive lowers armour permanently.  Blast knocks down.  Toxin and Slashing do damage directly (toxin doing more but slashing bypassing armour) to health if non-machine, and so on.
- All Clans are tiered by the number of members in it.  All research and clan-based items have a multiplier based on that tier.  Thus, smaller clans need less and bigger need more.  This makes having a small clan not crazy and having a large clan of mostly inactive people ridiculous; both good things.
- The game runs rather well, even in borderless.
- The having so many factions, and even factions within factions.
- Details.  So much detail and little addons that mean nothing to most but is appreciated by those who are detail-oriented.  The voice work alone!  You can shoot out windows of a spaceship and lockdown a room until you hack the security windows down.  During this time, your shields and then health will be slowly drained as you don't have life support.  Rooms later on and failed survival missions just don't have life support.  The sound gets all muffled and subdued, and it sounds like you're underwater.
Here are some things I don't particularly like about it:
- Grinding.  Like any online game, there is a lot of grinding to get that one piece you need/want.  Some pieces I have never gotten.  Also, the game gives you Mastery which is based on the highest level you've achieved with every weapon.  This is fun and forces you to
- Achievements.  The higher level Steam achievements are supposed to be literally impossible (although apparently 1.4% of the game's players have them), as the maximum Mastery you have right now MIGHT get you to twenty (Silver Tiger).
- Affinity/XP is object-specific, not player-specific.  If you get rid of a weapon, sentinel, or warframe, and then you reacquire it, you must relevel it to max.  Last I heard, it did cost you only half the experience after the first time, but ow, still.  But it makes the weapon/warframe slots so much more of a hindrance.  Also, because some weapons are building components for higher weapons, ugh.
- Microtransactions.  The game does try to get you to spend money.  Now, I know the game is free-to-play and I have legitimately dropped money on this game, but the amount for some things is silly.  Such as rushing anything, or the price for colour palettes.  They give out colour palettes freely during holidays and some events.  I have one for Easter, Halloween, and Valentines, I believe.  As well as the Gamma.  All free.  It just feels pushed a little more than it needs to.  It's not in your face about it, at least.
- Trading.  It needs a better trading system that isn't just a channel and then hobbling to a clan dojo and then paying in-game funds for the privilege.
- Grineer armour scaling.  The Grineer armour levels to ridiculous points.  It makes Corrosive damage almost necessary.
- Figuring out bosses.  Some of the bosses will require some research to figure out, but they've gotten a lot better at "telegraphing".
- Mission spontaneity lack.  There are times missions will be modified in the midst of it, but this is rather rare and more often than not scripted and more of it would mix things up a lot.
- Mission type difficulty.  Mobile defense, defense, and interception are very difficult if not impossible alone especially at harder areas.  Maybe that's the point.

There are very few games that have held my attention for 1,000+ hours over the years, this is one of them. I created an account back when the game was still in Alpha (late 2012), back then it was was just a simple module with some enemies to kill with a handful of warframes to choose from. Even then though it showed promise. Over time they have added tons of content, new warframes, weapons galore, new planets, mission types, Archwing (fly in space!), events, clan dojos and foundry, player to player trading system, syndicates to join, player HUBs (relay stations), PVP, 8 player Raid etc etc. If you enjoy third person shooters, 4 player coop, pvp, raiding, RPG's and/or ninjas in space (lol) this game is a dream come true then for you. Being that it is free to play there is literally nothing to lose checking it out.
The game is a constant work in progress and the developer Digital Extremes (DE) is constantly tweaking and adding new content all the time. Warframe has a very decent crafting system and you will most likely find yourself trying many different warframes/weapons combinations to see which one(s) fit your style the best. Believe me the game encourages you to do so, it is surprising the amount of variety in the game. When you find something you like it is a rewarding feeling and you will too it is just a matter of time. Also decent customization for your warframes, weapons, Sentinels (companion), Kubrows (dog companion), Liset (your ship), with a multitude of color choices, skins and attachments.
Every Warframe has its own set of individual abilities, they all have a total of 4. Some are better at being tanky, dps, sneaking (cloaking), solo play, healers, AOE damage, defense etc. There is a Warframe for every situation it seems. You can also make your own builds for each frame based on what mods you have (you attain them while playing missions they are dropped by enemies) For example "Continuity" mod allows for longer power duration time, when you ability is activated. More ammo, damage mods etc etc sooooo many. Making building your perfect Warframe/weapons very flexible and enjoyable. You have the opportunity to have a Primary, secondary and melee weapon. With the opportunity to make your own builds for everything here adds to the games replayability imo. Same goes for sentinels and kubrow companions they all have their own set of mods, especially made for them.
That being said the game can be very grindy, especially for newer players. That is to be expected though being that it is an MMOish experience. Especially to gather enough resources and credits to craft your items. Well worth it though if you have the time to invest. Sometimes they seem to nerf warframes and weapons for no reason at all and then they rework it again and "fix" it. Nerf/Un-nerf is the nature of free to play MMO' ish kind of games. (Constant "balance" tweaking) This is not an instant gratification game either, the game gets better the more you play it. You can also purchase items with real money from the in game market, it is
necessary though. Most things can be attained just playing the game gathering resources and crafting them accordingly. Except, of course vanity items, skins, unique color palettes and limited time only items that have been available over the course of the game.
DE sometimes gifts players new color palettes and send them to your inbox (valentine's day, halloween, St. Patrick's day etc.) Free weapons too, they seem to do somethings special on the games anniversary every year. The developer also listens to community feedback and designs and have added many things based on that. Which is always a plus. The game can also get repetitive at times, but with the amount of content in game now that is harder to happen. You just have to mix it up from time to time and try new things within the game.
All in all the future looks bright for this game. A Developer that actually listens to community feedback. Constant updates/hotfixes. Plus there is so much new content coming soon! Game is not perfect of course, but what game truly is right. There is a lot to enjoy here and unique setting and premise to the game, definitely sets itself apart from the competition.

After witnessing alot of people hating on the new DLC, Im going to defend ARK as the game is the best open world survival game in the world. You have it all, dinosaurs, dragons, reptiles, birds, mammals, sharks, insects, etc., you name it, they have it all. This is your childhood dream in a toybox. Ever wanted to tame the legendary Tyrannosaurus? Fly in the sky on Pteranodon? Face the mighty Dragon? Swim into the sea monster infested ocean? Explore the darkest caves? This is that.
When this game first started out in June 2nd, nothing worked out right. There were only 3-10 servers up at the time for players, and nobody couldnt play online that day. Then, as weeks went by, things got smoothly better with more servers. While having a computer built back in 2013, my game didnt function that greatly with rendering issues and lag bombs/spikes. But months later, my game was more optimized for smoother gameplay on my computer. Guys, face it, your computers are like Xbox 360s and PS3s trying to play a next gen game, its just not gonna work. YOU HAVE TO ADVANCE!!! And that requires money. Sorry, but thats the stone cold truth. If you dont wanna buy a new computer to play, then stick with what you got.
I would also like to take point against all the whiny little PVPers who are upset that those who bought Scorched Earth. Is it  Pay to Win? In a sense, yes. Every pvper in their dominant alpha tribe are scared to get their base raided hard by a swarm of Wyverns. Guess what, deal with it. You didnt buy it, so say bye bye to that alpha tribe status. Also, buying the DLC would sure help ARK get more money to pool into the game's budget. And before you go saying they have plenty of money, lets remember: They arent Microsoft or Sony, so they arent chalked with millions of dollars.
But aside that, this game is LOTS of fun. Everytime you join a new server, its a whole new adventure for you and your friends, and your enemies. So go have the best fun you had taming dinosaurs and killing other players or the bosses. I know I'm having  fun. Find your fun.

What can be said about Warframe? Well a lot actually, for a small indie F2P game it is absolutley incredible. Ive logged countless hours into this game just hacking my way through hoards of enemies, jumping off walls, and flying through space just because the game is FUN.
Warframe starts you off as a lone Tenno, no weapons, just you and your chosen Warframe. Instantly you are thrusted into combat with your guide The Lotus to teach you about the power of the Warframes. Wether you are Excalibur, master of swords, Volt the commander of electricity, or Mag manipulator of enemies, all 3 starter frames are solid choices (pick Excalibur). Not to say the frame you choose is now bound to you more than that piece of gum you swallowed in 3rd grade, as you go along you can create new Warframes, each a master in his or her (yes there are lady space ninjas) field, want a Tank frame who can rush enemies with a greatsword throwing caution to the wind? Then may i suggest the brute Rhino, or our femme fatale Saryn. A high damage dealing Warframe who can wipe out an army in the blink of an eye? Then our local ASSASSINO! Ash, or the hot headed Ember! Perhaps you arent the type to get your hands dirty, why not have the enemy destroy themselves? Invade the minds of your enemies with the lovely Nyx, or manipulate the souls of both the enemy and the dead with really frickin creepy Nekros.~
Now I cant say it dosent have it flaws, yes there are some, and they are pretty glaring. The first is the most infamous. The Grind. Yes this is a free to play game, yes there are weapons to collect and pieces to gather... and yes, you will need luck on your side or a willing sacrifice. Along with the grind there is also the glaring issue of the fact that it IS still in beta. There will be bugs, there will be a lot of bugs, and they will be noticeable. Gamebreaking? Sometimes, but not all hope is lost. The team behind this game are dedicated to making it the best it can be and almost every week we see an update hit the game to squash those pests. The bugs may be there, the issues are large, true, but that dosent stop me from playing it.
Is Warframe a Pay to Win game? Quite simply... well... no. No it isnt. Nothing bought with money you cant get in the game in about 12 hours, plus you can profit from others buying the premium currency (Platinum)! Platinum can be traded amongst other players as a form of payment. Did you pick up a piece to a weapon you already have? Trade it for some Platinum! Ive played this game for a lot longer than my steam profile says i have (this game wasnt always linked with steam) and not ONCE did I ever feel that those who paid $100+ got anything better or anything special from that i didnt have. Warframe is, in my opinion, one of the FINEST examples of a Free To Play game that is not Pay To Win.
Warframe has brought to me a sense of giddyness i havent felt from a game in a long time, and i cant express how amazing i feel after sprinting through a door, sliding on one knee, taking down 3 enemies, jumping on a zipline and riding it before leaping onto a nearby wall only to take out 4 more enemies while wall-running, all in the span of 10 seconds. This game is defintley worth a try, its free so i mean come on, what do you have to lose?

The game graphics are awesome. But the amount of time consumed by this game if you are playing official PvP is insane, to the extent that one can call it unhealthy. It's no country for relaxed gaming and few hours of PvP. You must plan for a 24x7 schedule.
To me the the game and the official gaming servers were much better during the initial release. Metal, polymer, CP were rare resources which meant that people had to put more of effort in making weapons and explosives. Both making and destroying buildings was difficult, which was good for long term players who played few hours a day. Some plants were good enough to protect your base from couple of raiders.
The current version does not allow for such gameplay. Any building less than metal is basically of no use. Weapons and explosives are so cheap, that you can farm for a day with couple of your friends and go destroy bases which took weeks to make.
Life is not easy for new players who are starting a new tribe on a PvP server. There are nice players who help you start-up and there are players who will kill u for nothing. But that's the fun of PvP.
There are players who seem friendly in general on the PvP servers, but would have secondary steam accounts which they would use to raid other bases, using resources they collect from primary account. Sadly u cannot vent your anger by attacking back, since u can't trace back the original supplier, and their secondary characters (who attacked) don't have a base.
And off-course there are player killers who dun have any base, they just login to kill.
With the introduction of bola (for movement impairment) and swamp fever(which gives movement speed boost but reduces max health), there are whole bunch of players who just login to troll and kill. The fact that a lot of early stage dinos (wolves, raptors, pteras etc.) get affected by bola, means you don't have an effective countermeasure. Increased movement speed from swamp fever means they can outrun almost any land dino. This is especially effective for player killers who launch surprise attacks,
The swamp fever and bola along with club (there is no effective countermeasure for torpor effect induced by club), are blessing for player killers who don't have any base and just login to kill players.
Few suggestions if I may suggest-
Bola - The introduction of bola has made taming flying mounts-ptera and mid size dinos a lot easier as well. But frankly I liked it when we had to run behind a ptera to tranq it or escape powerful jaws of a wolf pack. Also, it seems unreal that a ptera and wolf that can carry a human, goes down to a bola thrown by single hand. They should limit its effect to humans and small dinos only.
Club -  I get it that new players should have a weapon capable of fighting established players. But the way club works seems stupid to me. There is no effective countermeasure (only riots gear (level 80) protects against club's torpor effect). You can spend points on fortitude but the torpor resistance you get is too less.
They should add other realistic measures like, additional damage on attacking a player from outside his line of site (increasing the weapon damage based in the duration attacker was incognito and proximity attained). This will encourage people to use strong tactics while attacking rather than just depending on club, plus things like ghille armor will finally have a use. It's like being an assassin, once I am behind you with a dagger on your throat, u are dead meat.
Trading - The game provides ways to secure the base while u are away like auto-turrets and stuff, but no way to trade when u are offline. I would like to see some form of offline trading option. May a trading vault that u can keep out in open, which players can use to trade or break it to steal the stuff.
Inventory - Making the inventory visible. I may be carrying a complete set of armor and a automatic rifle, but no-one can see that. Armed player (naked) lure people out of their base, pretending they need help. This is stupid - I should be able to see that he is carrying a goddamn automatic rifle and grenade launcher on his back.

I figured since this game managed to claim 500+ hours of my life I should probably give it a review.
Except I wondered if it actually needed one...
It's a free game where you get to be a flying space ninja with super powers, that alone warrants at least trying it out.
After you try it out, you quickly become enthralled in running up/along walls and discovering 1000 different ways to kill hordes of mooks in satisfyingly visceral combat, whether it be blades, bullets, arrows, explosions, acid, poison, ice, electricity, flames, magnets, lasers, other mooks, your kubrow, quasi-space magic or a flying-kick-to-the-face if you're feeling fancy.
A bit of a haze later you discover 100 hours of your life has disappeared somewhere that you can't quite recall the specifics of but have this odd desire to spend another 100 hours doing precisely the same thing.
And then it's too late.
Warframe has you.

This is the tale of a love lost, a love between a gamer and his longtime favorite game, ARK Survival Evolved. I have owned ARK Survival Evolved since Jun 16th, 2015 and in that time the game has defied its subtitle devolving greatly. At the time of this review Ark is an unplayable mess.
Somewhere between version 245.1 and the current version 247.85 I lost the ability to play ARK, now it’s worth mentioning that this game has always been something less than efficient. For the first 6-8 months of ownership the game featured brutal rubber-banding that made combat a comical game of button spam. Even in this early stage the game was playable and dare I say, stable.
This is no longer the case. The current ARK is a frozen mess that freezes the entire operating system anytime I leave the pause menu. Now I’m going to say upfront that I’m not running a Titan or i7, however my machine is well above the minimum specs. Further I routinely play Dark Souls (all of them), The Witcher 3, Dragon’s Dogma, Dragon Age: Inquisition and Warframe among other games on high settings. Not only do I play these games but I almost always play them with open browsers running Twitch and/or YouTube with no sign of diminished performance. With ARK not only can I not do this but having any program open simultaneously is impossible.
Each time I open the Steam client I am greeted by an ARK update. Each of these updates leads me to the patch notes where I routinely see the word “optimization” and I am almost always confused by this inclusion. What optimization could be happening for a game that is clearly less optimized with each content update?
What makes this most maddening is the fact that ARK offers a host of options meant to accommodate a wide range of machines, yet somehow the game bricks on even the lowest settings. Even with all the options turned off the game is unplayable. I am strangely impressed by this incompetence.
I suppose the time has come for me to provide a final verdict on the game. As it stands right now I cannot recommend ARK to anyone who doesn’t own a top of the line computer. The games optimization is a step above broken and shows no sign of improving. Even if the game goes on sale, avoid it until you can be sure it’ll run on your machine.

Being the type of gamer that has been gaming since Atari, owned a lot of consoles during the years, played all kinds of games and also managed to never stop playing as I matured (although I did calm down on the hrs a bit as life got serious, work happened and what not!), I found Warframe to be an exhilarating ride that assumingly will never end, but in the end (because it does sort of end) I had to remember this game is not meant to end as it's meant to make money for a long time by being called an open beta game.
What I mean from the above is that if you are new to Warframe now, the more you login in and do and the more you learn, the more you feel like you don't know s**t, and that will only result in one of two things. You'll give up at around Mastery Rank 7 when in the game there's technically 29 Mastery Ranks, 10 of which are not available to new players because it's impossible to rank higher without having more gear available in the game... or you will play a whole lot of hrs (and have lots of entertaining experiences) to come to find that you simply won't reach any conclusion in the game.
I know this is a lot of  what's to be expected from an Open Beta game and it's fine, I played about 1000 hrs of Warframe between my account here on Steam and an account in my PS4 and those hrs were phenomenal... enjoyed playing with friends, helping out others, discussing the game mechanics, trading gear, etc... but I got left with a bit of a bad taste in my mouth because it's impossible at the moment to complete the game or get to the point where things "end" and you can continue to do more on a harder level or what not.
The above might be perfectly fine for you, and that's cool, but it wasn't for me (even though the 1000 hrs were super fun, yeah, no doubt about that!) because I was hoping to get 100% of the achievements and calling it a day. We all know these achievements are only self fulfilling rewards to pat yourself on the back or bragging rights with your other gamer buddies, but they feel good and this is why we chase to achieve them.
Let me list out a lot of what I mean by the above statements in simply unordered lists to give a broader idea of what's to like and not to like about Warframe in my opinion.
The Pros:
The Cons:
In conclusion, I do recommend the game because it has a lot of playing hrs, this game is very fun, very addictive, worth spending money on to support the developers, and definitively worth playing and exploring... but! if you're the kind of gamer, like me... who likes the feeling of beating a game and completing all challenges with achievements to go with it, then the above is probably useful to know now from the get go!
While the expressions above might seem mixed, it's still worth going through if the never-being-able-to-complete-the-game idea doesn't bother you at all.

This is the tale of a love lost, a love between a gamer and his longtime favorite game, ARK Survival Evolved. I have owned ARK Survival Evolved since Jun 16th, 2015 and in that time the game has defied its subtitle devolving greatly. At the time of this review Ark is an unplayable mess.
Somewhere between version 245.1 and the current version 247.85 I lost the ability to play ARK, now it’s worth mentioning that this game has always been something less than efficient. For the first 6-8 months of ownership the game featured brutal rubber-banding that made combat a comical game of button spam. Even in this early stage the game was playable and dare I say, stable.
This is no longer the case. The current ARK is a frozen mess that freezes the entire operating system anytime I leave the pause menu. Now I’m going to say upfront that I’m not running a Titan or i7, however my machine is well above the minimum specs. Further I routinely play Dark Souls (all of them), The Witcher 3, Dragon’s Dogma, Dragon Age: Inquisition and Warframe among other games on high settings. Not only do I play these games but I almost always play them with open browsers running Twitch and/or YouTube with no sign of diminished performance. With ARK not only can I not do this but having any program open simultaneously is impossible.
Each time I open the Steam client I am greeted by an ARK update. Each of these updates leads me to the patch notes where I routinely see the word “optimization” and I am almost always confused by this inclusion. What optimization could be happening for a game that is clearly less optimized with each content update?
What makes this most maddening is the fact that ARK offers a host of options meant to accommodate a wide range of machines, yet somehow the game bricks on even the lowest settings. Even with all the options turned off the game is unplayable. I am strangely impressed by this incompetence.
I suppose the time has come for me to provide a final verdict on the game. As it stands right now I cannot recommend ARK to anyone who doesn’t own a top of the line computer. The games optimization is a step above broken and shows no sign of improving. Even if the game goes on sale, avoid it until you can be sure it’ll run on your machine.

ARK: Survival Evolved Has progressed over time into a good survival game, I’d recommend it to anyone.
When I first bought the game the server memory leaks were so bad I could hardly login to only crash. Now to this point the game developers have corrected, fixed & continued to create a vivid world with much to experience. The game is still in the early access state so they have much to go, yet the playability is very stable even for low end computers. I say this being my box was built for AoC in 2005.
Studio Wildcard, Instinct Games, Efecto Studios, and Virtual Basement are doing a good job to update issues, what to me seems like on a daily basis, every time I login there is some new patch for some bug or issue that has been corrected. This being said it is still not a release level game, they have miles to go, but they are working hard to get there. I honestly feel the game will get there and it is worth the time to try if you are a casual gamer. It is a survival game so it is not a Monty Hall Style game, which it should not be. You got to earn what you got, your gonna die in the beginning maybe many times until you can get established but once you got your hut set up a bed to respawn too down and a storage with equipment to replace what you may have lost in the last death you will be on your way to some good old fashion game fun.
There are many Official ARK servers to choose from, you can play single player set the game as you like, you can find an Unofficial server hosted by other players to jump on and try your luck too. The options are open for you to choose from it is all up to you. The mod crafters are also hard at work creating some of the most amazing addition to ARK from baby dinos to Stupid Hats some right out of Guild Wars 2, I’d swear. You can find most of the mods listed under the workshop in steam, or just google ARK mods, all are very easy to add to the game without third party mod control apps like are needed in Fallout or Skyrim. Just remember it is not a completed game YET.
There are issues that have to be addressed but they are working to get as many as they can, I had to wait almost a year before I could log in and get to 10th lvl without crashing and being♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off. Had I paid more than I did when I first bought it I would have refunded the game within the first few hours to be honest, but they have made great strides in that time and I can see that they are going to create an even better game than it is now. I’ve waited this long I’m willing to give them some time to see what they toss out for me to discovery.  I have enjoyed the challenge up to this point, I’d bet you may to if you give them the chance. Now if you’re the give it to me player, then maybe you should stick with WoW.

What can be said about Warframe? Well a lot actually, for a small indie F2P game it is absolutley incredible. Ive logged countless hours into this game just hacking my way through hoards of enemies, jumping off walls, and flying through space just because the game is FUN.
Warframe starts you off as a lone Tenno, no weapons, just you and your chosen Warframe. Instantly you are thrusted into combat with your guide The Lotus to teach you about the power of the Warframes. Wether you are Excalibur, master of swords, Volt the commander of electricity, or Mag manipulator of enemies, all 3 starter frames are solid choices (pick Excalibur). Not to say the frame you choose is now bound to you more than that piece of gum you swallowed in 3rd grade, as you go along you can create new Warframes, each a master in his or her (yes there are lady space ninjas) field, want a Tank frame who can rush enemies with a greatsword throwing caution to the wind? Then may i suggest the brute Rhino, or our femme fatale Saryn. A high damage dealing Warframe who can wipe out an army in the blink of an eye? Then our local ASSASSINO! Ash, or the hot headed Ember! Perhaps you arent the type to get your hands dirty, why not have the enemy destroy themselves? Invade the minds of your enemies with the lovely Nyx, or manipulate the souls of both the enemy and the dead with really frickin creepy Nekros.~
Now I cant say it dosent have it flaws, yes there are some, and they are pretty glaring. The first is the most infamous. The Grind. Yes this is a free to play game, yes there are weapons to collect and pieces to gather... and yes, you will need luck on your side or a willing sacrifice. Along with the grind there is also the glaring issue of the fact that it IS still in beta. There will be bugs, there will be a lot of bugs, and they will be noticeable. Gamebreaking? Sometimes, but not all hope is lost. The team behind this game are dedicated to making it the best it can be and almost every week we see an update hit the game to squash those pests. The bugs may be there, the issues are large, true, but that dosent stop me from playing it.
Is Warframe a Pay to Win game? Quite simply... well... no. No it isnt. Nothing bought with money you cant get in the game in about 12 hours, plus you can profit from others buying the premium currency (Platinum)! Platinum can be traded amongst other players as a form of payment. Did you pick up a piece to a weapon you already have? Trade it for some Platinum! With upwards of 600+ hours in this game, having started during the winter event my first day in ark. It saddens me to see how everyone is responding to the DLC that they've come up with.
I've seen people arguing they are making the game play to win, that they are trying to milk us for every cent they can, and quite frankly this behavior saddens me.
The wildcard team has been very upfront about their goals and expansive view for the game. They've never hidden the fact that they have considered DLC in the past, they've just never been sure how to impliment it into the game well.
The system they have in place is not perfect, no. As the game IS as everyone is more than happy to say, Pre-Release. oh the cruelity that they are subjecting us all to by wanting to include console players in this massive game. I am sure having more people playing the game will cause the generally online experience that the game is to suffer for having a wider range of people playing it.
The DLC is balanced with things that have already been implimented. The OP Wyverns are only OP because you're seeing them in the scorched servers. Unofficial servers and private servers can just disallow anything being transfered to their server, while on the official servers you can only transfer things FROM the Scorched maps TOO the Island or Center maps. And if you think even a fully imprinted Wyvern level 150 egg is gonna be able to handle things like Gigas, Titans, or a moderately non-sucky defended base, Well...You're gonna have a bad time.
Yes the game is not fully optimized yet. But you know what...Its early access. They are still trying to impliment all the dinos, all the armors, all the weapons, structures, items and countless other things they have planned for the end game. No♥♥♥♥♥♥its taking them longer, especially with everyone ♥♥♥♥♥ing about how the game isn't finished yet and how they don't having to pay for something beyond what the wildcard team had already promised us.
As it currently is, Ark is a unique and wonderful experience for anyone that enjoys titles like Minecraft, Rust, but feels that there needs to be something a bit more to it. Its an experience that be just as much fun doing alone in single player as it is struggling against other tribes for dominance of a server. But know your own preferances. Do not go into a PvP server if you like building massive buildings and exploring things with freinds. Play PvP expecting to be raided on a daily basis. If you prefer the building and just exploring what you can do with the Dinos, try to find a PvE server or start a private one up with some friends.
Ark as it is now is a brutal, challenging, yet absolutely amazing game. And its going to get better. If you can tolerate dealing with bugs from time to time, then you might find the game plenty satisfying as it is now. If you can't tolerate bugs however, I would suggest tucking it away in your wishlist and waiting for the official release, because I imagine that is not terribly far off.
