I am a season pass subscriber, and I have owned Ark:Survival Evolved since day 1 of its Early Access launch on Steam.

1 - A huge amount of tameable/rideable/breedable creatures. Breeding your tamed creatures is massively rewarding and surprisingly intricate, and almost every single creature that you tame and breed serves a purpose in your collection.
2 - An impressive array of diverse biomes
3 - hundreds of recipes accompanied by an open-ended progression system
4 - huge open-world maps with several maps to choose from out of the box
5 - Jaw-dropping exploration
6 - Incredibly deep building system, made all the much better by full Workshop support and an active and engaged modding community.
7 - Amazing visuals
8 - Boatloads of gameplay elements, so it caters to many styles of play. It is genre-best by a huge margin in diversity of content.
9 - Fairly in-depth survival mechanics, including weather, disease, hunger, thirst, overheating, freezing, etc.,
10 - Best end-game content, both PvP and PvE, in the genre. There's enough here to keep you busy for several hundred, if not thousands, of hours
11 - Well supported. There has been an extremely proflific and steady steam of new content and updates since the game's launch back in Early Access.
12 - Active community with thousands of player-run servers
13 - A dizzying amount of gameplay adjustment sliders to give your single player that perfect feel for your level of engagement, and fully-customizable server options for multiplayer. You can make this game whatever you want. The amount of tweakable gameplay elements and server functions  hark back to a much more free and open time in gaming history.
1 - Bugs. This is a now fully-released AAA-priced game, and shall be judged as such. It's buggy as hell. You can expect to be infuriated by getting stuck in a stupid part of the terrain or by having a dinosaur eat you through a wall. Slide down cliffs where it looks like you should be able to land, taking complete fall damage and getting your body, and al of its loot, stuck in the side of the cliff in the process. Those are just examples of some of the glitches you will encounter. Overall, the game's fun factor and replayability outweigh these issues for me, but everyone is different and you should know what to expect.
2 - Unoptimized. Want your plastic Dell Minecraft laptop from the Best Buy hot-buy section to run this? Don't even bother. I have a GTX 1080, i7-6700k, 32gb DD4 RAM, Samsung EVO SSD, and this game is a rig-eater. No matter the resolution, it uses 98-100 percent of my graphics card. I've found the perfect settings for my machine at 2k resolution with most things on ultra or high, but you can expect to spend more-than-normal time tweaking your graphics settings for maximum prettiness. At 4k ultra, this beast of a game runs at about 8-15 (sometimes 25) FPS on my setup.
3. Toxic community in official servers. Seriously, I can't stress this enough, stay away from official servers. The official server PvE content is hindered significantly by the restrictions in place to combat griefing, and good luck ever finding an admin on official. PvP official is terrible for more reasons than I care to delve into. Just know that there are hundreds of well-supported, well-established unofficial servers that have been operating for years with active admins, and thousands of servers in general to choose from.
4 - Weak server browser. May not sound like a lot, but read above. There are thousands of player-run servers, and the in-game browser gives you very little to help you make your decision. And there are still issues joining your friends through Steam (although the browse has a friends tab, which is nice). Mods can be downloaded in-game, but are often times too large to get in a single session, and the game kicks you out after a certain amount of time with no explanation on how to fix it or why you were disconnected. It's a frustrating experience for new players trying to join servers and getting inexplicably disconnected from every server they try. Even though just continuously joining the server will eventually work, this system is laughably archaic and ineffecient. I would suggest using external server browsing websites to find the perfect server.
5 - Balancing issues. May be impossible to avoid, however it is worth noting that Ark is not balanced in the least. If you are in the end-game progression stage, you are an immortal, untouchable godslayer to any newcomer on your island. Often Studio Wildcard released unbalanced and seemingly untested content that only widened this gap. If you're buying this game for the PvP element, beware. This technology gap makes rust seem 100 percent balanced. There's nothing else like the tech gap in Ark anywhere in gaming. This makes trying to inhabit a new island, be a new player, and learn the game with others very very very difficult.
6 - Time. This game takes an unholy amount of time unless you just use facerolling, grindless settings. Default official settings can see players regularly taking many hours to tame a single creature, and as much as a week to breed a powerful creature. Not to mention the slog of thwapping trees, rocks, and other stuff with your tools for days on end.
If I were some snobby professional reviewer, I would give Ark an 8,2/10, docking it for its buggy and unoptimized state at official launch. But I'm not a professional reviewer, and I love this game. It's easily in my top-five games of all-time, and I've been alive a pretty long time (30 years). Though not for the faint of heart or easily swayed, I can whole-heartedly recommend this game.
To sum it up, Ark if f*****g awesome.

ARK is amazing. It is brutally difficult, as well as equally massive. I have had so many awesome adventures playing this game. Lots of people want to complain about the paid DLC and I do get where they are coming from. I can't stand it when game developers nickle and dime us for every little thing. That drives me up a wall, but the Scorched Earth DLC is awesome. I took a look at the trailer for it and instantly decided to purchase. No hesitation and I have been playing on the Scorched Earth ever since, hopping back and forth between the two maps. Let's keep in mind that the Scorched Earth DLC is not just another map or a couple of cheap character skins. It is almost like a sequel, with a new map, new creatures, items, resources, abilities. The environment behaves very differently. You have to alter your entire play style to succeed and I think it is awesome. Let me share just a couple of my most memorable ARK experiences.
DAY 1: It all started with me waking up on the beach, basically naked. I start looking around, excited to find some cool dinosaurs. It didn't take long. I quickly found myself surrounded by all sorts of creatures. Triceratops, parasaurs, dodo birds. Everything seemed to be friendly. I went about punching trees, getting sun burnt, eating berries, and generally just trying not to die.
As I am roaming around, a little dinosaur comes right up to me. He's just chillin' there looking up at me, chirping like a little bird. I thought he was pretty cool. I figured that maybe I was making my first dino buddy. I was wrong. I look down to get a good look at him and he bites me in the face. Then again. I try to get away, only to find a whole bunch of these little guys chasing me around biting me. I tried to punch them, but they were tough to hit and there was a bunch of them. Then I died and they ate me. So, I started over.
This process repeated a few times with a couple other dinos, but eventually I had created myself a small little thatch hut. I had a few boxes of resources in there. I had some clothes, a few spears, a couple simple tools and was starting to feel pretty confident. I felt like I was starting to finally get somewhere. Then I met *@#^*, the leader of the *^(%*^&*$ and learned just how huge this game really is.
I was running around collecting things, when a big eagle showed up at my place. On it's back was a dude in full metal armor. He hopped off and told me that I should not build my base at this location. I wasn't about to argue with him. I just asked him not to raid me. He laughed and told me he wanted to show me something. He picked me up with his bird and we started flying.
We flew up really high and he told me to look across the river. There I saw a MASSIVE base. I could not see it from where I was playing, but from this bird's eye view it was revealled. It had tons of buildings, gates and pens with spiked walls everywhere. There were areas where I could see multiple T-rexs all lined up with saddles. They had flyers and brontos and all sorts of creatures, all painted and looking awesome. I saw ramps and walkways leading all over the place. It all looked really cool from this perspective, but I very clearly understood why I needed to move.
*@#^* flew his bird back across the water and landed back at my tiny thatch hut. He told me that was his tribe's base and I should move it further up the hill. I was cool with that. Afterall, he could've just rekt me to start with, but he didn't and he offered to give me some supplies to get going a little more.
Right about then, a bigfoot was walking around on the beach.  *@#^* got off his bird and proceeded to punch it. I decided to try and help so I started stabbing it with my spear. This very quickly resulted in me getting beat up by bigfoot and dying.
I respawned at my base to find the bigfoot defeated and Fortismo laughing. He said he was just seeing if he could punch it out, but thought what I did was really funny. He offered me to join his tribe, but I declined. I thought I should get a little better at this first, but told him that when I get more leveled, I would let him know. He seemed pleased and took off back to his duties, while I began moving my stuff further up the hill to a safer place.
That was my first day playing the game. Since then, much has happened. That guy ended up turning on his tribe and killed a bunch of dinos, kicked out all kinds of people and blew up all sorts of stuff. It was kinda crazy, especially because by the time that all happened, I had no idea. I had my own base on the other side of the hill, with my own tribemates and dinos. Nothing like they had, but I was feeling good about it. We were too caught up in our own adventures. We only came to learn of this crazy inside job through the grapevine of the server community.
As I said before, I have now been playing on the Scorched Earth. My son and I have been hellbent on raising a Wyvern. This has already proven itself to be a major undertaking. We have died SO many times. We have lost a ton of creatures and resources, but we have continued none the less. We now have built traps designed for dragons. We have trained our creatures to be able to outrun the wyverns. We have stolen their eggs, raised hatched them, milked adult females, fed the milk to the hatchlings, and still... still we have not succeeded.
That all said, I have never summoned any of the boss creatures, there are many caves I have never traversed, many creatures I have never seen and even more that I haven't tamed. There is still so much more that I have yet to complete in this game. Keep in mind, I like to play on servers that are purely vanilla or very close to that. I do not like heavy mods that make the game a million times easier. I like the game to be difficult, grooling even. All of this and more, ARK delivers. I absolutely recommend this game. I have even purchased this game for a few of my friends just so that they could play it with me, and almost all of them have been playing it regularly with me ever since. Buy the game. Buy the DLC. It is totally worth it. Especially if it helps this company make more content for this awesome game.

First things first:
The mostley negative and mixed review is FALSE. The only reason it dropped from the 72% rating is because they released a paid dlc during the alhpa that many people considered a very bad move. THIS DOES NOT EFFECT THE GAME! The game is still pretty damn good.
On to the review at hand. This is my second review for this game. I decided to write a new one since it is now in full release and out of early acces. A short recap of my early acces experience: 1: It has a lot of bugs. 2: it is quite a heavy game to run, but devs are working on it. 3: Devs are active and keep adding tons of new stuff. 4: Great learning curve and scaling from easy to hard the further you explore the island (without even adjusting the difficulty setting). 5: basics of the game work very well, there is ton of mods to have fun with, simple to install from the workshop. The devs also greatly support modding and try to make mods smoothly (as much as they can. it is mostly up to the creator of the mod) this game is great!
So how has the game changed since then?
Bug removal has been a bit slow but constant. I felt like the devs were more focused on adding stuff then fixing it. However I feel that, with this full release, those priorities will be switched. Overall a lot of bugs have been fixed, yet quite a few still remain.
As far as the optimisation of the graphics go... meh. It is a good looking game and it runs smoothly, however you still need quite an heavy pc to run this and the game could have been better optimized. I am unable to run it at 4k resolution with my GTX970 in contrast with Battlefield 1 and star wars battlefront (4k 30-50fps).
The positive things that I mentioned earlier still stand. Even more stuff has been added and it is fun too play with. They also added a lot more options to let you customize your dedicated server and solo game which I love. You can change anything from dino damage, to building settings and even choosing what you can and cannot build.
Summary:
It is a very fun game that lets you tame, ride, breed, paint and even pet dinosaurs. Beside that it is a nice survival game that brings you food and water needs, stamina, recource gathering (I think well over 30-40 maybe even 50 recources in the game) a ton of crafting. With those crafted items you can build very large bases (No limit, except for your pc and server capability) which go from wood, stone, metal or alien tech full with electricity, chemistry breedingrooms, gardening, cloning, teleportation you name it. You have quite a large map to explore and if you so choose the dlc can provide even more maps (1 free dlc and 1 paid dlc so far. with another free dlc upcoming).
Now after you get bored after 100-200 hours go ahead and download the mods which can add so much more. Some mods even add like +30% creatures to the game all with their own stats. Or just go ahead and build huge castles.
This game provides a ton of fun especially with mods thrown in and is worth picking up. Keep in mmind there are still some bugs, and yes, I have experianced one crash since the full release, but if you can live past that you can have tons of hours of fun.

Despite being a free to play game, the Warframe devs continue to add new and amazing content, like the open world map. This game is one of the best games and I highly recommend it, you have nothing to lose by downloading it!

What can be said about Warframe? Well a lot actually, for a small indie F2P game it is absolutley incredible. Ive logged countless hours into this game just hacking my way through hoards of enemies, jumping off walls, and flying through space just because the game is FUN.
Warframe starts you off as a lone Tenno, no weapons, just you and your chosen Warframe. Instantly you are thrusted into combat with your guide The Lotus to teach you about the power of the Warframes. Wether you are Excalibur, master of swords, Volt the commander of electricity, or Mag manipulator of enemies, all 3 starter frames are solid choices (pick Excalibur). Not to say the frame you choose is now bound to you more than that piece of gum you swallowed in 3rd grade, as you go along you can create new Warframes, each a master in his or her (yes there are lady space ninjas) field, want a Tank frame who can rush enemies with a greatsword throwing caution to the wind? Then may i suggest the brute Rhino, or our femme fatale Saryn. A high damage dealing Warframe who can wipe out an army in the blink of an eye? Then our local ASSASSINO! Ash, or the hot headed Ember! Perhaps you arent the type to get your hands dirty, why not have the enemy destroy themselves? Invade the minds of your enemies with the lovely Nyx, or manipulate the souls of both the enemy and the dead with really frickin creepy Nekros.~
Now I cant say it dosent have it flaws, yes there are some, and they are pretty glaring. The first is the most infamous. The Grind. Yes this is a free to play game, yes there are weapons to collect and pieces to gather... and yes, you will need luck on your side or a willing sacrifice. Along with the grind there is also the glaring issue of the fact that it IS still in beta. There will be bugs, there will be a lot of bugs, and they will be noticeable. Gamebreaking? Sometimes, but not all hope is lost. The team behind this game are dedicated to making it the best it can be and almost every week we see an update hit the game to squash those pests. The bugs may be there, the issues are large, true, but that dosent stop me from playing it.
Is Warframe a Pay to Win game? Quite simply... well... no. No it isnt. Nothing bought with money you cant get in the game in about 12 hours, plus you can profit from others buying the premium currency (Platinum)! Platinum can be traded amongst other players as a form of payment. Did you pick up a piece to a weapon you already have? Trade it for some Platinum! Ive played this game for a lot longer than my steam profile says i have (this game wasnt always linked with steam) and not ONCE did I ever feel that those who paid $100+ got anything better or anything special from that i didnt have. Warframe is, in my opinion, one of the FINEST examples of a Free To Play game that is not Pay To Win.
Warframe has brought to me a sense of giddyness i havent felt from a game in a long time, and i cant express how amazing i feel after sprinting through a door, sliding on one knee, taking down 3 enemies, jumping on a zipline and riding it before leaping onto a nearby wall only to take out 4 more enemies while wall-running, all in the span of 10 seconds. This game is defintley worth a try, its free so i mean come on, what do you have to lose?

I really love this game. It is a true survival based game, complete with strategy but in an open world environment.
PROS:
1) The game is hard. I mean HARD. I get bored easily, so I enjoy the challenge. You can tweak difficulty if hosting (read CONS) or if playing local, so there is still hope for you. It also gets easier as you level up (you keep your levels in most game modes.)
2) Graphics. The game is beautiful. The world is massive and diverse. It's actually easy to get lost on either currently available map. It rich and detailed. (read CONS for issues)
3). Gameplay. I've played this game for only 130 hours so far. It will take much longer to see the full scope of everything, but it's gameplay gets a little repetitive if you don't break it up. There is enough content (taming, building, leveling, gathering, gathering, and more gathering) to keep you occupied for months or even years.
CONS
1) Cardinal sin; developer is releasing paid for DLC that disrupts the current base game. You will also be required to update all of this information, even if you don't currently have the paid DLC, so you can support others that do. It really does add a pay to win aspect and is quite frustrating. This brings me to the next point.
2) Official servers are awful. There seem to be no moderation, other than a few servers that have alpha tribes moderate themselves, or bully new comers. The official server concept is cool, but this is rediculous. You can never tell how bad it will be until you have spent a week or so. Then, you will argue or be upset enough to start over. Unofficial servers go down, sometimes unexpectedly. Sometimes you are riding a new dino over a hostile area. Sometimes it stays down. You can host a server, but you need to prepare to write code. It's hard and there is no easy button. Best way seems to be to pay for a service provider. PVP servers will wipe you out, simply because you can. Some one has claimed every "territory". PVE servers will grieve you, if you can even find a spot to start on. You have been warned. This is not a "start on a server and play the game" situation. It takes time to find an even remotely functional server.
3) Lag and FPS drop is still this games #1 issue. I've built my monster PC with the latest and greatest and I run at medium graphic options just to not have lag issues. My wife has a pro built machine, two years older and lags in the lowest setting. The devs have not completed any major improvements since we purchased the game 2 months ago. There are days that the game is unplayable.
VERDICT
If you can stomach the issues, the game is a ton of fun. If the developers decide to fix the lag and FPS issues, the game will be a joy. Oh, and they need to stop focusing on DLC and add ons, and extra games. They do release lots of content for free, but don't plan on going to an official PVP or PVE without friends. It won't work and it won't be fun, unless you can devote 40+ hours per week to watching over your things. The game is fun, buy it or don't. I did, and I'm glad.

Pretty Good Game Review Considering (PGGRC)
TL;DR - Look at my playtime for a starter. My most played game and the reason is that it blends a lot of genres into one perfect mix. Beautiful looking and runs like a dream that puts triple A games to shame. You don’t expect this level of content and quality from a free2play nor a small dev but they listen and the level of quality shows this. Must try.
In depth:
Performance - Rock solid. Every setting aside bloom (for personal preference) and runs at 140fps on a GTX 760. Very good port with a lot of customization and frame counter to test. The game also looks very good and at such a high frame rate on a mid-high GPU they should tell other triple A companies how to optimise a game. There is an odd frame drop when there is a bad connection as it is pier to pier but it’s a small and rare price to pay.
Graphics - Well considering the great frame rate the game must look dated? Not even close. The game looks very good (above average) with very good textures and unique models. However a lot of the warframes abilities use PhysX so AMD users will miss out on better effects than usual. The atmosphere of each planet is also quite diverse; lots of locations like forests, snowy mountains, spaceships, air cities and now underwater maps. A lot of variation to choose with more coming.
Gameplay - When starting the biggest mistake you can make is not to uninstall. Stick with it and build some better gear. The game has a big learning curve and it requires some hours to get into it. But when you do it’s a game you won’t want to put down.
Digital Extreme are one of the best devs out there. Why? They listen. Yes some companies do but they don’t like DE, listen, change and adapt features to the audience as well as their own direction for the game. Community is solid with a lot of people willing to help but also rip you off when trading. The actual gameplay has to be good if its quite repetive. Thank god it is. The actual physics and animations are spot on. The gunplay is very strong with each weapon, old, current or future inspired all have a great look, feel, sound and punch through. If that’s an old revolver which spins as you fire and drops people like a ton of bricks to a crossbow that staples people to wall, there is a lot of variety. Even better are the frames. Power suits you can customize with colours, skins, armour, helmets and mods that enhance your frame to your playstyle. Want a frame that is a glass cannon, tank or one that relies on powers you can. Each frame has powers which give them a individual feel and playstyle. This is enhanced with a range of customization to your character, weapons and pets allowing you to play to your style.
Replayability - The game is an RPG at heart and therefore is meant to be repeated. With no clear story aside some lore, which is quite deep and unique but is lacked in missions, the game is all about that loot. There is a lack of new end game content for people with a lot of hours (like me) but they are working on it with raids coming out. But there is a lot to do and a lot of loot and frames to earn if you don’t mind a bit of grind. The game can be extremely grindy in the void, higher level content but I would take that over a pay2win game.
Conclusion - Having played 400+ hours into this game (My most played game, EVER) I can highly recommend. This game has destroyed to rules I have about early access/open beta games, one; don’t put in a huge amount of time and don’t spend money on it. I’ve done both and haven’t regretted it. This game has a lot of updates, fixes, balances and improvements all thanks to Digital Extremes who actually listen to their fan base. One of the fairest F2P games and blends many genres into a great shooter. This is a masterpiece of a game that gets better every update.

I love reading reviews from arrogant, over entitled scumbags who have 250+ hours on record in this game and have slammed it recently for deciding to release some paid DLC.
Here's a novel thought or two for those out there who are morally outraged by this devs attempt to generate some revenue...
-You paid 30 bucks for an absolutely huge game, good luck finding value like that elsewhere. Shut up and quit whinging.

THE GAME ITSELF
Should I buy it? Yes.
PROS
-It truly is a beautiful game, very demanding on your rig - suggest that those with SSDs load Ark onto their SSD and check to make sure you've maxed out your virtual memory, I found these two steps improved performance significantly.
-Regular content addition. Updates for this game roll out on an absolutely ludicrous schedule, do Wildcard live at their studio or something?
-The base construction is incredibly satisfying and even in EA has great polish. You look back at your base and truly feel a sense of gratification and achievement. Rivalled only by Subnautica in this respect.

CONS

-VERY demanding systems reqs. Make sure your rig is up to task to get the best possible experience.
-It is in EA, you might find a slight jank here or an oddity there, but the game is nonetheless very well polished.
BOTTOM LINE
A must have title for any survival enthusiast - just be wary of the jerks if you decide to play with random people.

I've been an on and off player of Warframe since it was in beta. I really dove in recently when my wife finally got a gaming PC and we were able to play together. Warframe is an excellent game, and is fairly reasonable as F2P titles go with pushing you towards real money purchases.
A F2P third person action game combining awesome guns and melee combat. Play as one of the Tenno, ancient beings that have been in stasis for hundreds of years. They utilize Warframes; armored suits from a long lost technological age.
*A wide variety of weapons and Warframes to acquire. Each has their own advantages and disadvantages.
*A pleasantly diverse array of mods that can be attached to weapons, companions, and Warframes, which enable a host of different builds.
*Exciting and fast paced combat.
*The ability to design and build your own dojo for your clan.
*You can trade items to other players for Platinum, the premium currency.
*Build times on new frames, weapons, etc., don't prevent you from playing. There's always something to be doing.
*A variety of content that blooms once you've ranked up a few times and unlocked some planets. Syndicates, Void Missions, the Void Trader, farming bosses for new frame parts, breeding your own pet Kubrow (alien attack dog), and more.
*Everything that affects gameplay can be earned in game without paying a dime. Only cosmetic items require platinum.
*The parkour system can be a tad unpredictable. This is supposed to be getting a rework with Update 17.
*The build times can be somewhat frustrating, as it pits your wallet against your patience. But that's what other games are for, and there's plenty of other things to do in the game.
*The item grind is definitely present. And while I don't mind it that much, it often relegates late game missions to just a few frames which are suited better for item farming.
*You have limited weapon and Warframe slots until you buy more with platinum. You do get some platinum to start, and it wouldn't really bother me, if they didn't already have build times that can be rushed with platinum, along with cosmetic items.
*The game does not allow you to craft multiple items of the same type simultaneously. If I've earned the blueprints and the crafting materials, I should be able to build ten Forma at once if I want.
*Forma, late game items that allow you to install higher ranked mods onto a weapon/companion/Warframe, also reset the item's level to zero. This forces you to re-level the item in question, and the item's level, is tied to the number of mods you can install. Most items would require several Forma in order to install max ranked mods in all of the slots, so this adds to the grind quite a bit, but does nothing for the gameplay, especially since Forma are an item you need to farm for in the first place, and you have to hit max level with the item in question each time before installing an additional Forma.
Overall, I enjoy playing Warframe quite a bit. Especially now that I've gotten our dojo up and running with the help of my clan mates. I know I listed more negatives than I did positives, but they also don't bother me all that much. The game is a lot of fun to play, and is truly unique among the masses of military shooters and zombie survival games.
Play it, you'll love it. Do so patiently, or be ready to shell out some cash.

Oh boy, this is gonna be a long review...
Buckle your seatbelts, Boys & Girls, Grab a snack and enjoy the ride.
So I've had the game for about a year & half, Two years, Something around that long. Though just to make it clear, I might get one or two things wrong about what I know during this so just bear with me.
------------------------------------------------------------------------
THE GAME:
So how do I explain Warframe? To put it in simple terms, It's a game about some kickass space ninjas.
You play as a Tenno, You have been in cryosleep for decades until you are finally awoken by a character we known only as The Lotus, Your guide through this journey. As you are awoken, you are giving a choice between three different suits, which are called Warframes that allow you to channel power, and three different weapons in primary, secondary and melee.
You are a defender of the Solar System and all its inhabitants, You will find yourself travelling to all kinds of different planets in our Solar System, Earth, Mercury, Mars, Pluto and so on.
So far, There are five different factions in the game, Four of them are your enemies which you must defend the System from.
Tenno, Grineer, Corpus, Infected & Orokin, Each with all of their own unique units and bosses. Tenno is the race that you play for, So you will not be finding any other Tenno units as enemies during Gameplay, Unless you count PVP, Where you fight other Tenno warriors in online battle.
So, You've picked your Warframe and your weapons, you've completed the tutorial, Now you have your personal stealth ship, The Liset, Controlled by your (un)trustworthy companion, Ordis, a computer AI. This ship is where you will be spending a lot of the game and is pretty much your main menu. From here you select planets and missions, you check the market for weapons and Warframes, You customize your gear in the back of the ship, You craft new weapons from materials you pick up in the game, you select mods to put on your equipment or sell or even transmute them into better cards. This is basically your own little HQ.
------------------------------------------------------------------------
THE GOOD:
- Variety of Warframes, Each with their own abilities.
- Huge variety of different weapons in all areas.
- Good planet variety, Each with enviroments detailed to that specific area.
- Decent level scaling, Higher level planets having tougher enemies and more variety.
- Detailed graphics, Apart from one or two pop-ins or missing textures, though it's very rare to find one.
- Brilliant lore in the game (Even though it could be hard to find...Use the Wiki, People.)
- Mods of all types to apply to your equipment, allowing you a different variety of elemental attacks to use on various enemies and specializing for different scenarios.
- Teamplay. You will always find yourself playing in a squad of up to four, Though this isn't forced on you as you can play strictly with friends or completely solo.
------------------------------------------------------------------------
THE BAD:
- Very repetitive. The game involves a lot of going back to the same areas for grinding for credits and resources.
- Controls can be difficult at first for new players, Though they should easily become used to them after tutorials and a few hours of gameplay.
- Very grindy game, You'll need to work hard to get that specific gun you just bought for 20,000 credits with 1,000 salvage to craft from.
------------------------------------------------------------------------

FINAL VERDICT:
So I know I went easy on this game, Not a lot of bad and plenty of good but this is my own opinion and how I see the game.
Yes, The game is very grindy and it does have platinum in the game which you purchase with your own money to buy equipment instantly without having to craft it at the Foundry. Although this is in the game, I personally wouldn't say that this game is Pay to Win, Because you can still get every single piece of equipment you can buy with Plats, Though it will take some grinding to get to but it'll be worth it.
Even if you do choose to buy a piece of equipment with Plats, It gives you a little extra by giving you an extra slot for another weapon and putting an Orokin Reactor or Cell in it, which doubles your mod capacity.
Personally, I LOVE this game, It's one of my most favorite games ever and will continue to be for the next few years, The Developers do amazing work and they can only make this game better than it already is, They have a great community that they keep in touch with and the players and clans are just as amazing.
And there's no subscription fee for this, All completely free for as long as you like, So I definitely recommend at least checking this one out.
My final score is 9/10. The game is brilliant, Has a lot of future potential despite a few faults here and there.
If you're interested in finding out more, I'd recommend checking out the Wiki to learn more about this game or go on Youtube and find some gameplay videos or tutorials to learn more about the mechanics of this game.
There is SO much more about this game that I can't fit into detail here, Things such as Companions, Syndicates, Relays, Bosses, Units types, Clans, Dojos, Levelling. Though I guess I must leave something to the discovery.
I hope to see you all on the battlefield soon.

2) Official servers are awful. There seem to be no moderation, other than a few servers that have alpha tribes moderate themselves, or bully new comers. The official server concept is cool, but this is rediculous. You can never tell how bad it will be until you have spent a week or so. Then, you will argue or be upset enough to start over. Unofficial servers go down, sometimes unexpectedly. Sometimes you are riding a new dino over a hostile area. Sometimes it stays down. You can host a server, but you need to prepare to write code. It's hard and there is no easy button. Best way seems to be to pay for a service provider. PVP servers will wipe you out, simply because you can. Some one has claimed every "territory". PVE servers will grieve you, if you can even find a spot to start on. You have been warned. This is not a "start on a server and play the game" situation. It takes time to find an even remotely functional server.
3) Lag and FPS drop is still this games #1 issue. I've built my monster PC with the latest and greatest and I run at medium graphic options just to not have lag issues. My wife has a pro built machine, two years older and lags in the lowest setting. The devs have not completed any major improvements since we purchased the game 2 months ago. There are days that the game is unplayable.
VERDICT
If you can stomach the issues, the game is a ton of fun. If the developers decide to fix the lag and FPS issues, the game will be a joy. Oh, and they need to stop focusing on DLC and add ons, and extra games. They do release lots of content for free, but don't plan on going to an official PVP or PVE without friends. It won't work and it won't be fun, unless you can devote 40+ hours per week to watching over your things. The game is fun, buy it or don't. I did, and I'm glad.

// ARK REVIEW AS OF SEPTEMBER 26, 2016. A NOTE FOR NEW PLAYERS. //
Honestly, I don't know why everyone is so butthurt over DLC in an early access game. I say this because I don't think anyone realizes WHY they released paid DLC so early. Just Google it and find out for yourselves.
ARK is yet another open world survival game set in a time of dinosaurs where you can customize and create your own character and give them their own name, tame dinosaurs and give them names, and collaborate with friends by creating tribes. The main mechanic of this game is the ability to tame dinosaurs. Different dinos and species can be used for different tasks to make your life easier. For instance, an Anklyosauras can be used for mining out Flint/Metal and a T-Rex can be used for gathering meat. You can also learn 'engrams' by leveling up. Engrams are basically tools/weapons/machines/buildings that you can craft. It is best if you are in a tribe with friends so each person can learn different categories of engrams. For instance, one focuses on weapons while the other on buildings/machines and so on. Being in a tribe is probably the best way to play, since you can share tamed dinosaurs, share gained xp, share buildings, and possible learn every engram on the list!
If you are a fan of open world survivals and Jurassic Park, you will love this game.
The main issue in this game is its optimization. Not so much that it's BAD, it's just you need a high-end PC if you want to run Ultra settings at 60 FPS. The system requirements are a lie. Of course, this is different for everyone.
For instance, I have a GTX 960, FX-6300, and 16GB RAM and I can run Medium-High pretty well. If you are real picky about how your game looks, have at least a GTX 970 or an AMD equivalent or higher.
Pros:
+ Good official servers
+ Great survival mechanics
+ No limit on inventory slots - just weight
+ Dinosaur taming
+ Tribes
Cons:
- Level grinding can be tedious (look for x3 servers)
- Single player is boring and tedious - can't learn every engram
- Requires high-end PC for Ultra settings
- Price - both base game and DLC (wait for sales)
Verdict:
I definitely recommend this game for those who enjoy open world survivals and are looking for a new one to play.

ARK: Survival Evolved Review (as of 9/26/16)
(NEW PLAYERS READ THIS!)
As it seems that this game is getting a whole ton of negative reviews lately, allow me to come in and shed some truth upon the matter. At the time of this writing the reviews for this game are Mostly Negative with an overall review rating of Mixed, so to any person who has not played the game or otherwise is considering buying this game presently, consider this review for you. I have been playing this game for over a year now and I have seen a majority of its development firsthand. Yes I will admit that there were some serious issues with this game in the early phases as it was getting off the ground, a few of which admittedly may still not have been completely solved such as graphical optimization, a few random and rare glitches and bugs, etc. However, with all of that said, I say with the utmost seriousness that this game is hands down one of the best games i've ever played (and I am including my console and PC experience in that list)!
So at this point you are probably asking why I can say that and yet the game has such unbalanced review scores. Well there are a couple reasons and I will discuss them here. For one thing, the issues I mentioned above, while uncommon, still have enough of a presence to make this game extremely troublesome to play on computers with lesser hardware. Even with my full desktop rig I still encounter issues from time to time. Another unrelated but still relevant con i'd like to mention is the AI of the creatures in this game is severely lacking in places such as their hit boxes and solo pathfinding abilities. The last is the the worst as I have had several tamed creatures die because they threw themselves off a cliff to kill an extremely insignificant wild dino that got too nosy for his own good. I have also been able to tame several wild creatures but strategically using terrain or flora to trap them in place and tranq them because they are too dumb in most cases to try to get you in any direction other than a straight line.
However in spite of these, the true reason behind the unbalanced reviews as of late are for one reason and one reason only, the paid DLC released about 3 weeks ago, the Scorched Earth package. For those of you who don't know, this DLC adds a desert themed map as well as several new items, creatures, and more into the game. A lot of people have said that this DLC should have been free as technically speaking the game is not out of Early Access yet and not "completed" and others have said that 20 bucks is a high price to pay for the content it provides. As someone who has the main game and DLC both, let me just state that these arguments, while not completely unfounded at their core, are completely overblown and overstated. I have seen a multitude of other games that have come out of early access or otherwise with paid DLC attached that offer significantly less in their main games than ARK does and moreover have far longer development cycles and far less community interaction. I could go on and on about what this game has to offer, but for sake of not ranting, i'll include my pros and cons in a compact list at the bottom of the review. I'll just leave this note off on that the game doesn't force you to have the DLC nor has it been shafting the main game in favor of it, so please don't put any more stock in the multitude of anti-pay arguments as any more than just opposite opinions ro my own and do not let them cloud your opinions more than normal.
Without further adieu, to wrap this up, here are my abridged pros and cons to ARK: Survival Evolved.
Cons:
Limited Graphics Settings and Server Performance Issues
AI Lacking
Random (but rare) glitches and bugs
Pros:
Great cooperative gameplay
Tons of replay value
Awesome crafting and building systems
Epic Mod Community
Awesome Development Team
Constant fixes and updates to make things run as best as possible.
I will admit that this review is probably as biased in favor of this game as other reivews lately seem to be against it, but hopefully you can take what i've said here, compare it to what others have said, and make an informed decision base on your preferences. I really enjoy this game and i'm sure many others will too!

You will see a lot of negative reviews sense the release of Scorched Earth. While people are entitled to their opinion, I feel some are missing the point. Yes, ark is in early access and it may seem bad to release paid DLC for an early access game, however the whole Scorched Earth DLC was in fact also an early access test, a feature in development to be sure that the means TO add expansions worked.
WildCard have mentioned there planning on releasing new arks, new maps to play on in the form of expansions. Scorched earth was an early access test to be sure the means to do so went smoothly and to iron out any bugs or issues that might come from adding new content in this means. (this is explained in one of their news reports).
Granted however: I do find the price choice they went for to be a little high. Scorched earth DLC is a map, just a map, granted a very nice looking map, but it is still just a map with new fancy weather effects. The dinos and items can already be brought into the base game even without the DLC, and WildCard gave the go-ahead for modders to bring the dinos into the world, allowing them to spawn on both the Island, Center, and all user made maps without need of the DLC.
While this can be seen as both a good and a bad thing...  Good as you don't need the DLC to enjoy some of what Scorched Earth has to offer, bad in that you're paying $20 for a map, and that feels a bit steep when there are many user created maps free to play on, some also with their own custom weather and effects. Personally, if the map cost maybe $5, it may have been received a little better.
See it how you will, Scorched earth to me seems really good and that they were able to fix many bugs that came with adding an expansion to the game, but the price to me is way too much for just a map. If anything, wait for a sale to get it, or enjoy it via the mods that allow the Scorched Earth dinos to spawn in the world.

Here are a few of my thoughts on this game
Pros
1) True F2P , only thing you need to pay for is cosmetics, everything else can be obtained through Grinding.

5) Lots of weapons to choose from. Dont Listen to people who say only 3-4 weapons are end game viable. The real reason is that they are the easiest to make end game viable. With proper mods , forma , catalysts/reactors every weapon is end game viable aside from maybe 2 weapons which are just hopeless ( Im talking about the Hind and Machete).
In the same vein , NO warframe is useless. Some do a certain job better than others but no single warframe is useless.
6) You can build your own clan home ( called Dojo) which are very customizable.
7)  Trade chat exists to help you when RNG ♥♥♥♥s you over. You can even earn the in game currency ( called Platinum) by selling Prime parts and mods when possible. If you are willing to grind enough you wont have to spend a dime on this game.
8) Developer that is very active with the community.
Cons
1) No dedicated servers, its all P2P. 98% of the time this is never an issue , but god help you if the host has a wooden PC , or is trying to play with a dialup connection.
2) Loot follows a RNG( Random Number generator) system which can really really really really ♥♥♥♥ you over sometimes.

4) Slightly hard for newer players to get into. My suggestion is get to MR1 and get into a good clan ( Dont get into ones with MR requirments they are not worth it) Most people are helpful.

All in all the game is really good, Its great if you want a non competetive game to just chill with. 8.5 out of tenno.

Obviously, I haven't dumped as many hours into this game as other players but I feel that I have put in my ♥♥♥♥ing time with this game.
Conceptually, it's perfect. It is exactly what you wanted as a kid when you were pretending to play dinosaurs. It takes Jurassic Park, which I suspect is what it owes the majority of its success to, to the adult, survival levels that you wanted.
However, in reality, this game is a mess. When it was first released, it was marketed as a AAA game for an indie price. OBVIOUSLY THAT WAS ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥T. The true release price hike is a slap to the face of everyone who was smart enough to wait until this game was finished unlike I was.
The performance has always been a lie on steam. No matter how good of a rig you had, you were going to run into huge FPS drops for literally no reason. Well, I say no reason because the reason isn't justifiable. Instead of putting together a base game, polishing it up, optimizing the performance, and then testing and releasing new assets and content updates like they should have, they took advantage of all this easy EA money just pouring in because of the Jurassic World movie release. This company was pulling in tens of millions of dollars a month. They could have afforded to do the game correctly.
The content itself never felt like how it was supposed to be. It was essentially dinosaurs that kind of move around but were more like if you placed a plastic toy on a bumpy hill. You'd get a sort of hover effect with all of the larger dinosaurs. It doesn't feel like the game itself wants the assets and the floor to actually interact. The smaller dinos had the absolute worst hitbox issues, even on solo where you couldn't just blame it on latency. Raptors on solo would kill you in a matter of seconds, as they should have. The raptors on servers couldn't even hit you if you just kinda bounce around a little.
This brings me to the servers. The official servers are absolute garbage. I would pick a server, something that shouldn't change in latency too much unless the save and links are moved to a new server elsewhere in the world, and within a couple of weeks it would go from about 90-120 ping to 300-400. There was literally never a good reason to play online. The game itself sucked up too much computing resources to run the game, and a server, while also linking in other players. So you were stuck between usually unplayable latency and solo. Solo, I might add, was ruined by the fact that you could just switch on god mode at any point. Other than that, solo was the only thing that ever felt like it was close to how the game was meant to be.
The DLC is a rip off. Survival of the fittest is a joke.
I admire the company for the ambition it had, and I wish them success on their next projects, but this was a flop in my opinion. I feel like the company took way too much advantage of the player base and then for sure took it to entirely new levels of exploitation with the price hike.
After having thrown away 140 hours of my life in EA, a major mistake on my part (But I did get much better with mouse and keyboard), I just don't think there's any fun left for me to have from this game and probably from this company. We'll see what they do in a number of years, but there are way better survival games made by companies who would rather focus on performance over content instead of the other way around like Studio Wildcard did. I waited and waited and waited just to play this game at more than 18-30 FPS and it literally never happened. I honestly don't care if it can do it now, either. All the fun has been stomped on and torn apart by endless hordes of titanomyrma.

If anyone is interested in an opinion about the paid DLC that isn't just whining over $20, keep reading.
First of all, yes, $20 for a EA game is pretty crazy sounding, but let us consider what the Dev's have done with the money they have recieved from the base game (pre-DLC).
1- They built onto a great idea for well over a year and added LOTS of new content that has given me more to do for $25 than a Triple A title has given me for $60.
2- They have introduced a new game mode that, while not popular among all players, is a nice change of pace (Survival of the Fittest).
3- They have hosted competitions (SOTF) that have had some fairly large REAL MONEY payouts for the community.
4- They have given away thousands of copies of the game for absolutely no return other than a community expansion.
5- Many people forget this, probably a solid 70% of players did not pay full price for this game, it is constantly discounted for $5 or more. While the price may have raised a mere $5 over the course of a year, that is nothing compared to other survival games such as DayZ or H1Z1 which have raised their prices of their games with not very much content additon to back it.
Keeping all of that in mind, the cost of the game plus the DLC is now a total of $50. Check the hours played for most of these other reviews. Most are in the hundreds or more. This game, with DLC, is still cheaper than a triple A title. I can't say for everyone, but I know I have had more fun and put more time into this game than most of my triple A titles. While 400+ hours isn't a lot, I have plenty of desire to continue to add to this.
Now as a Disclaimer, I have not paid for the DLC (yet?) but if you check the reviews for the DLC, they are "very positive". For those who ACTUALLY TRIED IT and didn't dis the dev's over a mere $20, the player base actually loves the additions.
While yes, it could be a free DLC as the other additions have been, you must consider the deal you are getting. The Dev's say the game will be released (In full version) on console this holiday. If they meet the deadline or not, the game will likely include the scorched earth DLC plus the game for $60, a common game price point. Now does that $50 (or likely less) pricetag sound as bad? Don't let the cry baby reviews get you scared of the game. The dev's have always been hard at work for this game, and will continue to do so. The reviews for this game were also "Very Positive" before the DLC, and that should tell you something.

Pretty Good Game Review Considering (PGGRC)
TL;DR - Look at my playtime for a starter. My most played game and the reason is that it blends a lot of genres into one perfect mix. Beautiful looking and runs like a dream that puts triple A games to shame. You don’t expect this level of content and quality from a free2play nor a small dev but they listen and the level of quality shows this. Must try.
In depth:
Performance - Rock solid. Every setting aside bloom (for personal preference) and runs at 140fps on a GTX 760. Very good port with a lot of customization and frame counter to test. The game also looks very good and at such a high frame rate on a mid-high GPU they should tell other triple A companies how to optimise a game. There is an odd frame drop when there is a bad connection as it is pier to pier but it’s a small and rare price to pay.
Graphics - Well considering the great frame rate the game must look dated? Not even close. The game looks very good (above average) with very good textures and unique models. However a lot of the warframes abilities use PhysX so AMD users will miss out on better effects than usual. The atmosphere of each planet is also quite diverse; lots of locations like forests, snowy mountains, spaceships, air cities and now underwater maps. A lot of variation to choose with more coming.
Gameplay - When starting the biggest mistake you can make is not to uninstall. Stick with it and build some better gear. The game has a big learning curve and it requires some hours to get into it. But when you do it’s a game you won’t want to put down.
Digital Extreme are one of the best devs out there. Why? They listen. Yes some companies do but they don’t like DE, listen, change and adapt features to the audience as well as their own direction for the game. Community is solid with a lot of people willing to help but also rip you off when trading. The actual gameplay has to be good if its quite repetive. Thank god it is. The actual physics and animations are spot on. The gunplay is very strong with each weapon, old, current or future inspired all have a great look, feel, sound and punch through. If that’s an old revolver which spins as you fire and drops people like a ton of bricks to a crossbow that staples people to wall, there is a lot of variety. Even better are the frames. Power suits you can customize with colours, skins, armour, helmets and mods that enhance your frame to your playstyle. Want a frame that is a glass cannon, tank or one that relies on powers you can. Each frame has powers which give them a individual feel and playstyle. This is enhanced with a range of customization to your character, weapons and pets allowing you to play to your style.
Replayability - The game is an RPG at heart and therefore is meant to be repeated. With no clear story aside some lore, which is quite deep and unique but is lacked in missions, the game is all about that loot. There is a lack of new end game content for people with a lot of hours (like me) but they are working on it with raids coming out. But there is a lot to do and a lot of loot and frames to earn if you don’t mind a bit of grind. The game can be extremely grindy in the void, higher level content but I would take that over a pay2win game.
Conclusion - Having played 400+ hours into this game (My most played game, EVER) I can highly recommend. This game has destroyed to rules I have about early access/open beta games, one; don’t put in a huge amount of time and don’t spend money on it. I’ve done both and haven’t regretted it. This game has a lot of updates, fixes, balances and improvements all thanks to Digital Extremes who actually listen to their fan base. One of the fairest F2P games and blends many genres into a great shooter. This is a masterpiece of a game that gets better every update.

This was a private server which can have it's own issues such as admins who don't share your idea of a fun time ... but there's always a server out there that matches your taste I feel.
I think at this point Ark really works best as a large scale co-op game ... if you had a group of friends who all wanted to play and explore the world together there is enough content to keep you busy for a year or more if you played on vanilla settings.  Which can be pretty painful with small number groups, but not too bad with abigger group especisally if they have good synergy,
I don't know if I'd ever play Ark again, but I do suggest it for anyone who wants to lose their job, friends and possibly significant other.

And with that being said on to one of the best games Ive had the honor of playing. Keep in mind this is Early Access and content is still being added. The game isnt optimized but they are still adding dinos and items so why would they optimize it just to add more codes shortly after. Controls could be better but I like the fact you can use mouse/keyboard or a controller. Can be tricky at 1st but got the hang of it very quick. Grinding to tame dinosaurs can be a hassle in the beginning until you start taming the right beasts. then farming and taming becomes sooo easy. Lots of servers to choose from (population declining due to Center Map and new Scorched DLC) but its still a great game. PvP is amazing, just keep in mind you can be taken prisoner. I have 2 people locked in my base. i have to keep them fed or hydrated or they will die and be free to roam the beautiful world of ark. I told them it was my area, but they didnt wanna listen("it puts the lotion on its skin"). Traversing the world is very dangerous until u get higher levels/gear or a flyer. If set correctly you will have to enter codes at every door you own(unless your the tribe leader. Than you have a bit of privacy and can set certain door/dinos to leader/admin access only. Review Warframe
Detail/Deskripsi Game
Warframe adalah  Co-op Online yang di mana game ini bisa juga dibilang Space Ninja dengan character yang memiliki Power & Skill yang berbeda dan anda di ajak untuk berpetualang di luar angkasa dan berperang menggunakan senjata yang Modern (awalnya senjata dibuat berdasarkan unsur ninja tetapi semakin menjadi Space Ninja) dan lagi karena ini Co-op Online sehingga anda bisa memainkan bersama 4 bahkan 8 orang didalam satu game (latest patch)
Kelebihan
+ game free to play terbaik yang dimana dari awal saya main sampe detik ini updatenya selalu gila-gilaan, apalagi pas update melee 2.0
+ pilihan primary, secondary, melee dan pet (saya bilangnya seh pet soalnya ambil barang kerjanya akowkwkokwkw)
+ graphic diperbaiki terus dan semakin baik
+ soundnya seperti nyata. apalagi kalau anda pakai yang bass lebih greget.
+ banyak pilihan warframe (job)
+ banyak pilihan skills
+ banyak syndicate
+ ada mode PvP
+ banyak pilihan mission
+ combo melee weapon membuatnya semakin baik
+ ada hewan peliharaan (kubrow)
+ punya pesawat luar angkasa sendiri
+ bisa membuat clan logo sendiri dan mengirim ke developer untuk aktivasinya
+ transaksi tradenya aman
+ pengaturan menu setting cukup sederhana
+ User Interfacenya seperti nyata
+ ada guide langsung dari pihak developer sehingga bisa review dengan baik
+ mod event benar-benar cuman ada di event dan tidak bakalan di ulang sampai kapanpun, jadi kalau anda kelewatan mod event selamat yah
+ event mission selalu keren
Kekurangan
- main and side story kurang lengkap, walaupun anda jalan dari planet pertama sampai terakhir semuanya tidak jelas jika wiki warframe tidak dibaca
- dsini ada 4 bangsa ( tenno, corpus, griner dan infection ) tetapi anda cuman bisa pake tenno
- dsini maennya dungeon terus (perumpamaan)
- dulu low end bisa, sekarang low end selalu patah-patah.
- clan host bisa ampe 50++ tapi maennya gak ada yang lebih dari 8++
- PvP kurang greget walaupun sudah dirubah berulang-ulang sampai detik ini masih membosankan
- untuk warna default hanya diberikan sangat sedikit
- Mastery rank = Levelling semua senjata, jadi klo ada yang level masterynya tinggi artinya dia udah coba dari senjata yang paling jelek sampe yang paling baik(sehingga Mastery Rank rendah tetap bisa mengalahkan Mastery Rank tinggi)
- kalau mau trade minimal harus punya clan dojo
- enchant butuh 12,14,28 jam bahkan sampai yang 3 hari
- kadang bosan karena maennya dungeon

suka FPS (first person shooter)? Suka TPS (third person shooter)? Suka yang berbau ninja-ninja? My Review is base on the game and gameplay. But before getting into that I would like to say
1# people complaining about the game being paid dlc should really STFU. If you feel the "early access" shouldnt have paid for dlc, dont ♥♥♥♥ing buy it. But to buy it and complain the game isnt finished not only underrates the game but also deters people from buying a game, based off your opinion on when content should be paid for. Thats not what this section is for. Its for the review of the game. Not the company.
2# If the game lags on your system... UPGRADE. There is a list with Minimum Specs Required to play. Make sure your atleast at recommended before you complain. If the person is lagging and not posting computer specs, thats mostlikely the main reason their lagging. This game is meant for good GPUs
And with that being said on to one of the best games Ive had the honor of playing. Keep in mind this is Early Access and content is still being added. The game isnt optimized but they are still adding dinos and items so why would they optimize it just to add more codes shortly after. Controls could be better but I like the fact you can use mouse/keyboard or a controller. Can be tricky at 1st but got the hang of it very quick. Grinding to tame dinosaurs can be a hassle in the beginning until you start taming the right beasts. then farming and taming becomes sooo easy. Lots of servers to choose from (population declining due to Center Map and new Scorched DLC) but its still a great game. PvP is amazing, just keep in mind you can be taken prisoner. I have 2 people locked in my base. i have to keep them fed or hydrated or they will die and be free to roam the beautiful world of ark. I told them it was my area, but they didnt wanna listen("it puts the lotion on its skin"). Traversing the world is very dangerous until u get higher levels/gear or a flyer. At which point you can be sniped out of the sky, once again depending on server playstyle. Watch the tribe system. I have never had an issue with it besides me not reading things correctly. Some people say entire tribes have been given away because of it. IDK because there is a feture to merge tribes. So maybe people need to read more. IDK. Playing with a tribe can be good or bad. Tribe system doesnt allow for privacy. Meaning you build a base and unless the tribe goverance is set a certain way, anyone in your tribe can get in your base. If set correctly you will have to enter codes at every door you own(unless your the tribe leader. Than you have a bit of privacy and can set certain door/dinos to leader/admin access only. If your looking for a challenging game and love sandbox games this is it.Ive been playing since day 2 seeing servers crashed all during day 1(overload) with 1600+ hours. This game is well worth the $20. I would also suggest going on♥♥♥♥♥and getting it on sale if you can. If you dont know about♥♥♥♥♥.. Your Welcome. Hello Steam Users,
This is a tough review to write and I will try to explain why as concisely as possible below.
Summary:
Ark is a great game where you enter a world of dinos, not many like it exist. It is a graphically pretty game with major optiimization issues using Unreal Engine 4. The best hardware will still not run this at 4k/60fps. I'm a player from a game called Ultima Online. It was the first sandbox MMORPG ever. UO was an amazing experience, it had High HIGHs and very low LOWS. The emotion was what made the game so enthralling, however, this game is not quite like UO. The things you lose in the game far outweigh the things you gain and being an open-ended sandbox MMO, you will get all kinds of trashy players in here.
I want you to understand. These types of games draw the very worse people. Griefers, Trolls and worse. Kids/Teens/Adults who want to play out their darkest fantasies of what is really in their person. They are miserable people with massive character flaws and anti-social tendencies.
The above may seem strange to have in a review, but it is important to understand the general population of the game. Now that you understand that,
You have to further take into account the Risk vs. Reward ratio of this game. You can spend 10 hours taming a dinosaur, for someone to come by and hit it with a metal pike a few times before it finishes, to reduce its stats or kill it. I want to highlight this. Think about who has the advantage. The person with 2 hours invested building a pike or the person with 100 hours invested getting all neccessary items/tools to take down and tame a dinosaur for 10 hours?
That is the core issue and why I cannot in good faith recommend it.
On top of that it is a huge time sink, because resource gathering and the like are overly hard. So like i said, you can spend 1000 hours building a super cool base, for someoen who spent 20 hours ONLY building rockets to come and mess up all your hard work in a moment of time. These are realities of the game.
Do not buy unless you understand these above factors.

Hello Steam Users,
This is a tough review to write and I will try to explain why as concisely as possible below.
Summary:
Ark is a great game where you enter a world of dinos, not many like it exist. It is a graphically pretty game with major optiimization issues using Unreal Engine 4. The best hardware will still not run this at 4k/60fps. I'm a player from a game called Ultima Online. It was the first sandbox MMORPG ever. UO was an amazing experience, it had High HIGHs and very low LOWS. The emotion was what made the game so enthralling, however, this game is not quite like UO. The things you lose in the game far outweigh the things you gain and being an open-ended sandbox MMO, you will get all kinds of trashy players in here.
I want you to understand. These types of games draw the very worse people. Griefers, Trolls and worse. Kids/Teens/Adults who want to play out their darkest fantasies of what is really in their person. They are miserable people with massive character flaws and anti-social tendencies.
The above may seem strange to have in a review, but it is important to understand the general population of the game. Now that you understand that,
You have to further take into account the Risk vs. Reward ratio of this game. You can spend 10 hours taming a dinosaur, for someone to come by and hit it with a metal pike a few times before it finishes, to reduce its stats or kill it. I want to highlight this. Think about who has the advantage. The person with 2 hours invested building a pike or the person with 100 hours invested getting all neccessary items/tools to take down and tame a dinosaur for 10 hours?
That is the core issue and why I cannot in good faith recommend it.
On top of that it is a huge time sink, because resource gathering and the like are overly hard. So like i said, you can spend 1000 hours building a super cool base, for someoen who spent 20 hours ONLY building rockets to come and mess up all your hard work in a moment of time. These are realities of the game.
Do not buy unless you understand these above factors.

Ark is an interesting survival game and construction sandbox.  Once you learn [Simple Bed] the game gets significantly easier.
Problems;
0) "E" Players curse the E button.  There is nothing quite like dismounting your flyers becuase E is directly next to W.  Mounting an animal should not be tied to the "Use" Key.  Even on land mounts you try to close a door and end up dismounting.  This was not really though out.  Most Controler games dont assocate Mount and Use under the same button.  It is frustrating and you will Curse the "Use Key" in due time.
1) [Center Map] once a group secures the entrances to the underworld they own the server.  They can simply monopolize the rare drops and reasources at that point.  This forces survivors to join the dominate tribe or be fodder.  On servers where the players have not yet figured this out, it is only a matter of time.  There should be a no build radious around the entrances that is twice the size of the max turret range or they need to create more entrances.
2) There is no warning before being blasted out of the sky with turrets.  Players have an option to set a warning but this is broken logic and not the defalt.  First person shooters are limited to tunnel vision.  This means limited perception which most games balance out with in game warnings. This is extreamly frusterating considering the amount of invested time into mounts.
3) Occasional DC due to lost server connection or fatal game errors usually cause you to fail tames or pass out durring an attack, which is never good for survival.
4) The snap building system needs work to ensure that structures are uniform in construction from start to finish.  Too often one floor or wall will not line up even though they started from the same structure.  This is because there are 6 wall/ceiling snap locations to each cube when the programers could get away with 3.  The other three snap locations could be covered by the connecting cubes like most other sand box games.  I am sure everyone has seen the two walls in the same place or stacked ceilings.  Add an additional 6 potental snap locations of pillers and it is no wander that the AI cannot maintain uniform building. Reducing the Smap location would reduce render time and lag without changing designe.
5) Also every contstruction piece needs a rotated or inverted function with a key command.  It is annoying trying to get a roof or wall to snap in the way you want it when it will not flip or roatate.  Also, when snapping pillars to an overhanging ceilings the piller should always start snapped just below the ceiling.  The pillar should not stick through the ceiling at all.
6) Construction pieces need to cut into terrain.  Most survivors will utilize natrual features such as cliffs or caves to protect thier base.  It is counter productive to have a wall with an opening in it becase the construction peice was obstructed, or too high off the ground when it is cutting throw a slope.  Pillers can penetrate the ground so should walls and foundations (Within Reason).
7) I normally don't like to demean anyone, but whomever wrote the Plumbing & Electrical was absent of all logic and common sence.  (In a snap building AI) to have walls one hight and Plumbing & Electrical a different hight is idiotic  Vertical peices should be exactly 2 walls and diaginals should end at 1x1  Currently it's not possible to combind electrical or plumbing systems that were not part of the intial snap, and they dont snap in-line with the structure.  A far more effectice method would be replace the Diaginal with a "soft line."  The coding is not that difficalt.  Users sellect two hard snap points and a soft line connects them using more mats the greater the distance between the points.
8) The colision engine needs to prevent Animals from sticking their head through walls and ceilings to prevent in-building agrros/raider kills.   Also it would be nice if our survivors did not fall through our beds and floors.  It is kind of broken when they fall through a tree house or dround under their boats after logging off.  It would also be nice to turn off the teleport function on some beds to make them cosmetic and keep the teleport map from being cluttered.
9) The boats  need a bump effect so that they can push unattended boats out of the way.  Also boats should not be able to push throw sea walls.  Forcing a turret throw a wall to kill all of the tames is broken.
10) A setting on the doors to close after 20/30 seconds would resolve a sigificant amount of problems.  If you are DCed from the server for 20 min while a door was open and have to go to work, that leaves your base open to raiders and hostile animals all day.
11) The fact that resource do no respawn around a foundation radius needs to be hammered into new players a little better.  For example a pop up warning could be used whenever a player attempts to place a foundation near an iron vein or atleast add it to the tips in the loading screen.
12) C4 and Granades need to be considered (Players)  It is obserdly broken to strap C4 to wild dodos and drop them on a base until the defences are distroyed.
13) Allowing DoDo Rexs to be summoned anywhere like base bombs is stupid.  They are raider candy which is worse than game exploits.
14)  About the most broken thing I have seen is = Rather than fixing code, the Devs have announce that utilizing some game features beyond their intend perpous is against the rules?  This is bad form in any gaming system.  There is a basic concept called the "Black Blade" that can be applied to just about everything.  It states that if a system is exploitable than all parties are required to paticipated to remain competitive.  In a Game it is foolish to establish rules against exploiting a game feature vs rectifying the issue with code, because says (dont do some thing) requires the Devs to provide fair and impartal GMs to investigated every potental occurance of the violation.  On ARK there is no way to police such a system fairly and as YouTube videos have shown ARK GMs are not always impartal or fair.  Nothing agaist ARK GMs but they do not have the tools or man hours to "Affirm each violation" and avoid arbitrarily punishing on a techicality.  Additional punishing a whole tribe over indiviuals is anything but justice.
15) Promoting compentions is good.  Promoting Greifing only gets players to leave your game and not buy your DLC. Rewarding Raiders with EXP for killing Dinos Set to passive is counter porductive to promoting game play.  You only support Greifers that way.  Players should LOSE x2 EXP for killing Dinos on Passive.  This would allow raids but deture complete wipes.  If some one wanted to kill a passive then they would have to pay for it.  Jumping servers to farm underdeveloped tribes would become counter productive, and thus allow players to find servers where they can build / survive.  Every player who rage quits your game will never buy a DLC packet.
16) False Possitive review???? Really?  Every gamer worth his or her salt can spot a series of false reviews.  A game Dev that resorts to padding their review numbers only succeds in deminstrating thier despertation.  If your GMs are making false accounts with free game passes just to post a fake review, than they cant be doing their job to enforce your rules can they?
17) Paid DLC is fine but not during Early Access.  Players base their views and ratings on the understanding that the game is still under development.  If you want Paid DLC thats fine but make the game Full Release.  The down side is that (at that point) the issues that I have pointed out here are no longer development bugs, they become Game Flaws.
This game has a lot of potental, but it will not amount to that potental if the Devs continue to cut corners.  Fix the mistakes, release the game, and be worthy of the reviews of your players.

Warframe is between a good game and a bad game.  So it's not for everyone.  It takes a page from older faster paced videogames from the 90's era in terms of speed, games like doom and quake.  Warframe is heavily gameplay focused and so might be hard for new players.  The game is fast and if you are new and kinda on the slow side it can be a bit frustrating without mods.
It's a game that begins to deflate quickly because there is a huge lack of content and the missions are highly repetitive.  That being said, for solo play the best missions in the game are spy missions, then survival, followed by excavation and defense.  Rescue can be good if you do short missions (specifically planet sedna, sector naga).
If you don't mind a first person shooter with old style RPG grinding then you should check out warframe.
General tips to enjoy warframe:
-If you need help with a mission go to recruit
-Always host your own mission if you don't want to deal with frame requirements (aka people kicking you for not having mesa/mag/frost/etc).
-You can get platinum by doing vault runs and selling rare mods or by doing void key missions for certain parts like soma barrel (t4 interception).  It will allow you to buy weapon slots (most important imho) and a couple warframe slots.
-Run then hold slide and jump to do forward flips it's all around better then coptering/needing specific weapon to copter.  Coptering is taking advantage of forward momentum bug when jumping and using the air attack mid air.
And one last link for everything you need to know about warframe so you can look it up when needed.
