0) "E" Players curse the E button.  There is nothing quite like dismounting your flyers becuase E is directly next to W.  Mounting an animal should not be tied to the "Use" Key.  Even on land mounts you try to close a door and end up dismounting.  This was not really though out.  Most Controler games dont assocate Mount and Use under the same button.  It is frustrating and you will Curse the "Use Key" in due time.
1) [Center Map] once a group secures the entrances to the underworld they own the server.  They can simply monopolize the rare drops and reasources at that point.  This forces survivors to join the dominate tribe or be fodder.  On servers where the players have not yet figured this out, it is only a matter of time.  There should be a no build radious around the entrances that is twice the size of the max turret range or they need to create more entrances.
2) There is no warning before being blasted out of the sky with turrets.  Players have an option to set a warning but this is broken logic and not the defalt.  First person shooters are limited to tunnel vision.  This means limited perception which most games balance out with in game warnings. This is extreamly frusterating considering the amount of invested time into mounts.
3) Occasional DC due to lost server connection or fatal game errors usually cause you to fail tames or pass out durring an attack, which is never good for survival.
4) The snap building system needs work to ensure that structures are uniform in construction from start to finish.  Too often one floor or wall will not line up even though they started from the same structure.  This is because there are 6 wall/ceiling snap locations to each cube when the programers could get away with 3.  The other three snap locations could be covered by the connecting cubes like most other sand box games.  I am sure everyone has seen the two walls in the same place or stacked ceilings.  Add an additional 6 potental snap locations of pillers and it is no wander that the AI cannot maintain uniform building. Reducing the Smap location would reduce render time and lag without changing designe.
5) Also every contstruction piece needs a rotated or inverted function with a key command.  It is annoying trying to get a roof or wall to snap in the way you want it when it will not flip or roatate.  Also, when snapping pillars to an overhanging ceilings the piller should always start snapped just below the ceiling.  The pillar should not stick through the ceiling at all.
6) Construction pieces need to cut into terrain.  Most survivors will utilize natrual features such as cliffs or caves to protect thier base.  It is counter productive to have a wall with an opening in it becase the construction peice was obstructed, or too high off the ground when it is cutting throw a slope.  Pillers can penetrate the ground so should walls and foundations (Within Reason).
7) I normally don't like to demean anyone, but whomever wrote the Plumbing & Electrical was absent of all logic and common sence.  (In a snap building AI) to have walls one hight and Plumbing & Electrical a different hight is idiotic  Vertical peices should be exactly 2 walls and diaginals should end at 1x1  Currently it's not possible to combind electrical or plumbing systems that were not part of the intial snap, and they dont snap in-line with the structure.  A far more effectice method would be replace the Diaginal with a "soft line."  The coding is not that difficalt.  Users sellect two hard snap points and a soft line connects them using more mats the greater the distance between the points.
8) The colision engine needs to prevent Animals from sticking their head through walls and ceilings to prevent in-building agrros/raider kills.   Also it would be nice if our survivors did not fall through our beds and floors.  It is kind of broken when they fall through a tree house or dround under their boats after logging off.  It would also be nice to turn off the teleport function on some beds to make them cosmetic and keep the teleport map from being cluttered.
9) The boats  need a bump effect so that they can push unattended boats out of the way.  Also boats should not be able to push throw sea walls.  Forcing a turret throw a wall to kill all of the tames is broken.
10) A setting on the doors to close after 20/30 seconds would resolve a sigificant amount of problems.  If you are DCed from the server for 20 min while a door was open and have to go to work, that leaves your base open to raiders and hostile animals all day.
11) The fact that resource do no respawn around a foundation radius needs to be hammered into new players a little better.  For example a pop up warning could be used whenever a player attempts to place a foundation near an iron vein or atleast add it to the tips in the loading screen.
12) C4 and Granades need to be considered (Players)  It is obserdly broken to strap C4 to wild dodos and drop them on a base until the defences are distroyed.
13) Allowing DoDo Rexs to be summoned anywhere like base bombs is stupid.  They are raider candy which is worse than game exploits.
14)  About the most broken thing I have seen is = Rather than fixing code, the Devs have announce that utilizing some game features beyond their intend perpous is against the rules?  This is bad form in any gaming system.  There is a basic concept called the "Black Blade" that can be applied to just about everything.  It states that if a system is exploitable than all parties are required to paticipated to remain competitive.  In a Game it is foolish to establish rules against exploiting a game feature vs rectifying the issue with code, because says (dont do some thing) requires the Devs to provide fair and impartal GMs to investigated every potental occurance of the violation.  On ARK there is no way to police such a system fairly and as YouTube videos have shown ARK GMs are not always impartal or fair.  Nothing agaist ARK GMs but they do not have the tools or man hours to "Affirm each violation" and avoid arbitrarily punishing on a techicality.  Additional punishing a whole tribe over indiviuals is anything but justice.
15) Promoting compentions is good.  Promoting Greifing only gets players to leave your game and not buy your DLC. Rewarding Raiders with EXP for killing Dinos Set to passive is counter porductive to promoting game play.  You only support Greifers that way.  Players should LOSE x2 EXP for killing Dinos on Passive.  This would allow raids but deture complete wipes.  If some one wanted to kill a passive then they would have to pay for it.  Jumping servers to farm underdeveloped tribes would become counter productive, and thus allow players to find servers where they can build / survive.  Every player who rage quits your game will never buy a DLC packet.
16) False Possitive review???? Really?  Every gamer worth his or her salt can spot a series of false reviews.  A game Dev that resorts to padding their review numbers only succeds in deminstrating thier despertation.  If your GMs are making false accounts with free game passes just to post a fake review, than they cant be doing their job to enforce your rules can they?
17) Paid DLC is fine but not during Early Access.  Players base their views and ratings on the understanding that the game is still under development.  If you want Paid DLC thats fine but make the game Full Release.  The down side is that (at that point) the issues that I have pointed out here are no longer development bugs, they become Game Flaws.
This game has a lot of potental, but it will not amount to that potental if the Devs continue to cut corners.  Fix the mistakes, release the game, and be worthy of the reviews of your players.

Warframe is how a free to play game should be. You can get absolutely everything in the game without spending a dime but only putting hard work into it.
The movement is really fun because of the sliding and the frontflipping and whatnot but it can also be a bit buggy sometimes.
The combat is really well executed with incredibly balanced weapons, incredible combos and flashy effects. You can also upgrade your weapons to your liking and playstyle.
There are different classes (Warframes) that you can unlock by either working hard or being a little wuss and paying for them. All classes are unique and powerful if used right.
No matter how much fun I've had with the game alone, I do not believe I would've played as much and have as much fun if I didn't co-op with my pals. It's filled with laughs and good teamwork.
TL;DR Warframe is bloody amazing with all content being unlockable for free, amazing combat and really decent co-op.

Cons:
-Loading takes a lifetime. I cannot stress this enough. I have an 8-core CPU 3.6Ghz, 10Gbs RAM (I know it could be more), but it takes 5-20 minutes to load a game. You got to be kidding me. Probably the biggest reason to make me stop playing.
-Resourses are not well used for RAM and CPU power (GPU can be fine depending on settings)
-Massive updates weekly with little to no changes to gameplay.
-Dinos are seriously dumb. Getting chased by a Carnosauria, just hop on this large rock and shoot it with a bow. It will just try to run up the same place it has been. Sarcosuchus on your tail? just stand behind a 8inch wide tree and stab it with a stick until it is dead. The dino ai's need a lot of work with knowing what to do in the terrain.
-Character progression is lacking.. "Yay, I can hold my breath for a few more seconds." seems like they could get more creative with how it works.
-Tamed Dinos WILL slow you down. I have 5 raptors following me and Freddy gets stuck on some driftwood and now I need to go back and free him... REALLY?
-You can only have one saved game per map... The save game system for this NEEDS to be changed.
Pros:
-Graphics are stunning
-Survival is a true factor, super easy to venture to far into an area you haven't been yet get murdered by dinos and lose your stuff. Also food and water are a constant need.
-Combat, although fairly simple, is smooth (some dumb ai bugs that will be discussed later though...)
-Multiplayer communities can be great. I know a few people that have spent 100s of hours on a server with groups of people and enjoy it.
-Dinos are super magestic and look realistic. There have been times that I've been walking in the jungle at night, see a rex turn and run toward me, and I literally scream.
-Crafting makes sense and is done well enough. Adds a lot of depth.

When you release a paid "Early Access" version of a game, the people that buy it support you financially with the agreement that you will work on and finish the game. Its a system that can really help small developers get their games out there. So its expected of you to actually finish the game before you start working on something else that you can charge people for. So when you release a paid DLC in the middle of developing a game that you have promised to work on until its finished, you are slapping everyone who supported you in the face. Its sad that the creators of Ark took advantage of the Early Access system, I really liked the game, but this practice is anti-consumer and if this is tolerated then more and more developers will do it.

Well I just cant believe in the turnaround of reviews for this.
I personally think ARK is potentially a great game.  A Good game as it stands, but potentially could be a great game if they tweak out all the bugs.
For a Year the Reviews on Ark were overwhelmingly positive. Wild Card were pushing all the right buttons and people were happy with the progress.  It seemed that we had found developers who were finally not rushing things for the quick buck, but taking there time fixing bugs and slowly improving optimization while at the same time constantly adding new features and content into the game.
However since the release of Scorched Earth understandably people feel betrayed by the company that shone bright for over a year.
How can a company move from a main focus of a core game and build, release and charge for an expansion for a game that has not been finished.
That would be like me writing a book and then deciding to write the sequel and release it while only the first 8 chapters of the original are written it makes no sense and I hope you have not breached the Steam Terms and Conditions with Early Access or you will lose more money in court cases than you ever made for releasing it in the first place.
But that is a problem from another day.  On another note.  I would ask the Devs to come forth and release a statement explaining there intent and reasoning behind Scorched Earth and why it took priority over the core game?
We may not like there response but  least they will get part of the respect I once had for them back.  We are all human and we all make mistakes, but speculating wont bring the truth.
And for that I am not recommending this game simply because until they release a statement I wont be able to know if they secretly are working on a second paid expansion prior to releasing this game.
I am running my own Unofficial server: 193.111.184.44:7877 for any who want to try the game but I would not recommend buying the expansion as after all this is still an early access game.

Details:
So I started playing ARK back in June 2015.
I bought the game four or five days after early access launch.
Compared to today the game had a lot more bugs back then
(e.g. damaging creatures through walls, removing bottom pillars
and the structures above wont crash, and so on...).
We started playing on a official PvP-EU server with over 200ms latency!!
With such high latencies Scorpions and Sabretooths were so easy to knock out with fists!
Back then it was usually that the game was updated at least twice or more per day.
After one of those countless patches, we weren't able to
enter our house. We were still in the same tribe and our structures
were also named by us - but there was no way in or out
without pin codes (luckily we added them before!) Just a few
minutes later we realised that we can't build on "our" area anymore.
We decided to write in the official Steam Discussions to see if there
are other players having the same problem...but we were the only one.
Within one hour Jat - the community manager himself - contacted us and
offered his help! He spent over an hour to remove our old structures and
helped us to rebuild a new one. The way Jat was helping us was so entertaining,
that was one of the best moments I had with this game!

Ark: Survival Evolved. The name of this game reminds me of the much older title "Halo: Combat Evolved." Unfortunately, this game has not delivered the same sort of revolutionary gameplay and endless fun that the original Halo was known for. The claim that this game is an evolution of a genre like Halo was is false. Ark shouldn't remind people of the greatness of a classic shooter with its name because it is simply not fun nor a timeless classic in its current state. The game is buggy, poorly optimized, needlessly difficult at times, and the developers have seemingly kept the game in Early Access to shove more of the same down our throats with $$$paid$$$ DLC. I have played this game for over 3 0 0 hours - weeks of my life have been spent enduring low framerates and stuttering on a gaming PC that laughs at the recommended hardware for most other titles. I held out hope for so long that Ark would eventually be improved by Studio Wildcard, but Wildcard has focused simply on adding content instead of actually focusing on the core of the game to make it more enjoyable. Don't get me wrong - the updates adding new crafting items and dinosaurs are much appreciated. I think it's great that a studio is willing to make so much content for a game. Sadly, the game still doesn't engage me. I've come out of the gaming honeymoon phase and now my eyes are open to the needy mess this game is. I want to love this game, but the lack of effort to fix the glaring issues with playability just irks me. I get excited for the dinosaurs like the Titanosaur and the features like variable-length rope bridges, but then I get in game and watch as I struggle to maintain 40 FPS, endlessly get killed by various species of carnivorous creatures that don't attack each other, and ultimately rage at the tedium of force feeding my dinos huge stacks of meat or berries one click at a time instead of having a good time. This game desperately needs optimization, an overhaul of the UI and a revision to AI of the wild dinos to be fun again.

My friends and i have enjoyed ark immensely, the vanilla game (no mods) is hard without being brutal. The devs give what they have offered, although the tiem frame they announce changes based on problems, or more easily finished projects that they can pump out for their next patch. Dont fall for the anti-hype about the DLC, people are only angry because the devs are thinking ahead and doing something different. Am i happy about a DLC before 'release'? No. But the game is MORE than playable, and so is the DLC. DLC does not mean the main game suddenly stops getting updates, and jsu tbecause the DLC is released doesnt mean its going to not get any in the future. The DLC in my eyes is a fundraiser for the project, because this game doesnt have a subscription their budget is ENTIRELY dependant on new players buying the game OR dlcs... and since most of the people writing negative reviews PROBABLY enjoy the game and want more content 'for free', they are only shooting themselves by giving such a great dev team and game crappy reviews. Less people buying the game = less money flow, which means stopping development sooner.
Overall gameplay is smoothe, i cant say much for pvp since i run a fairly small server and recently turned on PVE (we're all in the same tribe anyways) to stop friendly fire on our own dinos. As such i will NOT give an opinion on PVP.
PVE content is coming in nicely, though i would like to see unique drops off bosses that are not just cosmetic and/or full cosmetic sets that you can fight bosses for (armor skins). Alphas seem to not be as good as they used to, but offer a semi-exciting 'can i beat this?'
My only major complaint gameplay wise is the water. for as many awesome water dinos as are in the game, there really isnt a point in getting a big ovean critter. its a massive resource sink (i cant imagine on a full PVP server where people can kill your dinos and it can take 18+hours to tame something), and with no other 'big' islands to go to, they are basically just farming mules. This i hope will be allieviated some with the release of Procedurally Generated maps.
God job devs, ignore the haters and keep going. Release more decent quality DLC if you have to, i want to see ark keep going for a LONG time!

I don't think it's good to have a game which takes 10-30 hours to open up, even if the game is excellent. A structured single player campaign of 3-5 hours which gives players a boost in resources to start would be great imo to cut that setup time down and give new players a heads up for what to expect and how to play the game. I'm not sure what all the whining is about.
Yes, the game is still in alpha.  Yes, it still has bugs.  And yes, they released a DLC for a game that's in alpha and still has bugs.  But all along the way they've continued to add new content and while some of it is buggy, the technical merit behind what they've accomplished is pretty impressive.  There aren't too many games out there that can touch the depth of the gameplay, and fewer still who can do that while making it look as good as this game does.
The way I see it, the DLC that everyone's butthurt about is pretty over the top.  It's so different from the base game that it's almost a game in its own right.  Most of the content and gameplay is completely new to Ark.  That obviously took a lot of time and effort.  Why shouldn't they charge more for it?  Here's the other side to the coin:  I have about 1,300 hours logged in Ark.  For a measly $30.  I'm about to buy Scorched Earth for another $20.  Even if I bought the DLC and never played Ark or the DLC again, I will have spent 2.6 cents per hour for some of the best entertainment I've ever had.  Wildcard is still adding features to this game and at $50, I've still paid less than I would for many games of similar scope and quality that are in full release with *no* more features to come.
Maybe people don't understand the development cycle:  They're still adding features to the base game and until they're done doing that, it will continue to be in alpha.  When it gets to beta, they'll work on squashing most of the bugs.  But even in Alpha, Ark is more complete and playable than many games in full release.  When you look at other games of similar scale that are still in alpha, the expense and playability are far better (Looking at you, Star Citizen).
I place my full trust and faith in Wildcard and give this game my wholehearted recommendation.

I've now sunk 60 hours into ARK: Survival Evolved, and I have some things to say. I'm going to break out of my usual review mold and just list the pros and cons of ARK (as of 9/21/16)
Edit (11/19/16): More than 100 hours in and 2 months later, I can honestly say this review still holds true on most counts. The one that has changed is that they have added options to alter in game lighting to somewhat alleviate the glare issues. However, even these options do not 100% fix the insane levels of reflectiveness of certain textures.
- One of the most complete "alpha" games I have seen on Steam. One might even say this is the poster-child for what all early access games should look like. For the most part, it's feature complete and playable (but not functional, more on that later.)
- One of the best co-op games out there. I've been playing mostly with a buddy, and this has become our default go-to game.
- Lots of content for the price. I've played 60 hours on one character, and I'm not even halfway to max level. The basic gameplay of slowly building up a base and army of dino's is fun, and has yet to get old. New tools/weapons/etc. unlock just often enough to make me want to keep playing just to see what's next!
-
- Don't even bother if you don't have a gaming specific rig with at least 16gb of memory. Both I and the friend I play with have current year graphics cards and 16gb of RAM and still cannot play on higher than low-to-mid settings without experiencing massive frame drops. I imagine it's unplayable with even mid-tier pc's. Even with that much RAM, memory spikes will STILL sometimes crash our clients or create Windows errors.
- The bloom is bright enough to blind Ray Charles. Seriously, J.J. Abrams must be in charge of the lighting effects at Wild Card, because the brightness is obscene. While the sun is out in game, don't bother trying to look at anything even mildly reflective, like say your map, water (which is prevalent), or even dinosaur SKIN. You literally have to spend the morning portions of the game staring at the ground, or be blinded. There is a way to turn the light effects down or off via console commands, but honestly players should not have to do that. With how many graphics options are available, why isn't there a slider for this? (Edit 11/19/16: This issue has been reduced due to added control of lighting in the options menu. However, I have not removed it because glare, while reduced, is still a problem.)
- Glitches are prevalent, and game ruining. Your character will get stuck on flat terrain, and you will have to wait until you starve to death or have a friend kill you. That is, if you don't clip straight through the ground and get stuck halfway in/out of it. Also be careful if you kill a dino that you were hunting, sometimes their corpses fly into space and disapear for no apparent reason. A dilo (a small carnivore) might clip inside your Triceratops and kill it from the inside where you can't fight it. Not to mention, sometimes bigger carnivore's will spawn a hundred feet above your base and air-drop in to destroy everything you've ever loved.
- The UI (User Interface) is garbage. Everything from inventory management to controlling dinosaurs is a hassle. Crafting and inventory are on separate menus for some reason, so constant switching back and forth is necessary. Pet dino's require you to set options for their behavior, but the options on the UI will sometimes change positions. This can result in situations where going to access a dino's inventory, the option for that changes to set it's aggression just as you click and the dino sprints off to kamikaze the nearest T-Rex. To help fix that, your character has the ability to 'whistle', and change the settings on all of your pet's within hearing at once. However, this often hurts more than helps since rarely do you want to set all of your dinosaurs to the same settings. Want to whistle for your carnivore pets to attack whatever you are? Oops! Your entire flock of dodo birds just got skooshed because they happened to be within earshot. You also accidently militarized those flying dinos you spent hours chasing down to tame! Now they're dead because you accidently sent them to fight sharks...
- Paid DLC before any of the above has been fixed. Look, I get it; development is expensive, and DLC can bring in some extra cash to keep the train moving. But when I have to destroy my base for the third time because a pet dino clipped under the foundation, I wonder if spending more money on this game is worth it. Every time ARK is patched, I feel as though it's no closer to leaving early access. In fact, some of the patches are actively making the game worse! While I don't think the Scorched Earth content should be free, like some do, I do think it was a bit too early to put it out.
- The people who play on public servers are jerks. Every single PvP enabled server has one or two main clans, and if you aren't in them you might as well be dino-poo. Through an exploit in the graphics options, players from the big-time clans are able to fly around and spot bases of other players. They will not hesitate to destroy any base you've built and kill any dino's you've tamed, essentially undoing dozens of real-life hours of work in minutes. They can even do this while you are offline! The only way to stop the abuse? Join their clan, of course! This ensures that one or two clans will always be the most powerful, and is not fun for new players just trying to build up.
Don't buy this right now unless you are a huge fan of survival games, or have friends to play with. You will also need a good sense of humor to laugh your way through the jank and glitches. ARK has promise to be an amazing game when it's polished, but that doesn't seem to be Wild Card's top priority.
I give it: Dodo out of Quetzal.

About a year ago I posted a review of the game with a positive score. When said review was posted the game only cost $20, which was a great price for the then state of the game, as well as the current state of the game. ARK has never, and most likely will never be a stable/optimized enough game to merit a $60 pricetag, and Wildcard should feel ashamed for trying to ask AAA game prices for such unoptimized PC garbage. DO TAKE INTO ACCOUNT I HAVE ONLY EVER PLAYED ON PRIVATELY OWNED PVE SERVERS. However, with all of this said, the game is extremely ambitious, and for what it is I love the game. I play games particularly because I enjoy them, regardless of whatever the current state of the company and such is, so with all of this said, let's dive into the pro's and cons, eh?
Pros:
- A multitude of varied prehistoric animals, including dinosaurs, invertebrates, amphibians, and so on. Each dinosaur has its own specific strengths and weaknesses, with some having their own specific utility, such as Castoroides (Beavers) being used for acquisition of wood.
- Varied weapons from the simple crossbow to the flamethrower. Most likely has a weapon to suit your playstyle.
- Continual updates and potential future dinos and so on being released.
- Intuitive building system which allows for the construction of intricate buildings. This is further enhanced by the addition of building mods such as Structures+ and CKF.
- Fishing! (I don't care what anyone says. This is a pro for me.)
- Seamless integration of mods from the Steam Workshop, as well as server configuration for mod items, making their management/balancing a breeze.
- The ability to take your anger towards all trees out on the trees in-game by punching them until you acquire wood.
- Beautifully crafted landscapes which make for some extremely picturesque views.
- Graphically pleasing (Obviously goes with the landscapes one, right?)
- Exploration is heavily emphasized in this game in that the game itself has a multitude of underwater places to explore, the entirety of the ocean (if it can be called that) around the map. Multiple caves and so on to explore as well.
Cons:
- Horrible Customer Support from Wildcard Studios. Including refusal to acknowledge relatively common issues, no support for the awful network performance of their game (even on private servers).
- Price increase. From $20 to $60?!?! HOW IS THIS JUSTIFIABLE? I'm assuming Wildcard has obtained so much money during early access that they no longer feel the need for the game to remain $20, and any more sales now are just extra cash grabs.
- DLC Development whilst in Early Access. There's a whole legal battle debate and whatnot here, however even though that is the case it still comes off as somewhat fishy.
- Wildcard Studios. They as a whole are a con themselves. I can't really say more than what I've said already.
- Maps which were originally mods (The Center and Ragnarok) being better than the actual maps created by the development team. This is honestly just sad when a mod is better than supposed "AAA" material.
- Lackluster in-game music for battles and so on. Most likely there is a way to change them/mods to change them, but eh.
Conclusion:
This game is akin to what Minecraft is in that it allows you to create whatever you like, with seamless mod integration. With friends on private servers it's a blast when anyone wants to play (outside of the resource gathering at times). I've only ever played this game exclusively with groups of my friends, and therefore have only ever derived enjoyment from it.
Is it worth $60?: ♥♥♥♥ no. This game has never, and most likely never will be optimized and stable enough to warrant an AAA pricetag (though neither are most AAA games). Game is a buggy piece of unoptimized PC garbage, but the fun factor alone warrants a $30 pricetag, possibly $40 pricetag. Personally I've played the game over 700 hours, so I can't really say that it's not been worth it for me.

I'm not sure what all the whining is about.
Yes, the game is still in alpha.  Yes, it still has bugs.  And yes, they released a DLC for a game that's in alpha and still has bugs.  But all along the way they've continued to add new content and while some of it is buggy, the technical merit behind what they've accomplished is pretty impressive.  There aren't too many games out there that can touch the depth of the gameplay, and fewer still who can do that while making it look as good as this game does.
The way I see it, the DLC that everyone's butthurt about is pretty over the top.  It's so different from the base game that it's almost a game in its own right.  Most of the content and gameplay is completely new to Ark.  That obviously took a lot of time and effort.  Why shouldn't they charge more for it?  Here's the other side to the coin:  I have about 1,300 hours logged in Ark.  For a measly $30.  I'm about to buy Scorched Earth for another $20.  Even if I bought the DLC and never played Ark or the DLC again, I will have spent 2.6 cents per hour for some of the best entertainment I've ever had.  Wildcard is still adding features to this game and at $50, I've still paid less than I would for many games of similar scope and quality that are in full release with *no* more features to come.
Maybe people don't understand the development cycle:  They're still adding features to the base game and until they're done doing that, it will continue to be in alpha.  When it gets to beta, they'll work on squashing most of the bugs.  But even in Alpha, Ark is more complete and playable than many games in full release.  When you look at other games of similar scale that are still in alpha, the expense and playability are far better (Looking at you, Star Citizen).
I place my full trust and faith in Wildcard and give this game my wholehearted recommendation.

I've had Ark: Survival Evolved for a long time, but I have only been able to play it a little due to horrible optimization issues. I would assume that these have been fixed somewhat since the last time I opened the game - at least, I would hope so - but when I tried to play it before it would take TWO WHOLE HOURS just to get in. I wasn't even playing on a server or anything. It would take that long just to get the game to load - and I couldn't do anything else on my computer while it was loading. Once I was in, the lag was annoying but not too bad as long as I kept the game on medium-high settings (was obscene if i turned the graphics all the way up but that's not unusual for my computer with games like this), but the loading screens were so horrible I eventually stopped playing the game entirely. If you are interested in this game and don't have a decent gaming computer, I would be wary. The game has gotten better since I purchased it, but optimization is still pretty bad despite how long the game's been in Early Access. It's a fun game but if you aren't sure if your computer can handle the strain I wouldn't buy it until the optimization has improved drastically. Anyway, here's the rest of my review!
PROS:
- Diverse creatures, many of which you can tame. Each of them have their own interesting points and ways to improve your ability to survive on Ark. Plenty of dinosaurs, which is great, but also plenty of more unusual prehistoric and fictional creatures, which I appreciate. They can be your pets, guards, resource harvesters, warriors, steeds, and much more. The tameable creatures are definitely what makes this game so interesting and appealing.
- There are lots of things to craft and build in Ark. If you can get the resources, you can build pretty awesome bases.
- Lots of different ways you can be creative; aside from what you can build, you can also give your tamed creatures warpaint to make them stand out from the rest.
- Beautiful scenery and lots of stuff to explore.
- Very mod-friendly, with some mods that have even been officially added to the game as free DLC, like the Center map, Primitive+, and an upcoming mod where you can play as the creatures of Ark.
CONS:
- Like I mentioned before, optimization is poor. Very buggy. It's easy to get the impression that the devs are more interested in adding more stuff to the game - new creatures, new craftables, new game features and contests, even a paid DLC completely separate from the base game - that they're not paying as much attention to fixing what already exists ingame. Some of the stuff that they've done, like the PvP contests with real cash prizes and the Scorched Earth DLC, seem like things that would have been better done after the base game is already finished, rather than in the middle of development. While I love seeing new creatures as much as the next person, the emphasis on adding as much new stuff as possible when the game is still laggy and cumbersome as hell has gotten a little frustrating over time. There's a lot that can be said about adding a paid DLC to an unfinished game, but that's already been discussed to death in recent reviews.
- This game is NOT friendly to solo players. When playing in singleplayer I got the impression that very little was done to make this game better for people who don't have at least one person helping them. There's a lot of stuff that feels pretty impossible to access on your own. Taming anything remotely powerful takes an obscenely long time, in which you have to constantly feed, sedate, and defend a completely helpless animal. If you fail to keep it sedated or it gets killed, you have to start all over again. Even if you have taming time set on low, this is still a very tedious thing to do. Raising eggs can also require near constant attention for hours, and if you're a person who has other things to do in your life than play this game then you're gonna have a difficult time adding any powerful creatures to your roster, which makes it difficult to progress further. Nonviolent taming methods are also very awkward and tedious, I have found, as you basically have to follow a creature around and feed it, but if you get too close or something else attacks you may have to start all over again. All of this is easier if you have friends to help you, but if you don't you'll quickly find that making progress in the game is an enormous grind. Personally I'm not a fan of mechanics where most of the difficulty comes from how time consuming it is.
- You can do a lot of things with building but it is at times very clunky and difficult to deal with. If the floors, walls, etc. were a little easier to integrate into the uneven landscape, that would be nice.
- Animal AI can be kinda dumb and you may spend a lot of time micromanaging your tames (especially larger dinos) as you travel because they'll get stuck behind stuff. A lot. It sucks when you lose your hard-earned dinos to completely avoidable dangers.
- This is just a nitpicky thing and won't be a con for everybody but the general appearance and movement of many dinos is pretty awkward. I cringe every time I see those messed up pterosaur wings. Flying animations in general are probably the most painful aspect of the game to look at as they are nearly always too slow to realistically keep the creature aloft. Newer dinos mostly look better anatomically and in terms of animation but several of the original ones could use a bit of work. Basically all of the dinosaurs were designed more to look cool than to be scientifically accurate, so if Jurassic Park-esque monsters are a pet peeve of yours, it's probably best to skip this game.
TL;DR: ARK: Survival Evolved has a lot of issues that need fixing and despite loving the concept of the game I was unable to have much fun actually playing it. Overall, the game has a lot of interesting points but certain aspects turn it into a grind, especially if you're playing singleplayer. It's definitely a game that requires a lot of time put into it to be rewarding, which means that if you're a casual player or if you're hampered by bugs and lag your experience can quickly turn sour. I would recommend it to people who like multiplayer, grindy survival, and have a good gaming computer and a lot of time on their hands. I would not recommend it to anyone else at this point, even though I do like the creatures a lot.
Review will change if any of the above problems are fixed.

This is a wonderful game and it's VERY reasonably priced. Assuming you like survival games, you'll get more play time out of this that you would from a $60 game. I've got a little over 500 hours now and I got this game on sale for $20. Defintely the most well put together early access game I've played. With that being said, not everything is great, so I'll make chart of the pros and cons.
PROS:
- Genuinely Entertaining
- Great Longevity
- Wonderful, but tedious, building.
(Trust me it's worth itm because you can make almost anything)
- Constant Updates
- Free DLCS so far (excluding Scorched Earth, which I'll touch on soon)
CONS:
- Still in Alpha so bugs, glitches and lag are annoying.
(It's much better now, minimal problems but still worth mentioning)
- Building can be very tedious.
I guess another con could be the almost inevitability of getting thrashed by a warlike tribe on PvP, but that can be remedied by playing on PvE. Other than those things, this game is great and doesn't deserve the low ratings it's getting.
In regards to Scorched Earth, I completely agree with how unorthodox it was for them to release a DLC for an INCOMPLETE game. It's strange, suspicious and somewhat disrespectful to ask for more money when what we already payed for isn't done. I get it, completely. I understand people hating that, but you don't have to pay for it. It's not something you need to play the game or to thrive. So why so much hate? Don't get it and get over it.
On the other hand, this game is better than most survivals I've played and it was only $20 bucks, so whats the harm in making it a $40 game with almost double the content? It's totally reasonable, but once again, not mandatory. They've given us Primitive+ for free and added The Center Map for free. With Scorched Earth, consider it $20 for 3 DLCS. What's so bad about that?
I've said my peace. I hope people relax with the hate because it's not as bad people make it seen.
At the same time, I hope they don't do this again. FINISH the game we paid for then try to squeeze more out of us, please.
I apologize in advance for any typos.

This is the only game I've played consistently for the last two years. It's so content rich, with over 100 unique creatures that aren't just reskinned versions of each other, tons of things to craft, and infinite possibilities for base builds...I'm not often bored with it. Unofficial servers are still far better than official, they tend to have better communities and are faster paced, and I personally really enjoy single player.
I love the direction the game is going, the lore is surprisingly interesting- you learn about the ARK through finding explorer notes scavenger hunt style, and with every update they reveal more. The latest creatures have better models, animations and abilities, studio WC plans to give the old ones some TLC before the patch. As I said before, one of the coolest aspects about ARK is that the creatures are actually unique, most games with 100+ critters just have reskinned versions of already existing ones but these guys are actually different. The diplo isn't just a smaller bronto, it has its own niche, just like all the others, even the pachyrhinos are much different than the trikes. There's plenty of character customization, all though the player character models look a tad goofy, you can change your PC's hair, beard, etc.. (even the lady models can have beards).
Base building is incredible, and this is probably my favorite game for building in general. It's a simple system that's easy to make functial bases look like beautiful castles. Mods like Structures+ make this even better and really expand what you can do. There are platform saddles for creatures and boats that you can use to make mobile bases which I don't know of many other games that have that.
On a custom server, the breeding system is a lot of fun. I have mine set so it takes 1-3 hours for the creatures to mature, breeding for mutations is a lot of fun. You can get bright blue argents or green wolves that don't just look cool, they're powerful too.
After 1000+ hours, I still reccomend this game 10/10 IF your computer can handle it. I also reccomend the DLC, scorched earth, the map is a lot of fun and I get better FPS. The wyverns are one of my favorite mounts even with the flyer nerf, they're fun to raise to get perfect imprint in my opinion.
For reference I get around 40 frames with start up settings that limit some of the quality but still allow me to have high res textures and shadows, 1080p display, with this:
AMD Radeon R9 200 (MSi Gaming Edition)
AMD FX 6 core CPU
12 GB Ram

I highly reccomend this game for entertainment value; I haven't seen many reviews talking about singleplayer, which is where I've mostly been playing, and which would have been useful for me when I bought it, though.
This game is very obviously designed for multiplayer, with difficult tames made for more than one person to collaborate over. In singleplayer, I've found that the game only becomes possible by changing the settings for faster and easier tames, but since this is an option this isn't a huge disadvantage.
Since I've been playing on singleplayer, I haven't been affected by the new DLC at all, so I can't mention that. However, I've seen no drop in entertainment value for ARK - the devs have been regularly updating what they promised, including the new dinos (which is the game's primary draw for me), and even though they haven't met their deadlines the game is still progressing nicely.
I wouldn't reccomend this game in early access if you own a laptop or a low-performance PC, since it is yet to be optimised and won't run to its full potential on such devices. However, having experience with the better graphics settings I have to say that this game is absolutely stunning. The detail in the world is captivating; I could have played it for hours just for the view.
Pros:
- Stunning graphics and lighting.
- A huge variety in dinos to tame or escape.
- A number of smaller and larger goals that keep the game interesting (bosses, tricky or rare tames etc).
- Riding dinosaurs (this sold it to me from day one).
- It holds appeal for many different types of players; you can play it as a simple survival game, an RPG, play it for the final goals (bosses) or not worry about them at all, or to build some pretty nice bases.
- It looks as though it will have quite an interesting storyline if it's going to be revealed; there's obviously more to the setting than what your character knows.
Cons:
- It's very difficult to get started on normal settings, because of the time needed and everything you can die from.
- The game is unoptimised, and has difficulty maintaining a tolerable fps, although I hope this will be fixed in future.
- There are quite a few glitches, some of which can set you back quite a way with no fix.
- Certain goals are almost impossible on singleplayer.
All in all, I really enjoy this game and would highly reccomend it. However, it's still very obviously in early access, and this does affect gameplay. If you have a computer that would have difficulty running it, it would be better to wait until the game is fully optimised and in final release.

As I write this, ARK sits at 1,944 hours. It was supposed to be the first title I took to 2,000 and frankly, I don't see that happening now. I've purchased this game a total of 7 times (and given away 6 of them) and I still feel like I got my money's worth. I love what this game used to be, but I still cannot recommend it largely because of the direction it's going. No, this isn't about the DLC recently released - early access has long since stopped being a social contract and has metastized into a blank check of reduced responsibilities and expectations for developers to abuse. As such, I don't care about that (although on priciple it's wack).
What I care about is the fact that Wildcard has effectively done nothing but faff around and waste resources on side adventures that don't add value to ARK for the past 6-8 months (or more). All they do is add more dinos and talk about "eSport SOTF" and throw around large sums of cash.

= UI Improvements which were supposed to be "next patch sure thing" disappeared
= Motion sickness causing camera shake still an issue, despite their comments about it. I hate to take this attitude, but I really don't think they care that their game makes people ill or causes headaches.
= Modding scene is on life support, with almost all major mods transfering ownership to a few caretakers; although there are still a few good ones left. I can ride around naked on a giant Dodo so, you know, there's always that.
Eh, I had more, but I don't really care any more.

Wanted to start by saying this game has great potential. I love the dinosaurs and cooperative aspects of it. I only played on private servers as I'm not so much into PVP and that is a heavy aspect on the public servers. That will obviously color my opinion of the game.
On the highest settings, the environments and dinosaurs are beautiful, and I appreciate that they added an underwater ecosystem as well as a land one. There's a good base here for an engaging system of taming and breeding dinosaurs. Unfortunately, that's all it is: a barebones system. Taming dinosaurs is monotonous after the first few times, and passive taming is worse. Gathering is basic and grindy - even with dinosaurs to help - and you either eat what you gather or try to use it in a building system that functions in only the loosest sense of the word. Meanwhile the game is riddled with bugs, such as the one where your corpse falls through the world and you have no chance to recover anything in your inventory.
The free mods kept this game alive for me for a while, but the recently released paid DLC has put the nail in the coffin. The developer's refusal to finish the core game and actually do something about bugs/optimization prior to asking for more money says poor things about their future endeavors. It looks great visually, but the quality of life improvments included belong in the base game. The reskinned creatures, the wyverns (which were inspired by a FREE mod), the foxes - these can be a paid side option. But it shouldn't come out BEFORE the core game is functional and you absolutely shouldn't be able to take those things back to a server running the base game.

Update to review: Nearly 2 years on, with a couple of thousand more hours (non-Steam install) as a top-level veteran...
Pros:
+ Not limited to just one class and one build.  Craft more frames and take your pick of being a healer, a tank, a necromancer, a fire caster (etc.).
+ Slaughter enemies by the hundreds, with a wide variety of weapons that you can tailor to taste.
+ You can play it how you like: solo, public, or just with a group of your friends.
+ Still free to play, and you can trade items in-game instead of spending real money on "platinum" (which is used to buy inventory slots, cosmetics, etc.).
Cons:
- The developers are well-meaning but don't seem to understand the player experience of their own game so keep implementing poor design decisions that they subsequently have to roll back, and are notoriously prickly about criticism on the official forums.  The remaining playerbase that they choose to hear from reminds me of a sycophantic cult.
- Grindy, and seems to have become more so with the designers' poor choices.  RNG upon RNG and requiring repeating the same thing over and over again are poor substitutes for interesting content and good game design.
- A definite feel of quantity over quality; as others have noted, there are a ton of weapons in the game but most of them are very similar to one another and entirely disposable.  The continual powercreep, which is a result of their business model, only makes this worse.
- Not much for higher level players to do while waiting for new content, unless you want to participate in the hamster wheel RNG gimmicks that the devs have implemented.  Waste two hours of my life for no gain, or play something else and actualy enjoy it?  Tough one...
All in all, it's fair to say that eventually you'll understand all the criticisms that people have directed at this game.  You won't play it forever, but it's fun while it lasts and I would still recommend it.

A classic case of a game that "the more you put into it, the more you get out of it" - it's confusing to begin with, but invest a little time and effort on the excellent wikia as and when needed, and you'll reap the rewards.  It might be a little grindy, as people have said, but the actual gameplay is a lot of fun and there's always something to look forward to, a new goal to reach, a new warframe or weapon to try out.
This game ~really~ opens up when you go public multiplayer.  I was hesitant to play public games at first, but gave it a go when I found solo play to be dull, and haven't looked back since - the action is fast-paced (missions can be over in a matter of minutes), your fellow players are helpful and will save you when you're down if they can get to you in time, and it's insanely fun to work together to achieve the mission objective.  It's also enlightening to see how experienced players play their different frames, and immensely satisfying when you can synergise your playing style and your own frame's strengths and powers with those of your squad's.  Best of all, once you start crafting additional frames, you're no longer restricted in the type of role you can play.
The game server constantly comes up with alert missions, which are time limited in how long they're available for and deliver a reward upon completion.  This is the best - and sometimes only - way to obtain certain useful items, as well as creating a sense of a living, breathing game world in which you and your fellow warriors drop everything when the Lotus issues a call to arms.  Every once in a while a major event takes place (coinciding with the developers adding something major to the game), and it seems that it will then become part of the game's lore.  Once again, that "part of a living, breathing game world" thing.
It's just a shame that the slow pace of the solo introductory missions may put people off anything more than a cursory look at the game, but there's a large enough gamerbase that jumping into a public mission is rarely an issue.

i love this game; its fast, expansive and best of all: YOU DONT HAVE TO PAY AT ALL TO UNLOCK EVERY MOD, WARFRAME OR WEAPON IN THE GAME!!!!! though it will take a long time grinding away for materials it is possible to fully complete for free, and that brings me to the one real downside to the game; to get some of the better weapons you will have to grind a lot. but still...... fantastic
IN DEPTH REVIEW:
first of all you are going to grind wether you like it or not but you should know that's the case with every free to play game. of course the game isnt perfect but nothing is. but if you like a ton, and i mean a ton, of different ways to equip yourself this game will hook you due to its modding system. whenever you kill an enemy there's a slight chance they drop a mod wich you can equip on your frame, primary, secondary, melee or companion to make the item faster, stronger, give it more health or a larger magazine, shorter reload time you name it...... it is really satisfying to watch as you mod a weapon and see its base damage go from a couple hundred to maybe even twelve thousand damage in one shot with a 95% chance to fire two shots at once.
there is honestly no reason to not try this game because its a completely Free to play game in its purest form. in other words: every weapon that is obtainable by spending IRL money is also obtainable without paying at all. wether you have loads of time to play games everyday or only an hour or less each week this game always has something you can do.

Excellent game, with nice graphics and lots of content, which keeps changing and expanding. Even though there are repeatable missions, I keep having fun with them, because of multitude of other varieties in game, you can try out.

You don't NEED all those weapons (The starting Braton can be modded/forma'd/catalysted to handle whole game really, but it becomes the thing that the game is.  Now hopefully more and more content will be added.  To give us more to do other that get weapons/stuff just for the sake of it.  Unfortunatly the Devs lately have been wasting time with PVP and screwing with a star map that doesn't need screwing with.  Just make more maps/tiles/planets/enemies and we will be happy.  I would love to see more progression for progression sake rather than for RNG drops.
Everything about this game is great and no other game makes you feel like such a badass, a fantastic control system is the reason for this and it's only getting better.  Play this game for fantastic gunplay with (contrary to other reviews I'm seeing) a fantastic assortment of Weapons that all play very different.  Many games weapons are just re=skins but not here.
Then of course the Warframes, The grind is real but nothing feels as good as getting all your parts finally then having  "Ready to Collect" in your foundry, then going onto the field and seeing what powers you have, how they will come into play.  They make it very tactical.  There are many players who build one way per frame according to Meta.  Screw that, they can be a boring spreadsheet artist, I'm gonna have fun and use everything I have.
Conclusion, I Downloaded to just check it out, well I checked it allright.  Just for the gunplay variation alone I would recommend.

What ARK Survival Evolved game has in content and committed staff, it lacks in balancing and good decision making during development.
First off the Good:
Ark Survival Evolved has excellent single player and PVE gameplay, the game mechanics are well suited and the work you put into creating a town with a guild with different specialisations and jobs is rewarded excellently.
To Summarise:
The Good.
Graphics
Gameplay mechanics
Taming
Crafting
Engrams
Basically it has everything going for it for single-player content and has one of the most addictive and yet varied gameplay with huge longevity.
This game falls short in pvp, one of the most popular game modes currently out there.  If you wish to play pvp, do so on the survival of the fittest. Do not...  I repeat, DO NOT try and PVP or establish yourself on a pvp server, even with 50+ tribe members.
Arks excellent game mechanics backfire in pvp, creating a situation where it's not just hard, its impossible to play pvp against a currently established tribe on a pvp server.  I know from experience that 50+ members can be wiped out be one person and a base destroyed on a whim. Imagine if you were attacked by an entire tribe.
PVP based around longevity and continuing conflict is all about control of in-game items and mechanics in order to sustain both parties.  Its as if the dev team thought the idea behind pvp servers and then promptly abandoned the whole project.  Any disbelief in this fact can be remedied by a quick google search, with any remedies offered by commenters easily countered by the sheer number of people afflicted with this problem.
You just can't have a game mechanic where retaliation is not possible in a pvp game, its just silly.
An established tribe has the ability to outrange any defences and no matter what, eventually destroy a lesser tribes base.
I personally was lucky.  I had only invested a small amount of hours into the pvp server.  My tribe mates were not so lucky.  I can easily accept the release of a paid DLC on an early access game, what I cannot accept is just plain ignorance to a prevalent problem so many are having with this game. It has been designed to be self defeating.  This was one of two poor reviews i have ever given.

Hello gamers, this is my review of the game after more than 300hr game play. This is based on my opinion and experience in game.
To start, it’s a survival game, it’s HARD to survive in the land where dinosaurs roam the land. So if you’re not into survival game where dinosaur that eats you for daily snacks, don’t play. Try “Rust” instead =).

Now if you read through the recent reviews, there are a lot of them SALTY WHINER’s talks about the “Paid DLC”. YooHooo!!! Nobody is forcing anyone to buy it. If you’re so salty about current ARK business models then don’t buy, quit and play other game that you’re salty cry-baby whiners love. It’s not a force to buy model. It’s just merely to offer a different map with additional creatures (Lightning Wyvern, huge bloated water belly WTF flying ants, giant stomping stone golem and much more), new craftable items and of course different ways to survive than the original map.
There are 3 ways to play this game. 1) PvP official/unofficial server, 2)PvE official/unofficial server and 3) Make your own server/solo play.
1)	PvP is hard if you play it solo, so make friends and grow. Remember you’re in a PvP server so getting raid and doing raid is part of the game, don’t be salty about it. I played solo most of the time and PvP with/against big players just for the heck of it.
2)	PvE……I don’t like it…there are currently an issue where the earliest group of player in the PvE server blocking an entire area with just “pillars”. New players can’t build anywhere near and you can’t destroy that pillar. But it’s a safe place to play since you cant be raided. Some people like PvE server but not me. I like to raid and be a pain in the butt to them Soft Salties PvP Pretender. =).
3)	Your own server/solo player in your own time. You can test everything, set all the parameters of the game according to your own taste for example taming speed, hunger, resource gathering and experience gain.
Overall the game engines runs fine despite still in early access. There is no story line at all, no tutorial and No MERCY!!!
ARK is:
An open world with mainly land dinosaurs, few flying dino, some water dino, some large insects, and prehistoric mammals like giant kangaroo, bigfoot and mammoth to name a few.
All the while player will also face with hunger, thirst, and different weather system that will affect your health and in some cases will kill you if you are not ready for it.
Lots of crafting, from weapons, buildings component, refining, dino harness and etc.
Capturing or taming dino is a long process, needs preparation but worth it. In solo mode or some unofficial server one can adjust the timing speed to tame a dino. Once a player tamed any creature, they can make a harness to ride it. Riding a T-Rex is Glorious!!! ROAR!!! Some creatures don’t need a harness to ride such as the dire wolf.
There are steam worskshop that provide some of the most interesting mods out there.
Numerous Youtubers provide much information regarding the game on how it plays, and tips and tricks.
PvP is a lot of work and fun. Please don’t be SALTY if you lose, it’s just a game and when you’re in PvP server DON’T EVER TRY to give excuses that you’re not doing PvP…if you want to play PvE pls GO to PvE server. In PvP you play Hard, Die Hard, and Laugh Hard.

My world, was a dark void. I had nothing, knew nothing. I felt my will slip away, each and every day. What was life? What.. what was I here for. Questions drifted through my empty head, persisting me with answers, answers I couldn't give. It was one night I almost took my life. Pills or, or, a gun to my head. But there was a shining light in my life. Something that I'd almost overlooked ever since my world started to ruin. Something inside me made me stop. I dropped the gun, dropped the pills and ran from the kitchen. Through the living room, and past the hallway towards my room. I slowed to a stop as I reached my computer. I turned on the computer and logged on...
I opened Skype to check if my best friend had replied and said he'd talk to me again, let me have my girlfriend back, pay for my car that he broke and convince my parents to accept me again.
My eyes glanced over the page hopefuly then drifted to the bottom.
"You're a ♥♥♥♥wad who plays Warframe all day. Get a life."
I sat down on my chair and let out a sigh.
I lost my job, my friends, my girlfriend, my parents, my life...
The only thing I had left was Warframe.
Then again, Warframe made me lose my job, my friends, my girlfriend, my parents AND my life.
Eh.

I have had ark since June 2015 and I have played 1000+ hours. In this time I have seen many changes some I loved some I didn't quite like initially. When it comes to actuals gameplay I have to say I love this fantasy Dino game. Even though I would have loved to see more realistic dinos I love what they have done with their artsy subspecies. The models are great and it feels so rewarding to get through a tough big tame. I find that it is well worth the current price for the fun I have had. Just as always remember it is in early access and things change, bugs happen, and not gonna lie performance can use quite a bit of work. Of course I believe these issues will be dealt with in time so I patiently await the future updates, content, fixes and more. If you want to ride around on your own pet dinos and explore challenging caves and maps (If you can handle this games performance quirks) I'd say this one is a great one to get. I am however afraid that I can not give you much for a PVP perspective. Most of my time has been on unofficial servers with friends. If you don't have a ton of time on your hands I would not recommend trying the games base settings they are very grindy but if you are up for the challenge go for it! Hope this was helpful and should you choose to get it have fun on the Ark you spawn on. I have not gotten the Scorched Earth so I can't say what that is like. "More bosses and the end-game cycle including the Ultimate Life Form & Ascension

So they're outright saying they're being scummy and intending to create a haves and have-nots economy by making people who refuse to spend more money on an unfinished game jealous.

An above average Hidden Object Game. If you've played a lot of HOGs, you won't find anything unique about this title. The story is the usual fare. A shipwreck, find your boyfriend, oh no, there's something supernatural going on! I've played this story countless times before.
The voice acting, graphics, and visual effects are all solid, and the HO scenes were well defined. The puzzles ranged from easy to difficult. The ending was abrupt, but thankfully the bonus content fleshed that out.
The only three negatives I have for the game is that it's nothing we haven't seen before, the click detection is off in some scenes, especially the bonus content, and there's a huge amount of backtracking required. There is no map, and no fast travel, so all locations need to be travelled through. The game loves giving you objects that you need to use on the other side of the island which means clicking through scene after scene after scene to get there, only to arrive, complete the action, and then have to travel all the way back again. It was a serious time-sink and made me enjoy the game a whole lot less.
Overall, the game is a typical example of the "adventure" HOG and the annoyances aren't enough to thumb down. If you like HOGs, you'll probably enjoy this one despite all the backtracking.

A very original game ! I didn't find a style close to this Genesia Legacy.
You build your city, from nothing, in a pure natural landscape. And nature is not so friendly! You have to assign farmers, woodcutters, gather water, in order to survive, and grow.
You have also research trees to evolve, and, for example, resist to diseases, build vehicles, trade, ...
But, the game is difficult, in the sense of "punitive" : you make a strategic mistake, and your village will die from disease, or starve in winter, etc...
So, the idea is : you won't win on your first try.
Make a game, learn why you failed. Restart, and integrate you experience in your next play.
Just like an action-platform game, you can lose, but applied to a pure strategic game : this is unique at this level of "punishment".
And where the game succeeds : it is great fun. It is really great fun to fail because of a strategic mistake we missed. And try again. There is no frustration, and for me, that means it is indeed a very good game.
Completely different from Civilization, in every way (so, it is something new, and not a clone).
I HIGHLY advice this game. You won't find another one similar.

Some tips after many headaches I had! :)
1.	Each season has its own particularity. For example: Autumn is the best period to chop down a tree and Spring to turn it into planks.
2.	Make sure to plant flowers otherwise you may run out of log during winter and you population get ill and would die quickly.
3.	Never attack a wolf. It won’t attack you unless you do it. I did in my very first game then my pop got attacked and I lost less than 50 seasons.
4.	Try always to have one male and female per house, so you can keep you pop growing. Otherwise move it, as pioneer, to another house.
5.	Build ASAP a Lab so you can research interesting stuffs to progress in the game.

I'm recommending this game, but I personally am refunding it.
The game is good, it's a nice little strategy puzzle game, it's very difficult which is great.
The reason I am refunding however, is the developers really bizarre attitude that the terrible UI is a feature, not a problem. Take for example, logs - if left out, they degrade. To prevent this you have to put them in storage. However, when you click on the logs, you are presented with a choice of villagers, and only one action they can take - chopping the logs. You hit this, and they turn into a lumberjack automatically and chop the logs into planks. How do you store the logs instead? Well let me quote the advice from the moderators (and not corrected or contradicted by the dev):
Start quote:
This game is made to be HARD above all it was made in a way that you NEED to discover everything for yourself.
The game is realistic, if you're struggling with the tree wood gathering (for example), then ask yourself a simple question: How a lumberjack (is that era of time) will do if he was in that situation?
(sic)
End quote.
Yeah - the official line is that part of the difficulty of the game is learning a UI that was purposefully made to be hard.
If that sounds like mana from heaven for you, then my recommendation stands - this game is genuinely good, you will have a lot of fun.
If that is a turn off, then I drop my recommendation. Walk away, check back in 6 months to see if they have sorted it out. That's what I intend to do.

I see this game has quite a low rating and that saddens me because this game has huge potential, it looks amazing and the story-line is solid, but bugs and errors are everywhere you go, the game freezes, lags, and completely stop working, some textures go missing and the screen goes black, it sucks to see such huge potential being wasted.

+ The gameplay is.... interesting...  Very mysterious setting, and it's sort of up to you to explore and figure out what to do. You play as a Titan of Death, and you go around looking for towns to destroy collecting souls to improve your Titan's abilities. I believe you are then intended to take on various bosses.
+ Encourages exploration and discovery. (As a side I think it's interesting to note that there's no main menu or settings, you are sort of just dumped into the game at the beginning lost and confused)
+ Visually the game has a nice gloomy pixel art style with some good looking envionmens.
+ Great use of atmospheric sounds and music
- Controls are poor. The arms are controlled with the arrow keys with Q and E to grab objects. However the arms are tiny, and hard to move the way you want them to, and often get caught on things. The combat relies on you being able to swing objects as weapons but it can be very frustrating when they don't behave correctly. ( I tried using a gamepad as well, and it still did not feel right )
- The game does not exlain itself enough, and it can be hard to grasp what is happening or what you are supposed to be doing. After some time you may learn, but it can be very confusing to say the least.
- The combat system seems almost random at times. There's really no indication of how much health you or enemies have, or when you are about to die. I found myself constantly dying unexplainably in very strange ways.
Overall, I must say I did enjoy the atmosphere and mysterious vibe this game prevents. It is pretty unique, and seems to encourage the player to learn on their own.   The controls and gameplay itself is a bit of a let down though, so I'd only suggest this to those looking for a new experience.

After looking more into it the story also seemed interesting...playing as a giant destroyer of the human race and not the savior felt refreshing. When I got to the mechanics is where I was most surprised. This game, to me, is a tad reminiscent of  simulation games. By that I mean how you have to hit a series of multiple keys to get the character to do anything and when they do it comes out odd. Even though I am not a huge fan of those types of simulation games I found is a 2D puzzle platforming setting to be very interesting.
From the start I was terrible, moving in the wrong directions, moving the wrong arms, that sort of thing. And with all that it was fun...and when I started getting the hang of it the game got more fun! I also like that the game doesn't hold your hand and tell you exactly how to do everything. I got stuck on some of the puzzles...not that they were hard to figure out, just hard to perform due to the controls. Once I solved it I felt genuinely excited to move on to the next one. I look forward to playing more of this. After spending more time with it I might not feel as excited but only time will tell.

Jane and Mike are separated after their yacht shipwrecked in a storm. However, a mysterious person dragged Mike away, letting Jane alone the island to solve the mystery. However, it seems that this separation was intended so that the young woman can break a curse...
While the plot isn't really bad, I must say that I was quite getting bored in the end of the game. I mean that I was probably expecting more revelations or more mysterious happenings. However, as it's a collector's edition, you get a bonus chapter, a very much interesting one, as the main game was cut abrupty. There, you can play Mike while he's hanging on a cord and discover how he escaped and how he managed to help Jane in the end. However, it does not stop there: the bonus chapter is the epilogue of the game, on what happened after the reunion. And I was kinda asking myself if it was going towars a certain direction and it did but I was wrong on one point.
Anyway, the gameplay is pretty standard: minigames to solve, hidden objects scenes to clear and items to find in each location. However, I regret the lack of map so that I could fast travel. And while some minigames were refreshing, as not common in the genre, others were kinda boring and hard. As for the objects scenes, some of them were well hidden, or near the HUD, too much for my taste (though it happened only in the bonus chapter). I wished that there were more to do in some locations, like in the old cemetery for example.
The story happening during a storm on a island, I loved the creepy ambiance and the animations. I also loved the mysteries around all the ships that wrecked on the island and how everything is related to the mysterious signs shown in the sky. However, I perhaps wished a little more locations related to the Ancients, so that I didn't feel that it was rushed in the end.
The soundtrack is also quite adapted for the game too.
In the end, while Sea Legends: Phantasmal Light isn't the best game in casual adventures, it's not a total failure thanks to refreshing minigames and the interesting plots. However, be also warned that the game may crash: it did twice: the first time when I arrived near the boat in front of the lighthouse and a second time when browsing through the extras (screensavers). You can find better games but for the price, it's still a good purchase.

Another enjoyable Hidden Object Game that doesn't stand out from the crowd, but is still definitely a decent play.

Looking back on the game it doesn't feel like there was many puzzles, but the ones that it did have, i remember thinking a few times that they were slightly more interesting then the standard ones you find in these games. Not all of them were unique, but it was still something noteworthy in my opinion.
The story is quite decent, it's definitely something you can follow. It isn't anything life changing but it's interesting enough.
You and your partner are stranded on an island, your partner is dragged off whilst you are half conscious and your aim is to find them, find out where you are and discover the truths behind the mysterious island you have ended up on.
After you finish the game, there is an optional bonus chapter you can play through in the perspective of your partner. Which in honesty, i was quite impressed with.
The object scenes themselves are pretty straight forward. I would say the items blend very well, they're in proportion and easy (but not too easy) to find.
It felt like this game had quite a bit of back and forth, but not really in a bad way. You'll just notice early on that there are things you will need to come back to. Returning to earlier locations happens quite a bit.
All in all i think this is a decent one for the collection.
TL;DR : A decent HOG in pretty much all aspects (as far as HOGs go anyway).

"Sea Legends: Phantasmal Light Collector's Edition" is an acceptable Hidden Object Game (HOG).  The puzzles and HOGs, themselves, are decent and the story is no worse than most in the genre.  The voice-acting is few and far between, and is tolerable.  I've got some complaints about the game, but they're fairly trivial:  clicking on a few of the objects is a bit specific (I ended up getting stuck becauseI didn't click in the right place once), and the objects in the HOGs do not maintain a set scale (i.e., a small object might be huge and a big one next to it might be tiny).  That makes finding some objects a bit difficult.  But, it's a reasonable 4.5 hours of game-play (3.6 hours in the main game and 0.9 hours in the bonus chapter).  So, I'm recommending it.

Doesn't feel like it has a lot to offer in terms of replayability ... after one or two failed attempts I felt like I'd seen everything the game had to offer, and it wasn't very intriguing.
There just doesn't feel like there's a lot of depth to the game... having only one character to control instead of a whole squad makes things proceed in a fairly simple matter: walk up to dude, empty your clip, hope you don't die in the process. Repeat. Repeat. Sometimes you pick up things to help.
How you manuever your character relative to enemies has very, very little effect on gameplay... if any. If you sneak up on a character who is facing away from you and fire your gun, well ... in that same instant, the enemy manages to spin a full 180 degrees and land a bullet in your chest armor, so positioning and manuevering in this game means nothing.
Kudos for trying a simultaneous move/turn system, but the end result is that you have all the enemies moving the same speed as you, and most of them have the same range as you. The end result ends up being that once you're engaged in a fight, there is little-to-no hope of disengaging from the fight to set up a defensive position or do a tricky manuever on the enemy, or whatever ... you just both continually fire on each other, hoping that the enemy dies first.
